Ask HN: Fake abuse reports keep auto-blocking my site on Cloudflare
I run a small site on Cloudflare's Pro plan. Since 26 September, someone has filed the same fake abuse report against it six times. Each time, Cloudflare automatically puts a "Suspected Malware" warning on my homepage and login pages, and it stays until a person reviews it. The reports are word for word identical. They describe an "order" and product pages that have never existed on my site (they return 404). The file hash in the report doesn't match the hash in its own VirusTotal link, which returns "Item not found". Only the date changes, and twice it's been misspelled ("October 52026", "Octoboer 8 2026"). Cloudflare's team has cleared four of them. The reporter pastes the same text again within a day. The result is that my homepage has been blocked for most of two weeks, my traffic has halved, and Google is indexing the warning page instead of my site. I've opened support cases and requested reviews each time. I've had one reply, on 5 October, and nothing on a lasting fix. I'm not asking for special treatment. I'd like to know:
1. Is there a way to stop automatic mitigations from a reporter or text that has already been shown to be false?
2. Is there a manual-review setting for a domain?
3. Has anyone else seen the abuse form used like this, and how did it end? The same problem is described in my open case with Cloudflare (#02370521). Thanks for any pointers, and if anyone from Cloudflare's abuse team reads this, I'd welcome a reply.

source_text:
Official Docker image 2.43.3 ships @napi-rs/canvas without any native binding → "DOMMatrix is not defined" in all PDF nodes
### Bug Description

PDF parsing fails in the official Docker image `n8nio/n8n:2.43.3` with
`DOMMatrix is not defined`. Both independent PDF code paths are affected:

- `n8n-nodes-base.extractFromFile` (operation: `pdf`)
- `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.documentDefaultDataLoader` (dataType: `binary`, loader: `pdfLoader`)

Downloading the PDF (e.g. via HTTP Request node) works fine; the failure
happens only when the PDF is parsed.

**Root cause:** the image contains the JS wrapper `@napi-rs/canvas@0.1.80`,
but **no platform-specific native binding at all**. Neither
`@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl` (which this Alpine/musl x86_64 image would
need) nor any other variant is present. As a result, pdfjs-dist cannot
polyfill `DOMMatrix`, `ImageData` and `Path2D`, and PDF parsing aborts.

This is reproducible in a **pristine** image with no mounts, environment
variables or customizations.

### To Reproduce

1. Check which `@napi-rs/canvas` packages ship with the image:

```bash
   docker run --rm --entrypoint sh docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3 -c \
     'ls /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm | grep -i "napi-rs+canvas"'
```

   Output:

```
   @napi-rs+canvas@0.1.80
```

   Only the wrapper is present; no `canvas-linux-x64-musl` (nor `-gnu`).

2. Try to load the package inside the pristine image:

```bash
   docker run --rm --entrypoint sh docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3 -c \
     'd=$(find / -type d -path "*node_modules/@napi-rs/canvas" 2>/dev/null | head -1); \
      echo "Path: $d"; node -e "require(\"$d\"); console.log(\"canvas OK\")"'
```

   Output:

```
   Path: /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/@napi-rs+canvas@0.1.80/node_modules/@napi-rs/canvas
   Error: Failed to load native binding
     [cause]: [
       Error: Cannot find module './skia.linux-x64-musl.node'
       Error: Cannot find module '@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl'
     ]
```

3. In a running instance, execute any workflow that uses Extract from File
   (operation: PDF) or the Default Data Loader with a PDF binary. The node
   fails with `DOMMatrix is not defined`.

### Expected behavior

The image ships the native `@napi-rs/canvas` binding matching its own
platform (`linux-x64-musl`, and `linux-arm64-musl` for arm64 images), so
PDF extraction works out of the box.

### Debug Info

## Logs (running instance)

```
Warning: Cannot load "@napi-rs/canvas" package: "Error: Failed to load native binding".
Warning: Cannot polyfill `DOMMatrix`, rendering may be broken.
Warning: Cannot polyfill `ImageData`, rendering may be broken.
Warning: Cannot polyfill `Path2D`, rendering may be broken.
ReferenceError: DOMMatrix is not defined
```

## Environment

- n8n version: 2.43.3 (self-hosted, `N8N_RELEASE_TYPE=stable`)
- Image: `docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3`
  (digest `sha256:d4eca183959b30fb1ba5ecda7e58363c5be49a7bcf8c0227a6384a47ce2f7a65`)
- Base OS (from image): Docker Hardened Images (Alpine) 3.24
- Node.js: v26.7.0
- Architecture: x86_64
- Running via: Docker, with external task runners
  (`n8nio/runners:2.43.3`, `N8N_RUNNERS_MODE=external`)
- Database / binary data mode: not relevant (reproducible without any instance data)

## Additional context

- Earlier images did contain `skia.linux-x64-musl.node` (see #23754 for 2.0.0),
  so this appears to be a packaging regression: the optional platform
  dependencies of `@napi-rs/canvas` seem to be omitted entirely during the
  image build (e.g. via `--no-optional`, production pruning, or pnpm not
  resolving optional deps for the target platform).
- Related historical reports of the same symptom: #16593, #16438, #16422.
- Possible fix: make sure the Docker build installs the matching platform
  package, e.g. by adding `@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl` /
  `@napi-rs/canvas-linux-arm64-musl` explicitly, or by configuring pnpm
  `supportedArchitectures` with `os: ["linux"]`, `cpu: ["x64", "arm64"]`,
  `libc: ["musl"]`.
- Current workaround: extract the PDF text outside of n8n (e.g. Python/pypdf)
  and send the text to n8n via webhook.

### Operating System

Debian 13 (host); container: Alpine 3.24 (Docker Hardened Images, official n8nio/n8n image)

### n8n Version

2.43.3

### Node.js Version

26.7.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

TypeError: r.firstEvent.getTime is not a function in WorkflowStatisticsRollupService.foldBatch (Postgres) — logged ~1,400×/hour
### Bug Description

On n8n 2.30.7 (self-hosted, Docker, PostgreSQL) the container log is flooded with:

```
TypeError: r.firstEvent.getTime is not a function
    at src/services/workflow-statistics-rollup.service.ts:126:19
    at WorkflowStatisticsRollupService.foldBatch (src/services/workflow-statistics-rollup.service.ts:124:19)
    at WorkflowStatisticsRollupService.rollup (src/services/workflow-statistics-rollup.service.ts:113:18)
```

Rate: ~1,400 occurrences per hour (~34,000 per 24 h), continuously since 2026-09-29. Without log rotation a single container log grew to ~700 MB. Restarting the container does not help — the error reappears within ~3 minutes (1,340 occurrences in the first hour after a restart).

It looks like `firstEvent` comes back from PostgreSQL as a string (not a `Date`) in the rollup batch, so `.getTime()` fails. Possibly related: #28541, #28640 (same pattern with `dbTime.getTime`) and #40019 (rollup refactor).

### To Reproduce

1. Run n8n 2.30.7 in Docker with `DB_TYPE=postgresdb` (PostgreSQL 17).
2. Have ~50 published workflows with ~1,400 executions per day.
3. Watch the container log — the error is emitted continuously by the workflow statistics rollup.

### Expected behavior

Workflow statistics rollup works with PostgreSQL (timestamps parsed as `Date`) and does not flood the log.

### Debug Info

See the stack trace above.

### Operating System

Linux (Docker host)

### n8n Version

2.30.7

### Node.js Version

Bundled with the official image docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.30.7

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

source_text:
[Bounty #743] Validate /api/upload files and reject missing or dangerous uploads
## Problem

POST /api/upload accepts empty upload requests without a file attachment and returns a 201 Created status code with "no-file". Furthermore, it lacks MIME type whitelisting and file extension sanitation, allowing arbitrary executable scripts (.sh, .exe, .bat, .php) and unbounded file streams that can cause denial-of-service and remote code execution vulnerabilities.

## Requested fix

Harden the upload endpoint in uploadController and uploadRoutes:
1. Reject requests without an uploaded file with a 400 Bad Request error ("No file provided").
2. Enforce a 10MB maximum file size limit.
3. Validate MIME type and file extension against a whitelist of safe document and media types (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif, application/pdf, text/plain), blocking executable and script extensions.
4. Return standard structured response envelopes for success and 400 validation failures.
5. Add focused route integration tests for successful file upload, missing file rejection, oversized file rejection, and dangerous executable file rejection.

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

This issue is created under the Low Handing Fruit Automation bounty. I will submit a PR that references this issue and issue #743.

source_text: Corrupted decrypted content in asymmetric mode from the crypto Node when dealing with the MS Graph Subscription resource ### Bug Description MS Graph API has a Subscription endpoint to receive email messages with the content. The content is encrypted according to [this](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/changenotificationencryptedcontent?view=graph-rest-1.0) schema. General flow for decryption: 1. Decrypt the `body.dataKey` with the PEM key file (asymmetric mode). 2. Decrypt the `body.data` with the symmetric key from the step above (symmetric mode). The key is in RAW bytes format. The Decryption process is described in detail [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/change-notifications-with-resource-data?tabs=csharp#example-decrypting-resource-data). The node successfully decrypts the symmetric key; however, it tries to output the result as a [UTF-8 string](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/bb45bca5ff7ef7d2cd2b2f2e98812d96a5971b01/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Crypto/v2/CryptoV2.node.ts#L823), but the key is raw bytes, so it returns a corrupted key. The next issue is that it's not possible to use this key in the node in the second step. I have to use an n8n credentials API method to update the symmetric key (passphrase) before I can use the crypto node. I can update the node and create a PR to fix the issue and make it possible to use the raw symmetric key. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a new PEM key + cert pair (even self-signed works fine) 2. Show HN: Gauge CLI – Open-Source Hillclimbing for Agent Experience
Hi HN! We're releasing an open-source CLI for hillclimbing Agent Experience. That means optimizing your agent-facing surfaces (Skills, CLIs, SDKs, and docs) so that your users' coding agents can easily use your product. Pointing your own agent at the repo is enough to get started.  https://github.com/gauge-sh/gauge-cli  We've found that power users generally want to hand a CLI/MCP to their agents and get started from the terminal. They rarely want to log in and use the web UI themselves. We think developer tools must be agent-friendly to remain relevant. Here are some common findings that Gauge identifies: - agents get confused with CLI/SDK behavior and start source diving
- interactive commands block agents
- agents use deprecated/old CLI commands
- agents don't use Skills when you'd expect
- agents confidently assert limitations that don't exist
- inconsistent terminology confuses agents
- agents can't figure out how commands fit together into a workflow Locally, the Gauge CLI uses Docker containers to run agent harnesses (you can bring your own subscriptions). It finds where agents get confused or stuck and tests changes using your pre-release artifacts (Skills/CLI etc). We normalize events from Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode into standardized transcripts, and store them locally, alongside structured information in SQLite so that your agent can easily analyze the data. This enables automatic hillclimbing toward a great Agent Experience. We also offer hosted compute that enables more features, built on our custom Gateway (for credential brokering and transparent, per-session response rewriting). Hosted compute enables many more concurrent sessions, easier collaboration with teammates, a GitHub App for PR reviews, sessions with logged-in MCPs/APIs, and most importantly it lets you close your laptop while the sessions actually run. You don't need a Gauge account to run the full loop end-to-end though. We expect that local execution with the CLI is enough to find and fix several agent experience issues in a typical project. You'll be able to validate fixes for these issues locally, before publishing new versions (we inject pre-release Skills and code artifacts into the sessions). We would love your feedback!

source_text:
Question: would an AEAP-shaped Execution Receipt fit the approval boundary already in procure-agent?

你好 刘正享,

I came across procure-agent via GitHub search for LangGraph + human-approval workflows and read through the README carefully. The combination of a LangGraph StateGraph with explicit interrupt points, SQLite checkpointer, Decimal-deterministic money arithmetic, and the explicit "approval has checkpoint-version verification; does not execute email or procurement transactions" boundary is unusually careful work. The `BOUNDARY_TEST_RESULTS.json` file in the repo suggests you've already thought about this surface.

My team at Aiyoplane published the first public draft of **AEAP** (Aiyo Execution Authorization Protocol) earlier this month. It overlaps with your approval boundary in a specific, narrow way, so I thought I'd ask rather than guess whether it fits.

**The overlap:**

Your current approval design verifies the LangGraph checkpoint version before an approval can resume execution. AEAP goes one step further: it produces a cryptographically-signed **Execution Receipt** (Ed25519 over an RFC 8785 JCS canonicalized intent) that binds the approver's identity to the exact tool invocation and arguments at the moment of approval. If the plan state changes between approval and execution — even in ways the checkpoint version doesn't detect — the receipt no longer validates and the tool fails closed.

For procure-agent's shape, that would mean: when a human approves a specific quote (报价 A at 1195.00 CNY from a specific supplier), the receipt binds that exact quote-ID + supplier + amount. A later resumed run cannot silently execute against a different quote, even if the LangGraph state looks consistent.

We shipped `aiyoplane-langgraph` and `aiyoplane-langchain` (both Python, Apache 2.0, zero credentials to run locally). Rough shape of what it would look like on your `evaluate_plan` tool:

```python
from aiyoplane_langchain import create_aiyo_langchain, create_local_rdp, BlockedByPolicy, EscalationRequired

authz = create_aiyo_langchain(
    rdp=create_local_rdp(policy=load_policy("procure-policy.yaml")),
    tool_config={
        "evaluate_plan": {"aiyo_gated": True, "action": {"type": "procurement_commit"}},
        "finish_sourcing": {"aiyo_gated": True, "action": {"type": "procurement_commit"}},
        "search_suppliers": {"aiyo_gated": False},
        "request_quote": {"aiyo_gated": False},
        "inspect_offer": {"aiyo_gated": False},
    },
)

@authz.wrap("evaluate_plan")
def evaluate_plan(args, ctx):
    # Runs only on ALLOW. ctx.receipt binds the approver + quote + supplier.
    # ESCALATE → EscalationRequired (fits your LangGraph interrupt pattern).
    # BLOCK   → BlockedByPolicy  (fits your "报告本轮未找到可执行方案" rule).
    return commit_procurement_plan(args)
```

**Three specific questions, since you'd know best:**

1. Is the approval boundary in procure-agent intentionally scoped to checkpoint-version verification only (meaning signed receipts would be out of scope on purpose), or is it a layer you'd consider adding?
2. If it's a layer you'd consider: would the fit be at `evaluate_plan` / `finish_sourcing` (where the plan commits) or at `request_quote` (where each quote is pulled)?
3. For the real-model mode where `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is live, is the "model cannot overwrite the hard rules" invariant something you'd want cryptographically enforced, or is the tool-side forced verification already sufficient for your use case?

If AEAP doesn't fit procure-agent's shape, closing this issue is a perfectly good answer — I'd rather hear "not a fit" than have you consider something that doesn't match.

Spec: [github.com/aiyoplane/aeap](https://github.com/aiyoplane/aeap) · aiyoplane-langchain: [pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langchain](https://pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langchain/) · aiyoplane-langgraph: [pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langgraph](https://pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langgraph/) · Trust surface, including §15 non-guarantees: [aiyoplane.com/trust](https://aiyoplane.com/trust)

Thanks for the careful work on this surface. The combination of Decimal arithmetic, explicit boundary tests, and the "不执行邮件或采购交易" ("does not execute email or procurement transactions") constraint is a pattern worth more of in agent projects.

— Rashon

source_text:
Show HN: Chkit – Schema, migrations and backfills for ClickHouse (like Drizzle)
Hey HN, im Marc, co-founder of ObsessionDB.
We are open sourcing ChKit, our tooling to manage schemas, migrations and backfills for clickhouse. I am a big fan of the type safety drizzle provides for the database. Manage the schema in typescript and generate migrations from it is a powerful workflow. I always wished something like it would exist for clickhouse, so we could manage our analytical workloads the same way. It didn't exist, so we build it. We build it after running ClickHouse at petabyte scale in our previous company, were we managed hundreds of tables, MVs and endpoints reading from them. The way it works: 1. You define your schema in typescript, with typed helpers for tables, mv, column types etc..
2. You generate the migration, that contains the DDL, to get your clickhouse instance from status quo to what your current typescript schema defines
3. Your CI can check for drift
4. You run the generated migration against production
5. You use the defined types in your code, to ingest your data while making sure it has the correct type.
   Bonus: if your schema change was BC breaking, we generate the sequence on how to backfill the data, into the intermediate table to migrate (this is quite the hard problem with large tables and schema evolution) In case you have already a clickhouse instance with a schema, you can pull it down and start using ChKit from where you are. Run our generator to setup the boilerplate:     npm create chkit@latest
  
If you folks are running clickhouse in production, I am curious to hear what other challenges you are running into.

source_text:
Microsoft Teams Trigger silently stops receiving messages after ~3 days (Graph subscription is never renewed)
### Bug Description

The **Microsoft Teams Trigger** (channel messages) creates a Microsoft Graph change-notification subscription when the workflow is published/activated, but nothing ever renews it. Graph caps `channelMessage` subscriptions at 4320 minutes (3 days), so the trigger stops receiving messages roughly 3 days after each activation or n8n restart. The workflow still shows as **Active**, no execution fails and no error is raised: the trigger is simply silent. In our case it went unnoticed for 12 days (messages with photos were not processed).

What we observed (delegated OAuth credential `microsoftTeamsOAuth2Api`; first seen on 2.39.10, same node code on 2.42.6):

1. After re-publishing the workflow, `GET /v1.0/subscriptions` listed one subscription for `/teams/{teamId}/channels/{channelId}/messages` with `expirationDateTime` exactly 72 h after creation (2026-10-09T17:13:25Z -> 2026-10-12T17:13:25Z). It was unchanged 3 days later, i.e. no renewal happened.
2. Graph lifecycle notifications (`@odata.type: "#microsoft.graph.subscription"`, only the subscription id present) are delivered to the workflow as normal trigger items shortly before expiry. Nothing handles them (no PATCH, no re-authorize, no re-create); users have to filter them out manually.
3. From reading `MicrosoftTeamsTrigger.node.ts`: `checkExists()` only lists subscriptions and keeps those valid for more than 5 minutes; `create()` creates them and `delete()` removes them. We could not find renewal logic or handling of `reauthorizationRequired` / `subscriptionRemoved`.

Related (not GitHub issues): https://community.n8n.io/t/problem-teams-trigger-webhook/147354 (users report the same ~3 day expiry; workarounds: nightly PATCH or nightly unpublish/publish).

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with **Microsoft Teams Trigger** on a channel (resource: channel message) using a delegated OAuth credential.
2. Publish it and post a message in the channel: the workflow executes.
3. Wait more than 72 hours without republishing the workflow or restarting n8n.
4. Post a message in the channel: no execution is created. `GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/subscriptions` no longer lists a valid subscription for the channel.
5. Unpublish + publish again: it works for another ~3 days.

### Expected behavior

The trigger keeps working indefinitely while the workflow is active, as Microsoft requires apps to renew subscriptions before expiry (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/subscription). Either renew the subscription periodically (`PATCH /subscriptions/{id}` with a new `expirationDateTime`, which also re-authorizes it), and/or handle the lifecycle notifications Graph sends (`reauthorizationRequired` -> PATCH; `subscriptionRemoved` -> re-create) instead of passing them to the workflow as items. At the very least, failing to keep the subscription alive should be visible (workflow status, execution error or log), since today the workflow looks healthy while it receives nothing.

Workaround we use: a separate scheduled workflow (twice a day) that does `GET /v1.0/subscriptions` with the same credential, picks the subscription whose `resource` matches the channel, and `PATCH`es its `expirationDateTime` to now + 4300 min; it alerts if none exists or the PATCH fails.

SG-11 | Real Supplier portal and minimal Admin review, plus PO/ready integration
**Outcome:** operators perform everything from UI, not manual DB/Swagger/console.

**Supplier Business UI:** only (1) Requests/PO and (2) My Products & Prices. Own offers with actual purchase cost/reported quantity/unknown, upload Full/Partial and coverage, stored profile, first-time mapping approval if authorized, parsed/skip/invalid counts, before-after exceptions, apply job, row-history errors and retry; server state not decorative. Allow manual corrections/offer update. Supplier can only view own data; no customer PII/margin/other supplier costs. PO consolidates by SKU, full/partial/unavailable/price-changed, safe award/binding outcome, ready only after awarded commitment (not Hub Received); verify data propagation into sourcing and future stock signal.

**Admin minimal catalog review:** one contextual review surface for pending Candidate/Brand/Line/Ingredient/Media/Publish decisions (no full Admin dashboard expansion). Arabic RTL mobile and desktop, loading empty unauthorized stale 409 retry and file error states; accessibility.

**Acceptance:** fully logged-in supplier imports and verifies real DB changes; owner reviews and publishes candidate; browser refresh persists; wrong-supplier access 403; draft not binding; 2 browser roles and responsive smoke. Cross-link AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#2/115/124/207.

**Execution dependency:** blocked by AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#141. Complete and review previous gate before starting this stage.

### Supplier manual returns / credits — complete only the necessary operational seam

Reuse existing supplier payable / financial reconciliation contracts (see AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#17 and AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#124). Within contextual PO/Supplier and Finance actions, verify that a Hub-accepted customer return sent **physically** to the same supplier with the next purchase delivery is recorded as `SupplierReturn` pending; supplier confirmation yields a verified `SupplierCredit`; applying the credit to the next invoice is a separate, auditable action. Do NOT treat handed-off return as accepted monetary credit, double-deduct purchase COGS, or lower the new PO's genuine gross acquisition cost. Show gross new supplier invoice, credit applied, actual cash paid distinctly. Record a disputed/rejected credit and monthly cutover. If existing APIs cannot support this, report a focused contract gap and add the smallest required API/conditional UI; avoid a separate Returns portal or full accounting suite. Acceptance: supplier next bill 600 EGP minus verified old credit 100 EGP = 500 cash paid, **new goods acquisition cost remains 600**. Backlink to supplier invoice/return and monthly statement.

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

WPF XPS synthetic hyperlinks exposed through UI Automation can bypass restrictive navigation checks and reach attacker-controlled content, enabling remote code execution after user interaction.

## Discussion

Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/12021

affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. Ask HN: Are there AI models for generating sounds based on a text and reference?
I've been having a hard time finding a solution. Is there really no commercialized model that I can feed in a reference sound and text instruction and get another sound out? Right now having a multimodal inputs to image or text output is a commodotized, solved problem. IE you can put a prompt for some image and use a reference image to guide the model on what you want. After all, a picture is worth a thousand words right? Ive also used a text and audio input in order to get a text description or classification out. I cannot for the life of me find a solution for Audio + text -> Audio My usecase is that I'm trying to generate new sound effects based on a source that doesn't have that many clean examples and thought this would be just another solved workflow but I'm not finding much. Tried elevenlabs SFX but it's only text->audio and without the reference, it's hard to guide with just text and recreate a sound with any accuracy. I tried the Stable Audio 3 model which is supposed to do what I want but the results were terrible. This modality seems to be stuck where image generation was in 2016. Is there something else or is this just not a common need?

Feat: Gamification & Categorized XP System
### Summary

Expand Donetick’s existing point system to support **Gamification / XP Mode**, including custom **XP Categories** (e.g., *Health & Fitness*, *Learning*, *Chores*) and API endpoints to query user XP totals by type.

---

### 💡 Problem / Motivation

While Donetick currently supports basic points for tasks, standard points don't fully capture different domains of life or personal growth.

Categorized XP (Experience Points) turns task completion into an engaging gamified system. This helps:

* **Increase Engagement:** Gamification makes chores and habits fun for kids and adults alike.
* **Balanced Growth Tracking:** Categorizing tasks allows users to see *where* they spend their effort (e.g., mental vs. physical tasks).
* **Home Automation & Dashboarding:** API access to XP categories enables custom dashboards or smart-home rules (e.g., enabling access to rewards/devices only after earning required XP). this would closes #832 

---

###  Proposed Solution

#### 1. XP / Gamification Settings

* Add an option to toggle display terminology between **Points** and **XP**.
* Allow users/admins to define custom **XP Categories** (e.g., `Health & Fitness`, `Learning`, `Home & Household`).

#### 2. Task Configuration

* When creating/editing a task, allow choosing:
* **XP Value:** (e.g., `50 XP`)
* **XP Category:** (e.g., `Health & Fitness`)



#### 3. API & Integration Support

* Provide REST API endpoints to fetch user XP statistics:
* `GET /api/v1/users/{userID}/xp` – Returns total XP broken down by category.
* `GET /api/v1/circles/{circleID}/xp` – Returns group/circle leaderboard or category breakdown.


* *Example API Response:*
```json
{
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "total_xp": 450,
  "categories": {
    "health_and_fitness": 200,
    "learning": 150,
    "chores": 100
  }
}

```



---

### Example Use Cases

1. **Custom Dashboards:** Display a RPG-style character sheet / radar chart on a smart display or Grafana showing current levels in different life stats.
2. **Smart Home Automations (Home Assistant):** Trigger an automation via Home Assistant (e.g., unlocking a smart lock on a snack drawer or enabling screen time) only after earning a required threshold of *Health & Fitness* or *Learning* XP.

---

P.S. I’m willing to place a $100 bounty on this feature if a maintainer or contributor is open to implementing it and the PR is accepted and merged.

I mean, many companies operate within particular domains but don't have much skin in the domain itself in a way that is meaningful to other participants there -- like Oracle builds software for healthcare, ostensibly, but any actual user of their products will tell you they are nightmarish with regard to usability, and research shows that patients are often harmed as a result. In my cynical view, they are exploiting the exposure of mathematical research to automation in an effort to create a case study of their product obsoleting a highly visible and well-leveraged and relatively small profession. Regardless, I doubt even they would say they have durable skin in mathematics in any sense, certainly not in either of the senses I mentioned above. But their output inhabits the same space as mathematicians, who have to contend with the consequences

source_text:
Show HN: Lemma, an IDE for reading mathematics (macOS, open source)
I built Lemma while working through The Elements of Statistical Learning (using the Preview app). Kept running into references like "(3.41)" or "by Theorem 2.3" forcing me to scroll back through the entire book. And whenever a proof wasn’t detailed enough, I'd screenshot it, ask ChatGPT to explain, then go back to the PDF to add manual notes. Got pretty annoying. That led me to Lemma: it reads a PDF once (locally), lets you jump around between equations, theorems, etc. without constantly scrolling. I gave it a VS Code look because yes, I'm addicted to VS Code (there are other themes for normal people). A non-exhaustive list of things it can do (right now): - References to theorems, equations, figures, citations and index entries are all clickable (you can peek at them without leaving the page) - You can ask an agent or ChatGPT Web for explanations, longer proofs with one click, save the output in Lemma - When the pdf says “it is easy to show” or “proof left to the reader”, you can write the missing steps in LaTeX, and Lemma checks it on random numerical inputs and gives counterexamples if it’s wrong. You can also fold proofs to try them yourself first, and keep notes attached to specific passages (with exports to Markdown, Anki and Jupyter). Built in Swift/SwiftUI using PDFKit. The analysis runs in a helper process at low priority. No account, no telemetry, and it's GPL.
It’s for macOS 15+ only for now (unless a lot of people find it useful, then I’ll probably do it for other OSes).
It still struggles with some PDFs (scanned ones, other languages, different numbering, etc.) If you try it on whatever you're reading and encounter some problems, feel free to open an issue!

Implement Scoped, Expiring Keeper Delegations for Automated Operations
**Description:**
Introduce a delegation primitive that lets an account grant a keeper (the backend operator, a third-party automation service, or a bot) narrowly scoped, expiring authority to execute specific permissioned entrypoints without handing over full admin rights. Automation then runs with least privilege and a hard expiry.

**Problem Statement & Context:**
Several flows are designed to be executed by whoever is around: settling due escrows, executing due timelocked actions, extending TTLs. In practice the backend needs a key that can do these things, and today the only options are an over-broad admin role or manual multisig signing — both unacceptable for routine, high-frequency automation. This is also a prerequisite for unattended operation during an incident.

**Scope & Acceptance Criteria:**
- Add `delegate(grantee, scope, expires_at_ledger, max_calls)` and `revoke(grantee)`, callable by the granting account or its admin.
- `scope` is a checked bitmask of named capabilities (execute due escrow, execute timelocked action, extend TTL, trigger rate refresh), documented in the interface crate.
- Every guarded entrypoint accepts either a direct role holder or a delegate whose scope covers it and whose expiry/max-calls budget is unexpired.
- Delegates can never amplify: a delegated call that internally requires a stronger role fails instead of succeeding.
- Events on grant, use, exhaustion, expiry-triggered rejection, and revoke; view listing a grantor's active delegations.
- Out of scope: delegation of governance voting power (tracked separately) and off-chain key management.

**Implementation Guidelines:**
1. Key Files/Modules: `backstop/src/lib.rs`, `bounty/src/lib.rs`, `grants/src/lib.rs`, `treasury/src/lib.rs` for the guard, the shared interface crate for the scope enum, `tests/` for the authorization matrix.
2. Design/Architecture: a single `require_scoped_auth(scope)` helper backed by persistent delegation records keyed by `(grantor, grantee)`; decrement `max_calls` in the same invocation that performs the guarded action so a failed call does not consume budget.
3. Edge Cases/Constraints: expiry at the exact ledger boundary, revocation during an in-flight execution, scope combinations that are individually harmless but jointly dangerous, and keeping the guard cheap enough not to blow the instruction budget on hot paths.
4. Testing: a full scope x entrypoint matrix, expiry boundary tests, max-calls exhaustion, revocation, and explicit negative tests proving no path escalates to admin.

**Complexity:** Medium (130 points)

Show HN: Frink – Desktop-first app for multi-step workflows and parallel agents
What’s up HN?! I'm Benji, and I’ve been building Frink since ~April this year. Frink is a desktop-first, open-source (MIT) app for running coding agents in parallel and multi-step workflows that start on their own. It runs on your machine (macOS and Linux) with your own provider login. It currently supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and OpenCode, but the latter 3 are in preview. No Frink account to use the app. The biggest USP of Frink is workflows: think n8n for agents. You describe a routine in a sentence, for example: "every weekday at 9am, run the tests; if any fail, have an agent fix them, then wait for my approval before it opens a PR." Then, Frink builds it as a workflow (or simply, Flow): a list of steps you can read and change before it runs. A Flow can start on a schedule, from any webhook, or from an event from a third-party such as Linear, Shortcut, ClickUp, Sentry, PostHog, etc. Steps can be agent turns, shell commands, conditions, approval steps that stop and wait for you, or steps you write yourself in code (or ask the agent to write one). Everything that needs you (an approval, an agent's question, a finished task to review) lands in one Work Queue. Other stuff: * Up to four agents side by side, each on its own git worktree if you want. Or, many agents out of direct view. * Every change shows as a diff; there's a code editor, a terminal, etc. * Local-first: chats, Flows and tasks live in SQLite on your machine. * Easier provider parity: currently working on and improving the tooling setup between providers. Once inside Frink, irrespective of what provider you use, the hooks, MCPs, and other tooling work out of the box between providers. Why I built it: I started building it when there weren’t many other competitors; now the industry is swamped with ADEs and harnesses. However, in my opinion, each still lacks good automation for more fine-tuned scenarios. I doubled down on the flows to help me with my actual day-to-day job as a SWE, and over time it’s helped me automate most of the PRs being shipped across my personal projects, team, etc., to the point that it’s a continuous loop and helps a whole ton. Notes: Windows isn't supported yet. Flows only run on Claude Code and Codex for now. It's a solo project, so expect sharp edges.

spec automation/service_ledger v3: one door settle_service for the money path (receipt, gate, books, delivery)
Owner's principle of 2026-10-23, in two halves: every service this project sells
emits a receipt, one splitter reads it, and the distribution is decided by rules
alone -- and all the accounting is settled without any person taking part.

This issue closes the money path on paper: service_ledger v1..v3 (four services,
one receipt gate, books derived from entries, and `settle_service` as the single
door), token-wallet v2 (the three-unit trade) and payout's `trade_split_fits`.

## Boundary

- specs/automation/service_ledger.t27
- specs/automation/token-wallet.t27
- specs/verified/payout.t27
- .trinity/seals/automation_automation::service_ledger.json
- .trinity/seals/automation_automation::token_wallet.json
- .trinity/seals/verified_VerifiedPayout.json
- docs/now/

## Goal

One spec-owned door (`settle_service`) that settles any of the four services in a
fixed order -- books-STOP, receipt gate, payout eligibility, books arithmetic,
delivery -- answering SETTLE_STOP / SETTLE_NONE / SETTLE_HOLD / SETTLE_PAY.

## Why this matters

Until v3 the rules lived in separate functions, so a host could call them in the
wrong order (pay before the gate, accrue before eligibility). One door makes the
order impossible to bypass, and HOLD separates "earned but not payable today"
from "not earned".

## Source of truth

- specs/automation/service_ledger.t27 (new)
- specs/automation/token-wallet.t27
- specs/verified/payout.t27

## Deliverable

- specs/automation/service_ledger.t27 v3: `settle_service`, `SETTLE_*` verdicts,
  books (`BOOK_STOP`), accrual only on `payout()==PAY_NORMAL`, flags
  (COMPLETION_HOST_EXISTS=false, BOOKS_HOST_EXISTS=false, TRI_PAYABLE=false).
- specs/automation/token-wallet.t27 v2: TRADE_UNITS 3, SHARE_HOUSE/BOUNTY/REFERRAL,
  trade_charged/trade_share/trade_split_fits.
- specs/verified/payout.t27: `trade_split_fits` refusal (subtract-not-add).
- Seals for all three specs regenerated.

## User Scenarios

Given a course completion receipt that passed the gate and books that read clean,
when `settle_service` runs with TRI_PAYABLE=false, then the verdict is SETTLE_HOLD
-- the accrual stands, nothing leaves.

Given unreadable books, when `settle_service` runs for any service, then the
verdict is SETTLE_STOP before any gate or payout check is consulted.

Given a receipt that payout() refuses (unverified or unreferenced), when
`settle_service` runs, then the verdict is SETTLE_NONE and no book entry exists.

## Requirements

- FR-001: `settle_service` MUST run the chain in the fixed order books-STOP,
  receipt gate, payout eligibility, books arithmetic, delivery, and no caller
  path may reorder it.
- FR-002: an accrual entry MUST exist only where `payout(...)` answers PAY_NORMAL;
  a slash or any refusal MUST accrue nothing.
- FR-003: an unreadable or inconsistent book MUST stop the run (BOOK_STOP /
  SETTLE_STOP) and MUST NOT read as "nothing was owed".
- FR-004: HOLD MUST be reachable only when the books already say PAY; a zero
  balance with a non-payable unit MUST be NONE, never HOLD.
- FR-005: the spec MUST NOT price, promise or mint $TRI; TRI_PAYABLE stays false
  until trust model, settlement path and mainnet are all live.

## Success Criteria

- `./target-bench/release/t27c test-report specs/automation/service_ledger.t27`
  exits 0 with 24 tests and 2 invariants proved, vacuous 0.
- `./target-bench/release/t27c seal --verify` exits 0 for all three specs.
- `t27c validate-seals --pr-files specs/automation/service_ledger.t27,specs/automation/token-wallet.t27,specs/verified/payout.t27` exits 0.

## How to verify

```bash
./target-bench/release/t27c test-report specs/automation/service_ledger.t27
./target-bench/release/t27c seal --verify specs/automation/service_ledger.t27
./target-bench/release/t27c seal --verify specs/automation/token-wallet.t27
./target-bench/release/t27c seal --verify specs/verified/payout.t27
```

## Risks

DESIGN, no host yet: COMPLETION_HOST_EXISTS=false, BOOKS_HOST_EXISTS=false,
LIVE=false, TRI_PAYABLE=false. Must not be sold as live until a host splits a
real charge and a real completion runs through these functions.

- Owner decisions 2026-10-23 (trace in service_ledger.t27 header)
- Host: gHashTag/999-multibots-telegraf (billing-shared.ts, token-ledger.ts)
- Network law: gHashTag/trinity-fpga specs/trinet/settlement_law.t27

source_text:
AI/semis morning brief, Oct 23: 92 updates, 24 high [part 1/2]
# China's optics makers say AI orders are booked into 2028

**The bottom line:** China's optical-module chain sent one message in a flood of filings. Orders are full, the 1.6T (1.6 terabit-per-second) generation is ramping, and big overseas customers are now giving demand guidance for 2028. Memory is the other pressure point: AI datacenters are absorbing DRAM supply, and phone buyers are paying for it. Beijing's chip ambitions also got fresh fuel from Cambricon's results, DeepSeek's reported record fundraise and a new five-year informatisation plan.

## Optical modules: full order books and longer visibility

Innolight (300308.SZ / 3308.HK), the world's largest maker of the optical transceivers that link AI servers, said orders from its main overseas customers run through 2027. Some key accounts have given 2028 demand guidance ([HKEX](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/1023/2026102300380.pdf)). First-half revenue was CNY 41.78bn, up 182.5%, and net profit was CNY 13.65bn, up 241.7%. The company described pricing as "healthy" and competition as "orderly." It plans to cancel 5.65mn repurchased shares rather than use them for staff incentives ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300308/AN202610231830833072.html)). Next-generation formats, NPO (near-packaged optics) and XPO, will "gradually release."

Its closest rival, Eoptolink (300502.SZ), said 1.6T modules have entered a sustained ramp with shipments accelerating ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300502/AN202610231830831587.html)). It also approved a RMB 800mn–1bn buyback ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300502/AN202610231830831590.html)). Accelink (002281.SZ) reported "ample" orders and no adverse change in trends ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/002281/AN202610231830830889.html)).

The read-through runs upstream to the component makers:

- **Sourcetech (688498.SH)**, which makes the laser chips inside transceivers, guided Q3 revenue up 265–293% and net profit up 579–660%. A second fab phase should add capacity around the turn of the year ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688498/AN202610231830832769.html)).
- **Lianxun Instruments (688808.SH)** tests 800G and 1.6T modules. It forecast Q3 profit up roughly 1,900–2,100% and says it is global number two in 1.6T core test gear ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688808/AN202610231830834114.html)).
- **TFC Optical (300394.SZ)**, a component supplier, reported H1 net profit of RMB 1.2bn on RMB 2.83bn revenue and said its co-packaged optics (CPO) parts are in stable mass production. Its new incentive plan targets net profit up 700% by 2029 versus 2025 ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300394/AN202610231830833517.html)).

Capital is following. Unlisted Nazhen Technology says its 2027 indium phosphide laser-chip capacity, more than 100mn units, is already covered by orders ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513186?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Shijia Photonics (688313.SH) is seeking up to RMB 2.8bn for chip and interconnect capacity, and itself flags the risk of a shift to silicon photonics and CPO ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688313/AN202610231830848648.html)). Langte Intelligent (300916.SZ), a newcomer to optics, is paying ¥663mn for 51% of a passive-optics maker ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513851?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

The 2028 guidance supports the view that hyperscaler capex runs well beyond 2026. The risk is the classic one: a wave of new capacity arriving in 2027 just as CPO starts displacing pluggable modules. Watch whether leaders' "orderly pricing" survives that supply.

## Memory squeeze reaches consumers

A Caixin investigation shows the AI memory crunch now hitting phone shelves ([Caixin Global](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-10-23/in-depth-chinas-smartphones-get-pricier-as-ai-strains-chip-supply-102496477.html)). Price increases before China's National Day included:

- Xiaomi's 18 Pro, up 1,000 yuan
- Huawei's Mate 90, up nearly 28%
- the 2TB iPhone 18 Pro Max, up 3,500 yuan

TrendForce data cited in the piece show server DRAM contract prices rose about 64% in H2 2025, with a roughly 270% cumulative increase projected for 2026. Qualcomm's China chairman said he had never seen memory prices rise 4–5x in a year and expects high prices to persist through 2027. Memory made up nearly 60% of the bill of materials for sub-$400 phones in Q1. Demand is cracking: China shipments fell 4.3% in Q2, the fifth straight quarterly decline.

The article frames this as good for memory makers and bad for low-end handset brands, with scale players best placed. Supplier filings back it up. Baiwei Storage (688525.SH), a Shenzhen memory-module maker, said DRAM and NAND prices rose "significantly" in 2026 and proposed another buyback ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688525/AN202610231830847055.html)). Giantec (688123.SH), which makes the SPD chips on DDR5 modules, grew Q3 revenue 26% as SOCAMM2/LPCAMM2 modules launched. Its chips for CXL memory modules, which let servers pool memory, are now in customer validation ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688123/AN202610231830847992.html)).

China's DRAM champion CXMT voiced "firm confidence" in long-term demand ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906520425.html)). Caixin profiled Micron (MU) CEO Sanjay Mehrotra's push into high-bandwidth memory, the stacked DRAM used beside AI accelerators ([Caixin](https://database.caixin.com/2026-10-23/102496333.html)).

## China's AI chips, models and five-year plan

Cambricon (688256.SH), China's best-known listed AI-accelerator designer, more than doubled Q3 revenue to 3.53bn yuan (+104%). Net profit was 1.40bn yuan (+148%) ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688256/AN202610231830847887.html)). Rival GPU maker MetaX (688802.SH) set incentive targets of 60bn yuan revenue in 2027 and 300bn yuan cumulative over 2027–29 ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688802/AN202610231830849193.html)). These are internal hurdles, not guidance, but they show how much domestic substitution management expects.

DeepSeek reportedly closed a round of about 100bn yuan (~$15bn), a Chinese AI record. CATL and Tencent led, with chip-linked funds also participating ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwfmnk5005978.d.html)). The headline of that report says 10bn, so treat the exact size as unconfirmed.

DeepSeek also open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference framework it uses to serve its own models. DeepInfer runs on both Nvidia GPUs and Huawei's Ascend 950 ([Caixin](https://www.caixin.com/2026-10-23/102496505.html)). That matters for Huawei's ecosystem: software that runs on either chip lowers the cost of switching away from Nvidia. Huawei separately raised a CNY 15bn offshore syndicated loan, its first in six years ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniweywq5020293.d.html)).

Policy points the same way. The 2026–2030 Informatisation Plan calls for:

- more advanced-node manufacturing capacity
- high-performance AI chips
- 3D integration and photonics-electronics convergence
- humanoid robots and quantum computing

([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwffek8270214.d.html), [CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513725?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Shanghai targets 85% AI penetration in industry by 2028, with subsidies of up to 30% on rented compute ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906136377.html)). These are demand-side tailwinds for domestic chips and cloud.

## Datacenter boards and power

High-end circuit boards remain a bottleneck. Shengyi Electronics (688183.SH) guided nine-month profit up 68–75%. It cited growing orders for AI-server and 800G/1.6T switch boards and a "breakthrough" in 1.6T optical-module boards ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688183/AN202610231830847403.html)). Victory Giant (300476.SZ), a key Nvidia board supplier, said some customers have released demand through 2027–28 ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniweqhs8199552.d.html)).

Power is next. Megmeet (002851.SZ) showed a liquid-cooled 800V DC power platform with Nvidia at OCP, built into Nvidia's MGX server ecosystem. It also debuted a solid-state transformer module ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906214393.html)). Battery maker XiongTao (002733.SZ) wants to move RMB 336mn from a stalled lithium-battery plant into a RMB 1.5bn AI-datacenter power-supply project. Shareholders vote on 11 November ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/002733/AN202610231830848099.html)). Datacenter operator Runze (300442.SZ) is taking RMB 4bn from a China Eximbank unit for an AI infrastructure project ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwffen5024680.d.html)), a sign of state-linked money backing compute buildouts.

## Materials and equipment

China Northern Rare Earth (600111.SH), the world's largest light rare-earth producer, grew Q3 net profit 161% on higher prices and volumes ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniweywn8173442.d.html)). That is consistent with tight magnet supply. In the US, the Department of Energy designated helium, essential for chip fabs, as a critical mineral ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwfruh5124819.d.html)).

Japan's September chip-equipment orders rose 48.2% year on year ([Wallstreetcn](https://wallstreetcn.com/livenews/3184259)). That is a supportive data point for toolmakers such as Tokyo Electron (8035.T). Quartz Pure Materials (603688.SH), which makes high-purity quartz for fabs, credited semiconductor sales for a 46% Q3 profit gain ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906242523.html)).

## What to watch

- **Optics pricing into 2027:** watch Innolight's and Eoptolink's full Q3 reports for gross margins, and whether new laser-chip capacity from Sourcetech, Nazhen and Shijia tightens or loosens component supply.
- **DeepSeek round:** confirmation of the final size, and whether DeepInfer drives measurable Ascend adoption.
- **Memory contract prices:** whether Q4 DRAM quotes keep rising and how far handset demand weakens.
- **Shareholder votes:** XiongTao on 11 November and MetaX on 9 November.
- **Follow-on measures:** detailed rules under the five-year informatisation plan, especially any advanced-node manufacturing support.

source_text:
SFTP upload sub-workflow stays running for days after parent timeout (n8n 2.42.7, Windows OpenSSH)
### Bug Description

We observe intermittent hangs in the built-in FTP node using SFTP to a Windows OpenSSH server. On three consecutive scheduled runs (October 17-19, 2026), the parent execution was canceled after approximately one hour, while its integrated child execution remained marked as running. The oldest child was still running after approximately 49 hours. The three children were subsequently canceled manually. A manual recovery run completed successfully.

Saved execution data consistently shows the first source download completed, followed by the destination SFTP upload node in nodeExecutionStack, with no completed run recorded for that upload node or any downstream CSV parsing/SQL nodes. This identifies the execution boundary, but does not establish whether upload, cleanup, or another internal step was pending.

Windows OpenSSH logs in the corresponding windows show successful authentication followed by a client-requested disconnect within approximately 0.3-0.45 seconds. These logs do not establish file-transfer completion. Other disconnects near ECONNRESET messages used different client ports and process IDs; we are not attributing those resets to the affected upload without further evidence.


### To Reproduce

Production topology (intermittent; no deterministic end-to-end reproducer yet):
1. A scheduled parent synchronously invokes a child workflow.
2. The child loops over files with batch size 1, downloads a file from a source SFTP server, and uploads it to a separate Windows OpenSSH server using the built-in FTP node in SFTP mode.
3. After upload, the child parses the CSV, imports data, archives the source file and continues the loop.
4. On affected runs, execution remains at the first destination-upload boundary. Successful runs of the same workflow finish normally.

Additional code-level evidence
In the installed Ftp.node.js, execute() awaits sftp.put(), then awaits sftp.end() before returning. Its outer catch also awaits sftp.end() before rethrowing the original error.

In the installed ssh2-sftp-client 12.1.0, end() waits for close when this.sftp is present, without its own deadline. Its temporary error listener ignores ECONNRESET during end().

A local event-based simulation using the extracted end/errorListener methods confirms that, IF ECONNRESET is delivered during end() and no subsequent close is delivered, the promise remains pending. Delivering close later resolves it. Pending cleanup also delays propagation of an earlier error. This simulation does not use a real SSH connection, does not reproduce the complete ssh2 event lifecycle, and does not prove that close was missing in the production incident.


### Expected behavior

The upload node should complete or fail with an actionable error instead of remaining running indefinitely. Cleanup should not indefinitely delay the original error. Please also clarify whether parent timeout/cancellation is expected to propagate to an integrated child; the observed behavior allowed child executions to accumulate across scheduled runs.


### Debug Info

Verified diagnostics below; this is not the full UI-generated debug-information export.
- n8n: 2.42.7 (self-hosted Docker; upgraded from 2.30.5 before these three incidents)
- n8n-nodes-base: 2.42.5
- Node.js in the deployed image: 26.7.0
- ssh2-sftp-client: 12.1.0
- ssh2: 1.16.0
- Database: SQLite
- Docker host OS: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS; Linux amd64 container
- Destination SFTP server: Windows Server 2025 / OpenSSH
- EXECUTIONS_MODE: unset (default mode)
- EXECUTIONS_TIMEOUT=3600
- EXECUTIONS_TIMEOUT_MAX=7200
- EXECUTIONS_DATA_SAVE_ON_PROGRESS=true

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Docker host; Linux amd64 container)

### n8n Version

2.42.7

### Node.js Version

26.7.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

Enhancement: Shared branded PDF template designer — logos, contracts, invoices, letters, plans, schedules and bookings
## Objective
Create one shared **Branded Documents & PDF Template Designer** module for all Sportarena / Gotmygame users. Coaches, referees, event organisers, physios, doctors, supply-chain sourcers/suppliers, sponsors and venue owners/managers can design their own contract, invoice and letter formats, upload logos and produce professional PDFs directly from their existing workflows. Extend to other authorised platform roles through a common capability rather than building separate designers.

Training/coaching plans, rehabilitation plans, event schedules, bookings and other operational outputs should carry the user's or organisation's approved brand. Branding must enhance presentation while preserving canonical business data, privacy and document integrity.

## Existing platform and backlog integration
Repository review in the preceding infrastructure assessment confirms Node.js/PostgreSQL, Expo React Native/react-native-web, the cap(...) REST/OpenAPI/MCP registry, durable jobs, encrypted sensitive data and existing local file routes. Indexed code search for PDF returned no matches; this is **not proof that no renderer/export already exists**. Before implementation inventory current invoice, contract, plan, schedule, booking, media and export code, screens and tests. Record existing behaviour → gap → smallest compatible enhancement.

Dependencies/boundaries:
- #247 owns scalable infrastructure, shared object storage, worker deployment and monitoring; consume those primitives while retaining local-development/legacy compatibility.
- #243 owns cross-module transactional email. This module supplies authorised PDF references/attachments to that service; it does not build a competing sender.
- #210 and #212 own physio/doctor practice, plans, billing and clinical controls.
- #145 owns sponsorship agreements; #231 owns legal matters/contracts.
- Canonical invoices/payments/quotes, bookings, appointments, teams/events, training/coaching plans, provider records and user/organisation identities remain authoritative. Rendering does not create a second finance, booking, clinical, contract or calendar system.
- Reinspect latest main before coding. A missing upstream structured plan/contract workflow must be tracked as a dependency; do not invent source data or silently implement an unrelated domain module here.

## 1. Roles and document catalogue
| Role/workspace | Initial template families and source integrations |
|---|---|
| Coach | Coaching agreement, quote/invoice/receipt, assessment summary, training/coaching plan, session schedule, progress letter |
| Referee/official | Appointment/engagement letter, assignment schedule, service quote/invoice, match report using permitted canonical results |
| Event organiser | Event programme/timetable, fixture schedule, booking confirmation, participation letter, supplier/sponsor agreement, invoice |
| Physio | Service agreement, invoice/receipt, authorised rehabilitation/exercise plan and progress summary |
| Doctor | Consultation summary, approved care plan, referral/clearance letter and service invoice; clinical authorisation/sign-off applies |
| Supply-chain sourcer/supplier | RFQ, quotation, sourcing/service agreement, purchase-order presentation, delivery note and invoice from supported canonical records |
| Sponsor | Sponsorship agreement, commitment/payment schedule, endorsement brief and authorised performance report |
| Venue owner/manager | Booking confirmation, hire agreement, invoice/receipt, facility timetable and event-use letter |
| Other authorised users | General business letter and supported personal/organisation document families |

A displayed template family must state whether its source workflow is available. Unsupported purchase orders, regulated certificates or legal-signature workflows must not be presented as completed integrations. Templates provide document structure; they do not guarantee legally valid agreements, tax compliance or medical authority.

## 2. Brand kits and uploaded assets
- Personal and organisation brand kits: primary/secondary logo, optional approved co-brand logos, colour palette, fonts, business/trading name, legal entity/contact/address, registration/tax identifiers where applicable, website, header/footer and optional stamp.
- Support multiple brands/branches per user where authorised; select the acting legal entity explicitly. Organisation membership alone cannot authorise changing its branding.
- Upload PNG/JPEG/WebP with transparent PNG supported; crop/fit, aspect-ratio lock, resolution warnings and reusable alignment/size presets. Validate actual bytes, size/dimensions, decompression limits and malware/quarantine policy; strip unnecessary metadata. Reject unsafe SVG/HTML by default unless a separately reviewed sanitisation pipeline exists.
- Private assets and scoped access by default; separate approved public brand assets from confidential signatures/stamps. Explicit permission to use sponsor/partner logos; no automatic brand endorsement.
- No broken/distorted logos, watermark covering body text or low-resolution silent stretching.
- Preserve an immutable asset/version reference in issued documents so changing a logo later does not rewrite history.
- Uploaded signature image is a visual mark, not proof of signer identity or a cryptographic signature. Restrict its use separately from ordinary logos.

## 3. Designer experience
Create **Documents & Templates** in common navigation and contextual actions in each source module: Preview document, Generate PDF, Download, Save to my documents and Share.

Responsive light-theme UI with:
1. Choose document family and starter template.
2. Choose personal/organisation brand kit and legal entity.
3. Edit layout/content with sample data.
4. Validate and preview using the actual PDF renderer.
5. Save draft, publish version and set permitted defaults.
6. Generate from a selected source record.

Use a practical block-based editor with drag/reorder and keyboard-accessible alternatives; a full unrestricted page-publishing tool is not required. Desktop/tablet supports page canvas plus properties; phone uses block/property editing and full-page preview without requiring precise dragging.

Supported blocks:
- Header/logo/business details, recipient/address, title/reference/date.
- Structured rich text, headings, bullets, terms/clauses and sign-off.
- Line-item and pricing/tax tables; totals and payment instructions.
- Training/coaching/rehab activity tables, goals/instructions and permitted exercise images.
- Event fixtures/timetables, sessions, venue/resource bookings.
- Page numbers, footer, confidentiality label, document status/watermark.
- Optional signature/acknowledgement placeholders and verification QR/reference where supported.

Controls: A4 and Letter, portrait/landscape, margins, spacing, alignment, sensible typography, repeating table headers, page/section breaks, header/footer on every page and keep-heading-with-content behaviour. A3 programme layouts are optional later. Warn on overflow, missing assets, unsupported fonts and low contrast. Display loading/empty/error/retry/conflict/permission states.

Offer polished starter designs: classic letterhead, modern invoice, professional agreement, weekly training plan, rehab/care summary, event timetable and booking confirmation. Provide a sample-data preview clearly labelled SAMPLE, not a fabricated real record.

## 4. Controlled data binding
- Versioned typed field catalogue per document family, with friendly labels and sample values. Examples: organisation.display_name, invoice.number, invoice.lines, invoice.tax_total, booking.start_at, plan.activities and event.fixtures.
- Allow only approved schema bindings and bounded conditional/repeating blocks. No arbitrary SQL, JavaScript, filesystem reads, remote fetches or executable HTML from templates.
- Server resolves source IDs, actor/entity, permissions, locale/timezone and permitted field projection. User-supplied field values cannot override invoice totals, confirmed booking dates, official results or clinical decisions.
- Required/optional/unknown distinctions; warn or block generation when required data is missing. Never silently turn missing values into zero, paid, signed, approved or medically cleared.
- Distinguish editable narrative/terms from read-only canonical values. Preview unresolved placeholders and validate before publication.
- All invoice arithmetic/currency/tax/discounts/credit adjustments and document numbers come from canonical finance services. The designer may choose placement/format, not recalculate authoritative money using client formulas.
- Templates cannot hide mandatory document fields/disclosures applicable to a configured family/entity. Maintain an explicit reviewed schema/policy, not a claim of universal jurisdiction compliance.
- Human-reviewed contract clauses and clinical text remain distinguishable from template/sample content. General templates cannot grant authority to issue prescriptions, medical certificates or legal advice.

## 5. Template ownership, sharing and lifecycle
- Scopes: private personal, organisation, and platform-curated starter. Sharing a template shares layout/approved assets, not patient/client/financial source data.
- Roles: owner, designer/editor, publisher/approver and document generator; implement smallest compatible permissions using existing organisation/delegation controls.
- Draft → published → retired with immutable published versions; duplicate/fork, rename, archive, restore and version history. Optimistic locking for concurrent editing.
- Defaults per user/organisation/document family/branch/locale with deterministic precedence; show which template/version will be used. No silent template changes after generation.
- Co-branded layouts require explicit authorised selection; a venue manager cannot use an unrelated sponsor's private kit.
- Team member departure/revocation removes future editing/generation access without deleting retained business documents. Define ownership transfer and orphaned-organisation handling.
- External sharing is document-specific, independent of template sharing. Public template marketplace is a later explicit feature; do not expose user templates by default.

## 6. PDF generation and source workflow behaviour
- Choose a maintained server-side renderer through an ADR comparing fidelity, table pagination, fonts/languages, security/isolation, licensing and resource cost. Prefer a constrained document schema compiled to controlled HTML/CSS or PDF primitives.
- Deterministic rendering from template version, brand-asset versions, approved source snapshot and render options. Embed supported fonts, selectable/searchable text, correct glyphs and locale-sensitive dates/amounts; preserve currency code and timezone clarity. Include Tamil and English test fixtures and evaluate RTL requirements explicitly.
- Use existing durable jobs for large/multi-page/bulk renders. Small renders may use a bounded synchronous path. Per-user/org quotas, job CPU/RAM/time/page/image limits, cancellation, retries/deduplication and cleanup prevent one user exhausting the platform.
- Preview and final PDF use the same engine. Contract/training-plan edits show accurate pagination before issue.
- Distinguish draft preview, generated export and formally issued/signed document. DRAFT/SAMPLE labels must remain visible where applicable.
- Store immutable issued PDF plus document metadata, template/asset versions, source references/snapshot, checksum, actor, generation/issue timestamps and relevant approval history. Protect sensitive snapshots with canonical encryption/retention controls.
- Regeneration creates a new version; changing template/source/logo does not alter an issued PDF. Existing issued invoices cannot be silently renumbered or edited; use canonical credit/replacement procedures.
- Define stale-source detection between preview and issue, and contract/clinical approval requirements. Patient-specific plan PDFs require live access plus publication/sign-off under the owning domain's rules.
- Generation does not confirm bookings, sign contracts, mark invoices paid, publish care plans or send emails. Each domain transition remains explicit.
- Batch output allows authorised selected records only, with individual status/errors, bounded size and expiring archive download. Never allow bulk rendering to bypass per-record permissions.

## 7. Secure storage, download and delivery
- Reuse canonical private-file storage and #247 S3 adapter. Every preview/download/regeneration/export rechecks permissions, organisation ownership and applicable patient/client consent/history scope. Deny insecure direct object reference access.
- Clinical/legal/staff/financial documents never become public due to a reusable template or branded logo. Apply data classification, region and retention policy to source snapshots, PDFs, temporary render files and backups.
- Run renderer with restricted filesystem/network, no arbitrary remote URLs, no internal metadata-service access, no template scripts and no untrusted executable content. Bound image decoding and PDF size.
- Short-lived authorised download URLs with clear expiry/revocation limits. For sensitive shared links requiring immediate revocation, enforce a gateway/access check rather than claiming an already-issued S3 URL can be revoked instantly.
- Share to named recipients/portal access using explicit scope/expiry; email delivery uses #243 preferences and secure links by default for sensitive content. Attachment mode requires appropriate document policy and limits; sending does not guarantee receipt or revoke downloaded copies.
- Audit template publication, brand changes, generation, issue, access/export/share/revocation; redact contents from logs, job payload visibility, analytics and notification previews.
- A QR/verification link exposes only deliberately approved authenticity metadata. Do not encode private medical data, bearer tokens or public-access secrets in QR codes.
- Digital signatures/e-sign provider integration are optional later adapters. Preserve legally significant signatures/bytes; do not confuse an uploaded signature image with validated signing.

## 8. Data/API contract and compatibility
Propose additive entities only where absent: brand kits/assets/versions, templates/versions, scoped permissions/defaults, generated documents/versions, render jobs and access/share records. Reuse existing jobs, file metadata, audits and canonical domain IDs.

Implement capabilities through existing cap(...) registry with Zod validation and REST/OpenAPI/MCP parity: manage brand kit, create/clone/edit/publish/retire template, list family fields, preview, generate, inspect job/status, list/download/share authorised documents. Binary transfer routes must enforce the same policy and be explicitly documented.

Use transactions, idempotency keys, uniqueness, deterministic pagination, indexes and optimistic locking. No unsanitised template evaluation, unrestricted model-generated HTML or client-provided private object paths. Existing templates/exports, invoice APIs, local development and legacy deployment must keep working behind compatible adapters/feature flags.

## 9. Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each listed role can select its authorised brand and generate at least one relevant document from existing canonical data; unavailable source workflows are explicitly identified.
- [ ] User can upload a logo, reuse it across invoice/contract/letter/plan/schedule/booking templates and preview accurate placement without distortion.
- [ ] Personal and organisation kit/template permissions prevent unrelated users or members without delegation from modifying or using private assets.
- [ ] Published template versions and issued document bytes remain unchanged after template/logo/source changes; replacements preserve history.
- [ ] Invoices preserve canonical identifiers, line items, currency, totals/tax and payment state; designer cannot forge financial values or remove required fields.
- [ ] Coach training plans and event schedules support multi-page tables, repeating headers and clear dates/timezones; physio/doctor outputs respect clinical approval and access scope.
- [ ] Cross-user/org, revoked-consent, youth/guardian, expired-share and direct object/download access scenarios are denied correctly.
- [ ] Preview-to-issue rejects or explicitly reconciles stale source/template versions; no race creates two issued financial document numbers.
- [ ] Renderer rejects executable templates, external/internal URL fetches and oversized/decompression payloads; resource/time limits and cleanup work.
- [ ] Duplicate/retried render jobs do not create duplicate issued documents or emails; worker failures recover with useful status.
- [ ] Visual QA covers A4/Letter, portrait/landscape, long names/addresses, many invoice lines, long clauses, absent optional fields, large logos, page breaks and Tamil/English fonts; no clipping/overlap/missing glyphs.
- [ ] PDFs have selectable text and sensible reading order; accessibility capabilities/limitations are documented without claiming PDF/UA certification unless tested.
- [ ] Phone/tablet/desktop editor and source-module journeys support keyboard/screen readers, clear errors and accessible previews.
- [ ] Secure delivery integrates with #243; no automatic email or contract/booking/clinical transition occurs from merely generating a PDF.
- [ ] Existing finance/booking/provider/source-module regressions, PostgreSQL permission/concurrency tests, API/MCP parity and Expo web build pass.

## Delivery phases
1. Inventory, document schema/renderer ADR, brand kits and curated starter templates.
2. Designer, preview, versioning and shared render/storage/job APIs.
3. Invoice/letter/booking/training/event integrations; role-specific contract/clinical/sourcing adapters as canonical sources permit.
4. Secure sharing/email integration, batch generation, visual/performance/security verification and operational runbooks.
5. Optional governed template import/export, e-sign adapters and curated sharing extensions.

## Definition of done
Deliver usable designer and contextual generation journeys, source-to-field/permission matrix, documented schemas/APIs, additive migrations and rollback, starter-template examples, realistic multipage PDF fixtures with rendered visual QA, meaningful security/concurrency/integration tests, renderer capacity/cost and retention/incident runbooks. Document supported languages and domain dependencies. Do not merge or deploy automatically.

I don't know whether you can really call it winning. Who is actually benefiting from the win here? Another small example: something you see now at res
I don't know whether you can really call it winning. Who is actually benefiting from the win here? Another small example: something you see now at restaurants are these QR codes being put on the tables, to remove the need for a waiter to come by and ask, or for you to get up and order, but by automating that away you also remove that little bit of social interaction for both the people ordering and the waiters. There are many other little examples like this, where beneficial side-effects go lost from automation. I suppose LLMs serve as a prime example of how this can affect people quite negatively (e.g. skill atrophy), if not careful. I think adaptation only goes so far, and we are being arrogant in thinking that we can adapt to everything, because a large part of how we function as humans is not as adaptable as we think, e.g. our emotional and instinctual needs, or how we maintain skills that are essential in the long-term. It also has been an incredibly short period with incredibly large changes, to be able to say that things will just adapt; perhaps they will, but at what cost, and who wins from it?

source_text:
Show HN: Singularity – memory that makes coding agents cheaper on repeat work
Coding agents start every session from zero. Ask Claude Code for a change like one it made last week and it reads the same files again, falls into the same test traps again, and you pay for all of it again. Singularity learns from your finished sessions (change committed, tests passing): where each kind of change goes in this repo, how it gets checked, and the mistakes made along the way. When the next task starts, a hook hands the agent the workflows that fit, pointed at the code as it is today. Picking them is plain text matching with no model call. It stores where to edit, never the code itself. Results, medians of 3–4 runs per side, hidden tests decide pass/fail, every run passed. On excalidraw: - A long task with four changes, all of kinds memory had learned: 1.9M → 423k tokens, $0.81 → $0.30, 28.5 → 9.5 turns. - The same kind of task, but two of the four changes were bugs it had never seen: 39% fewer tokens, 38% lower cost. The unseen bugs cost the same with or without memory. - Where it doesn't help: small tasks in validator.js and one-off bug fixes. The difference there is about zero, within noise. Each measurement was written down before it was run. The plans and results are in the repo. Caveats: 3–4 runs per side, mostly one repo. Only Claude Code sessions are learned from; Codex, Gemini CLI and Droid get the hand-over through their hooks. Learning uses your Claude account (about $0.25 a round, capped at $1 a day, and only if you opt in). Everything is stored locally in ~/.singularity. Install (Windows PowerShell and more options in the README):     curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pandacover/singularity/main/install.sh | sh
  
I'd love to hear where it breaks on your repos, and what memory should carry for one-off work like bug fixes.
