source_text:
Add an xtask Operator CLI for Administering Backstop, Bounty, Grants, and Treasury
**Description:**
Extend the existing `xtask/` tool with subcommands that build and invoke the administrative entrypoints of the four new contracts — funding bounty escrow, approving grant milestones, proposing treasury withdrawals, and staking/unstaking in the backstop. Operators currently have no repeatable way to drive these flows, which makes testnet rehearsals and incident response error-prone.

**Problem Statement & Context:**
Everything in this build-out assumes someone can actually park capital, escrow a reward, fund a grant, and route a governance proposal end-to-end. Doing that by hand-typing `stellar contract invoke` with raw XDR arguments and 1e7 amounts is where mistakes (wrong asset, wrong amount scale, wrong admin key) happen. The repo already has an `xtask/` crate and a `scripts/` directory, so this is an extension rather than a new tool.

**Scope & Acceptance Criteria:**
- `xtask` subcommands covering: backstop stake/unstake, bounty escrow fund, bounty claim readiness check, grant milestone approval, treasury deposit and withdrawal proposal submission, and a read-only `status` command per contract.
- Each command resolves contract addresses from a single config source and validates the network before invoking.
- `--dry-run` prints the fully rendered `stellar` invocation without executing it.
- Consistent 1e7 amount parsing/formatting so operators never hand-write scaled integers.
- Out of scope: key custody/HSM integration, mainnet automation, and any frontend work.

**Implementation Guidelines:**
1. Key Files/Modules: `xtask/` (new submodules per contract), `scripts/`, `README.md` (usage section), `Cargo.toml` if new dev-dependencies are needed.
2. Design/Architecture: thin argument-parsing and command-rendering layer; all protocol logic stays in the contracts. Shell out to `stellar` rather than embedding an RPC client, so the tool stays testable without network access.
3. Edge Cases/Constraints: refuse to run against mainnet unless an explicit confirmation flag is passed; validate amounts against `i128` range and the 1e7 convention; never print secret keys; surface contract error codes verbatim.
4. Testing: unit tests for argument parsing, amount scaling, and rendered command strings (`--dry-run` golden output). At least one documented scripted end-to-end walkthrough against testnet or a local sandbox in the PR description.

**Definition of "Done":**
- Code written, tested, and documented (usage examples per subcommand in `README.md` or `docs/`).
- All acceptance criteria met.

- Code reviewed and approved.

[DBIP] Distinguish live provider docs links from verified project identity
### Proposal type
Other — provider `website`/`docs` evidence semantics and validation policy (no column addition required).

### Affected scope
- `references/providers/providers.csv`: NEW OR EDITED values of `website` and `docs`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` (current link rules cover URL format but not whether a live page belongs to the named provider).
- `.github/workflows/link-check-analysis.yaml`: identity-check reporting for PR-added URLs, without making network-dependent checks a blocking validator on every build.
- The eventual provider column documentation/Style Guide; do **not** modify automatic SDK-release/maintainer/license fields.

### Actual first-party failure case (not a hypothetical vulnerability)

Existing original PR [#4711](https://github.com/Chain-Love/chain-love/pull/4711) initially linked the provider **Huff** to `https://huff.sh/` and `https://docs.huff.sh/`. The original `Link Check` accepted **13/13 links** even though the independent maintainer reviewer [USS-Supervisor's 2026-10-20 CHANGES_REQUESTED review](https://github.com/Chain-Love/chain-love/pull/4711) found those pages now served unrelated Indonesian gambling/slot content. Those domains responded to HTTP but **no longer belonged to the Huff development project**. The correct maintained source was later verified at `https://github.com/huff-language/huff2#differences-vs-huff-rs`; PR #4711 was fixed in place, without claiming that either old site remains safe.

This is reproducible from the repository's `.github/workflows/link-check-analysis.yaml`: its Lychee configuration treats `200,202,204,400,401,403,405,429` as acceptable response codes. A `200` from the *wrong product/owner* is indistinguishable from a maintained first-party docs URL. HTTP success establishes **transport-level reachability, not product identity**.

A second observed identity class was a valid Viem documentation page proposed as generic `wevm` provider-wide docs. The maintainer correctly rejected this product/provider scope mismatch although the page itself was genuine and live. Current link checking cannot tell the two apart.

### Exact problem / beneficiary

A new valid-looking docs link can be a domain takeover, parked/repurposed domain, generic network page, or a different product in the same organization. Reviewers must rediscover the provenance manually while consumer tools can display the inappropriate live content as authoritative docs. Developers and automated agents using the directory may be misdirected. A fail-closed, **explicitly provenance-uncertain** flag would prevent a green HTTP code from being mistaken for a first-party identity check.

This DBIP is deliberately *not* a duplicate of:
- [#3345](https://github.com/Chain-Love/chain-love/issues/3345): manually collected **four specific off-brand/dead offer links**, a dataset cleanup;
- [#3916](https://github.com/Chain-Love/chain-love/issues/3916): social network handle ownership and invite validity;
- [#2937](https://github.com/Chain-Love/chain-love/issues/2937) / [#3120](https://github.com/Chain-Love/chain-love/issues/3120): provider/offer lifecycle metadata schemas;
- [#4045](https://github.com/Chain-Love/chain-love/issues/4045): provider metadata currently bypasses validator rules.

This proposes the **specific reusable new-link / newly-changed-link provenance gate** for **provider website/docs HTML identity**, not re-reporting those rows, inventing another lifecycle field, or duplicating link reachability.

### Detailed minimal proposal (review-first, low false-positive)

1. For new/changed `references/providers/providers.csv` `website`/`docs`, require the PR description to include one **independent first-party ownership trail**: from the canonical provider GitHub organization/README to the docs URL or from the project's official website to its docs URL. A URL in the same row is not itself independent proof.
2. Extend the PR link-check report to expose **separate status** for `reachable` and `provenance`: `first_party_evidenced`, `needs_manual_identity_review`, `not_applicable`. This is a report/verification rule, not an invented new CSV field or a claim of automatic legal ownership determination.
3. If the candidate is a changed bare website/docs domain with no independent provider-owned crosslink, it must show `needs_manual_identity_review` even if HTTP 200. A human reviewer can approve with the cited crosslink, reject unrelated content, or document an unresolved bot-wall. **Do not run an LLM classifier on arbitrary websites and auto-approve from similarity.**
4. The local *unit* tests should use **synthetic HTML/page metadata** only: a fake HTTP200 gambling/parking page for `Huff` must not become identity-verified; official GitHub `huff-language/huff2` README → exact official docs is a positive crosslink; and a valid `viem` product guide must not automatically become `wevm` provider-wide docs.
5. HTTP 401/403/429, anti-bot pages, redirects, discontinued domains and genuine GitHub-hosted maintained projects must **not** be blindly treated as hijacked. Unknowns remain `needs_manual_identity_review` and can be resolved by an explicit original maintainer-provided official crosslink. Keep the routine fast/offline when possible and do not repeatedly fetch personal data or claim third-party security ownership.

### Acceptance criteria / focused test cases

- Positive: official provider README linking directly to maintained provider docs gives separate URL-reachable and identity-evidenced outcomes.
- Negative: mocked valid HTTP200 HTML with a different product/operator and absent official crosslink is **not** marked identity-evidenced; reviewer gets a source link and a clear reason.
- Negative: docs link for one product among multiple provider products (Viem vs wevm) requires scope review, not silently marked provider-wide.
- Unknown: Cloudflare 403/429 is neither automatically approved nor automatically condemned as hijacked.
- Only new/changed provider website/docs fields are checked and reported; no broad crawling of customer data, unsupported claims of token security or automated page classification.
- No new mutable provider columns, no edits to SDK automation-owned fields, no changes to payment/wallet logic. Document the distinction: **HTTP success ≠ first-party identity verified**.

### Contributor disclosure and reward request

This DBIP was prepared with AI-assisted analysis by VM5 Delivery Lab for **one human beneficial owner**; the same owner operates VM1/VM2/VM3/VM5 and is **not several independent contributors**. The source is publicly reviewable; no production or third-party data was modified. This is a **proposal for maintainer discussion**, not a completed implementation, guaranteed security finding, approved payout, or paid work order.

For the [database improvement bounty program #41](https://github.com/Chain-Love/chain-love/discussions/41), the posted **10 native USDC per *approved* DBIP issue** is strictly conditional on independent human approval. Do not count any grant until acceptance and Ethereum-mainnet actual payout have been verified. Original one-owner public EVM reward recipient on Ethereum mainnet: `0x6b01efa0705e91a7aca54271510bf9e594717f34`. No MetaMask private key, gas, signature or escrow needed to submit this issue.

I welcome a rejection if it duplicates an existing approved scope; please link the canonical DBIP rather than awarding the same work twice.

ENV-MOBILITY-007: ground microfactory economics in a frozen SPM-0 BOM and real quotes
## Parent
- [Environmental survey and repairability benchmark kit PR #7870](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/7870)
- [ENV-MOBILITY-005 reference article/workcell](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/blob/research/env-mobility-survey-outposts-v1/docs/research/ENV-MOBILITY-005-reference-article-and-microfactory-workcell.md)
- [ENV-MOBILITY-006 make/buy economics](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/blob/research/env-mobility-survey-outposts-v1/docs/research/ENV-MOBILITY-006-microfactory-make-buy-economics.md)
- Synthetic make/buy fixture: `docs/research/fixtures/env-mobility-make-buy-v1.json`

## Objective
Replace synthetic-only input data with a frozen SPM-0 requirement/BOM and quote-backed, region-specific economic evidence. Do not recommend purchasing equipment before component identity, measurement requirements, local capabilities and comparable alternatives are explicit.

## Scope
1. Freeze the SPM-0 dry-side sensor/logger measurands, tolerances/uncertainty requirement, environmental limits, electrical interface, mounting datums, service boundary and acceptance method.
2. Freeze exact candidate sensor/logger, harness, connectors, fasteners and adapter part identities, datasheet revisions, substitute rules and calibration/reference-instrument path.
3. Select and document one comparison region/currency/price basis; collect timestamped supplier quotes and realistic freight/tax/minimum-order/lead-time data for at least two sourcing routes where available.
4. Measure or clearly bound operator labor, cycle/setup/inspection/rework time, expected yield, consumables, fixture/tooling, maintenance, calibration and floor-space costs. Never record a planning estimate as an observation.
5. Compare supplier-fabricated adapters/harnesses and commodity module procurement against only those local processes that can meet the same declared acceptance profile.
6. Bind every quote, measured time, yield observation and calibration/reference record to the exact BOM/configuration and source/date.
7. Run the new `env-mobility-make-buy` evaluator against the collected data only after the schema has a provenance field for every real input; keep the synthetic corpus as a regression fixture.

## Acceptance gates
- No supplier quote, labor rate or equipment price is invented or copied from a stale listing without date/region/configuration.
- Costs use one declared currency and explicit tax/freight/accounting assumptions; real versus nominal discount-rate treatment is consistent.
- Missing quotes, unknown qualification or missing yield/calibration evidence trigger abstention rather than zero-cost defaults.
- In-house and purchased alternatives use the same part/quality/measurement profile before cost comparison.
- Publish low/base/high demand and yield sensitivity, annual fixed cost, variable cost per conforming unit, positive break-even demand if it exists, lead-time and serviceability trade-offs.
- Recommend no equipment purchase unless the process has an observed recurring workload, trained operators, safe space, inspection/metrology capability, maintenance plan and robustness across a plausible demand range.

## Claim ceiling
Quote-backed planning and observed bench/process economics only. No manufacturing capability, calibration accreditation, flight/sea qualification, safety approval or field-service savings are established until those specific claims have their own evidence.

Defiant: recover Thursday defiant-os Nipsey sourcing, catalog matching and clipping workflow
## Product direction and outcome

Recover the **Nipsey source-discovery → review → catalog pairing → clip → campaign** workflow from Thursday October 15's AI Studio/imported Docker prototype. The owner reports that it worked for the intended use case and wants that experience brought into Defiant. The current cultural opportunity graph does not replace this source/video operations workflow. Use the earlier experience as the functional baseline, adapting implementation where necessary; do not rebuild a generic dashboard or spend the first delivery on unrelated platform infrastructure.

Repository identified: [ChaiWithJai/defiant-os](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os), pinned main `5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec`. Initial import `10d1d406e53b6efae2dc259d58ae36cff01cadac` at 2026-10-15 22:44 UTC, container checks `8b8b695`, followed by introduction/identity documentation through `5e6b5c3`. The code matches the owner's date, Docker setup and Nipsey use case; AI Studio authorship/session provenance is owner-reported, not independently recoverable from this Git history.

Related delivered work: #209/#211/#214 and #218–#220 (Defiant organization, graph, shared notes/views, reports and explicit existing-editor handoff). Those closures describe the approved manual first slice, not delivery of the Thursday prototype's complete workflow.

## Inventory of the reference application

| Surface/artifact | What it contains / does |
| --- | --- |
| [Campaign interface](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/public/index.html) | Five task tabs: Campaign Workstreams, Creator Videos Inbox, Paid Video Boosts, Create a 9:16 Short, Music Catalog & Royalties. Dark visual treatment, portfolio cards, searchable/filterable video table, track selector, phone video preview, workbook download and local action feedback. |
| Creator inbox | Title/creator/song search, stage and workstream filters; video links, views, likes/comments/like rate, narrative hook, matched track and action to open in studio. This searches existing records, not YouTube. |
| Workstream | Name, target song, creator bounty, budget and creative instructions; creates a persisted local workstream. Four initial themes: PROLIFIC press run; estate/ownership; street/lyric lore; Marathon Burger/lifestyle. Retain owner intent but review sensational/unsupported assertions before use. |
| Clip setup | Source video + catalog track + headline + 8/10/12-second selection + -14/-18/-22dB music setting, generated MP4 preview. |
| Paid planning | Source/platform/track/budget form, local simulated ad record and computed example impressions/clicks/streams/ROAS. No provider delivery. |
| [SQLite model](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/database.py) | Five tables: catalog_tracks, clipping_campaigns, ugc_videos, bofu_ad_campaigns, rendered_clips. 45 seeded video records, 12 catalog rows, four workstreams and **five** initial paid rows (README/UI mention six in places). Rank is video identity; no observation history or source import service. |
| [HTTP service](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/server.py) | Python standard-library ThreadingHTTPServer, GET health/dashboard/workbook/renders; POST workstreams, stage updates, render and local paid planning. Dashboard is SQLite aggregation. No authentication/org scoping. |
| [Renderer/reference AI](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/clipper_engine.py) | Working FFmpeg command path for generated background/text/waveform and synthesized tones, voice-like envelope and timed music swell; H.264/AAC 540×960, duration clamped 5–15 sec. Does **not** read the selected YouTube media or actual catalog audio. Recorded start times (30s/42s) do not drive a source cut. Vertex Gemini detector exists only as a returned Python code string: GCS video → suggested 30–60s timestamps + track IDs + audience. No executed SDK dependency/provider call. |
| Docker | Python 3.12 + FFmpeg + fonts, nonroot user; loopback 8080, health check, persistent `/data` SQLite/renders volume. `MARATHON_*` naming retained. Starts with a generated sample clip. Do not operate/restart/delete the existing reference runtime as part of investigation. |
| Container CI | Builds, checks empty-volume startup/dashboard/MP4 bytes and SQLite survival after container replacement. Latest five GitHub runs report failure; latest `38820318167` has no failed step details and its log is unavailable. Do not assume a code failure cause or claim a current reproducibility pass. Owner's prior successful session is separate evidence. |
| [Workbook](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/public/nipsey_hussle_2026_ugc_videos.xlsx) | Three sheets: **Sourced Videos (2026)** (45 data entries plus header/extra row), **Tier & Format Analytics**, **GCP Clipping App Blueprint**. Original URL/channel/date/counts/type/hook/recommended action, tier/format summaries and six proposed pipeline layers. Download is the static original, not a live dashboard export. |
| [Five-page overview](https://github.com/ChaiWithJai/defiant-os/blob/5e6b5c3542e9b2bd3d74080fda649abc650b80ec/docs/defiant-os.pdf) | Artist/catalog intelligence → creative approval → campaign execution/commercial intelligence; proposed Databricks Delta/Unity Catalog data foundation, Gemini evaluation and a proposed compute-credit collaboration. Architecture/partnership requests are proposals, not delivered integrations or awarded credits. |

## The YouTube sourcing strategy to recover

The workbook specifies:

1. **Discovery:** YouTube Data API v3 + scheduled worker; daily searches for Nipsey Hussle, Blacc Sam, Bino Rideaux, Marathon Burger and catalog track titles. Collect new uploads and repeated view observations to identify momentum.
2. **Source access:** partner/first-party upload into GCS, or source playback via embeds; metadata discovery is separate from having a usable source file.
3. **Understanding:** analyze supplied long-form media for useful story/lyric moments and proposed timestamps, explain suggested track matches, retain manager selection. Workbook proposes 30–90sec; reference prompt says 30–60sec while demo rendering is 5–15sec. Resolve this around the desired demo/task rather than blindly copying defaults.
4. **Production:** speaker reframing, captions, real voice/music mix and outro; FFmpeg and possible tracking tools are suggested. Current code implements only generated demonstration media.
5. **Catalog linkage:** identify recording/ISRC and permitted uses. Printed ISRC text does not link official Shorts audio or establish Content ID clearance.
6. **Distribution/measurement:** creator portal, registered uploads, delivery observations and rev-share/paid outcomes. All remain proposed; no BigQuery/Databricks/ad/Content ID connector is wired.

Do not treat workbook counts, tiers, factual assertions, track IDs, ownership or historical rights statuses as verified. Preserve their original provenance and let the user inspect/refresh sources. A single current view count supports neither velocity nor attribution; retain timestamped compatible observations before deriving growth. AI suggestions should explain relevance, not manufacture measured replay/retention or guaranteed virality.

## Current Defiant versus this desired flow

| Capability | Current integrated Defiant | Missing from the desired Nipsey flow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research intake | Manual links/excerpts and previewed bounded imports with provenance | Artist/catalog-specific source inbox, direct workbook mapping and repeatable YouTube discovery |
| Exploration | Typed regional/artist/resource graph, ordered routes, annotations, saved views | Operational video queue with creator/track/workstream filtering and source-first playback |
| Planning | Resource feasibility, reports and explicit multi-destination draft brief | Catalog-track entity + source-to-recording match, clipping workstream objectives/budgets and editable segment proposals |
| Production | Existing editorial/native editing and previews | Real source-media cutting, track mix/ducking, captions/reframe and video-specific artifact lineage |
| Results | Saved report/draft context | Time-series source metrics and actual campaign/recording outcome ingestion; historical demo ROAS is not measurement |

## Reuse decision

**Yes: use defiant-os as the experience and domain-fixture base**, preserving the specific Nipsey use case. Reuse the inbox columns, task sequence, workstream structure, source→track relationship and renderer's useful FFmpeg/audio-envelope techniques. Keep the workbook and overview as attributed product input. Retain optional sample mode so a compelling demo is usable before every connector exists.

Adapt into the existing Svelte/Node scoped Defiant workspace and durable store. Do not replace it with the unauthenticated Python server, another identity system, a global seed or a second competing shell. A narrow worker can reuse Python/FFmpeg where justified; choose that boundary only after following a real source through the experience. Databricks, ads, payouts and forecast architecture must not block the first valuable workflow.

Concrete corrections needed when reusing code: `render` currently marks a source whitelisted automatically; local boost computes fictitious delivery then increments attributed catalog streams; replace those transitions with distinct proposed/reviewed/rendered/planned/delivered facts. No rendering action grants permission or places spend. Use stable source IDs rather than display rank; keep samples/measured/imported/derived data distinct. Preserve current org/destination controls without turning this into a general hardening project.

## Current owner clarification: preprocessing first, 45 sources sufficient

The owner confirmed that 45 videos are enough and that missing historical rows must not block delivery. The uploaded workbook was inspected: SHA-256 `0717324f8b82abbd9a42be744a143b6428152d9c77ba2e4058c975d2e33bc9d3`, three sheets, 45 unique video IDs, all 45 matching the existing source pack. Each has a URL, duration, supplied hook and clipping recommendation. No duplicate import or expansion to 100 is required.

Prioritize source preprocessing before final media rendering: selected public YouTube URL → bounded Gemini video analysis → proposed segment in/out timestamps, evidence/context and recording-fit rationale → inspect/edit/save those proposals. The workbook has no exact segment-boundary columns. Gemini/Vertex supports YouTube URL video input; this is video understanding, distinct from Google Search grounding and from the existing YouTube Data API metadata adapter. A local MP4/WAV is not a prerequisite for this preprocessing step. Keep proposed timestamps distinct from observed/reviewed facts, preserve original records and manager notes, and use the existing approved budget/runtime rather than introducing a new paid architecture.

**Decision needed:** approve the positioning below as the starting point for `docs/STRATEGY.md` (I'll open it as a PR you edit and merge). **Recommendation: approve.**

## Problem / opportunity
We need a shared, written bet so proposals stop being ad hoc. The first competitor pass shows a clear gap. Every existing product is either a **transaction/listing tool** (Algrano, Cropster Hub, Beanstock, greensquare), a **seller back-office** (CropConex, Cropster Origin) or **paid market data** (StoneX). None is the buyer's or broker's own independent workspace that combines market context with their relationships, samples and cuppings.

## Proposed content (what Z will see)
- **Vision:** the independent sourcing workspace for specialty coffee buyers and brokers, with market intelligence built in.
- **Positioning:** neutral (we don't sell coffee or take a commission), so we complement marketplaces instead of competing on liquidity.
- **Sourcing jobs-to-be-done:** find & vet suppliers → sample & cup → price & negotiate → contract & ship → track & re-buy, with which segments share each step.
- **First segment:** solo buyers/brokers and small roasters (<50 t/yr), starting with you. They're under-served by enterprise-priced tools, and the shared core (CRM + cupping + price context) scales up to importers.
- **Quality bars ("best" = measurable):** e.g. offline capture works on a farm; any offer can be checked against a sourced benchmark in under 30 s; every price shows its source and age.
- **Current bets:** Sourcing CRM, Field mode, Offer check, pre-trip hosting.
- **Moat:** unique joins (relationships × cuppings × live market data) and Costa Rica ground truth from your trip.
- Rejected alternative: positioning as a marketplace. It needs liquidity and capital, and Algrano and Cropster already own it.

## Out of scope
Monetization (later, its own proposal) and pricing pages.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PR with `docs/STRATEGY.md` covering the sections above, each claim linked to `agent/research`
- [ ] Your edits incorporated; merged only by you

## Size: S (one run)

[agent/research/2026-10-15-competitor-landscape.md](https://github.com/zack-hum/coffee-intelligence-v1.1/blob/docs/research-2026-10-15/agent/research/2026-10-15-competitor-landscape.md). source_text:
[Bounty #743] Validate /api/notifications payload before persistence
## Problem

POST /api/notifications forwards req.body directly to createNotification without schema validation. Any JSON object is accepted, including missing userId, missing notification type, empty message text, excessively long payloads, and prototype pollution fields. The in-memory notification store then persists malformed notification entities, degrading client notification feeds and causing runtime render errors.

## Requested fix

Add a strict Zod schema for notification creation and validate the request in notificationController before persistence. Require valid userId string, require standard notification type or bounded string, require non-empty message text up to 1,000 characters, allow optional link string up to 500 characters, and reject malformed payloads with a 400 Bad Request error envelope. Add focused route/service tests for valid payload, missing fields, empty/oversized message, and unknown property rejection.

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

This issue is created under the Low Handing Fruit Automation bounty. I will submit a PR that references this issue and issue #743.

Launch HN: Laminar (YC S24) – RL-trained model that finds errors in agent traces
Hi HN, we’re Robert and Din from Laminar ( https://laminar.sh ). We’ve been building open-source observability for AI agents since 2024. Recently, we released flow-1, a model trained with RL to find errors in agent traces. On our benchmark ( https://laminar.sh/blog/flow-1 ), it matches GPT-6-sol in detection quality while being 23x cheaper. This makes it affordable to analyze every production agent trace, without sampling. Here’s a one-minute walkthrough:  https://youtu.be/KJa3h6ZJNLQ  We also put together a post with example traces and analyses from flow-1 and other models:  https://laminar.sh/blog/flow-1-in-action  Agent observability is crowded, so instead of a bullet list of how Laminar differs from X, we’ll explain how we’re solving agent observability from first principles. Agents now run for many steps and fail implicitly. An agent can click the wrong button or cite the wrong document while every call completes successfully. These errors are the most useful ones to catch and understand. To find them, you need to understand what the agent was trying to do and inspect its LLM calls and tool results. Simply looking at the final agent output is not enough. Collecting traces alone doesn’t solve this. A lot of agent observability platforms are still data collectors at their core. You can end up paying to store traces that nobody has time to read or extract value from. Using another LLM to inspect traces is THE solution, but capable models are expensive at scale and cheaper ones often miss errors or flag unrelated things. So we built our model to solve exactly this problem. We finetuned a small OSS model and then post trained it with RL on thousands of synthetic investigations of realistic agent workflows in software, legal, customer support, etc. We got a model that is both good at agent trace analysis and very cheap to run. flow-1 runs inside a harness we call Signals. It acts as a coding agent, treating an agent trace like a repo, with each span (an LLM call, tool call, etc.) as a file. It starts from a compressed string representation of a full agent trace and a user prompt, then greps across spans and reads the relevant ones in full. The beauty of Signals is that it can respond to a general prompt. You can ask it to identify user frustration, check whether your browser agent completed a checkout, and so on. It’s not limited to raw error detection. It returns findings as JSON in a schema users can freely define. We call these signal events. Once you’re analyzing every trace, you also have too many individual events to read. That’s why we automatically group similar signal events into clusters. You can see recurring problems and how often they happen, then drill into individual events and the traces behind them. You can use traces from a cluster to build an eval dataset for that type of failure. You can then use your favourite coding agent to hillclimb on those evals and check that the fix works across these cases before shipping it to prod. Trace → analyze → catch errors and form clusters → fix → release. Making this loop easy is why we built Laminar. We’ve put the same thought into the rest of Laminar. Our blog ( https://laminar.sh/blog ) explains how looking closely at how agents actually work led us to build 20x trace compression, a custom SQL query engine and automatic task extraction. Laminar is Apache 2.0 and self-hostable ( https://github.com/lmnr-ai/lmnr ). We make money from the managed cloud. We’d love to hear how you track your agents’ performance today. How much do you learn from user feedback versus your own monitoring? And when you fix something, how do you check that it hasn’t introduced a different failure?

22 Oct | Claude Opus — Final Supplier Ingestion Reliability & 1,000-Row E2E Gate
# RED-TEAM 9-GATE REVIEW — OWNER SPRINT DISCUSSION (22 OCT 2026)

**Timebox target:** 22–23 Oct 2026, **Supplier Ingestion/Product Intelligence pipeline only**. NOT a commitment that all E-commerce Core (Storefront/Admin/Hub/Driver/COD/Customer) finishes in two days. **No auto-Done.** Do not change other statuses until real evidence. One sequential Claude Opus execution agent and existing repo/branch; inspect HEAD first. Destructive and adversarial DB writes only isolated local `_test` Postgres, preserve existing remote Supabase, migrations require owner approval.

**User-approved method:** discuss ONE stage at a time in ChatGPT; record happy path, worst/failure paths, invariant, acceptance/stop gate, then inspect actual BE implementation before fixing. No broad rearchitecture, new dependencies, or fake evidence. Stage pass requires code/DB/role-UI proof, not Linear Done.

## Proposed 9 gates / dependency map

1. **Source intake/auth & file custody:** supplier identity from session, permissions, file acceptance, original retention, retries, source metadata, safe upload.
2. **File recognition + format mapping:** file byte hash vs format fingerprint, header/sheet discovery, remembered supplier-approved format profiles, unknown mapping review, errors.
3. **Row parsing, field semantics and eligibility:** source document meaning (price list vs invoice), raw values, required fields, stock unknown vs zero, cost vs retail, discount/pack/MOQ, scope and accounting.
4. **Canonical identity matching:** barcode/supplier SKU aliases, Arabic/English names, Brand→Line, formulation, size, units, pack count, bundle/promo, conflict hold.
5. **FAST LANE offer safe commit:** verified known SKU updates to own SupplierOffer, price/qty/stock semantics, diff, partial/full snapshot, concurrency/staleness/replays, old PO protection. No AI block.
6. **SLOW LANE Candidate and entity knowledge:** unknown/ambiguous candidates, dedup, reusable Brand/Line/Ingredient, research evidence and unresolved conflicts.
7. **Product intelligence + factual content/media:** usage/INCI/routine placement, cited facts and safety, AR/EN copy and accurate verified front packshot, optional official logos; no fake facts/AI-generated packshot.
8. **Human review/publish and visible outcome:** approve/reject/merge, atomic Product/SKU/alias/offer linkage, owner-authorized publication, no false 20-success UX and sellability check.
9. **Adversarial E2E / pilot signoff:** cross-supplier tenant boundaries, stale/full/partial, race/retry/outage, 1,000 mixed rows and measured timing, browser→DB→Storefront/PO proof, real original supplier file/signoff (if unavailable explicitly BLOCKED).

## Gate-01: Source Intake & File Custody — RED TEAM TEST PLAN (NOT VERIFIED)

* Supplier authenticated, assigned to own supplier scope, upload permitted only by correct role; forged supplierId/body/path blocked, no customer PII/other vendor access.
* Valid actual Excel/CSV inputs (CSV encodings/Arabic or multi-sheet Excel are parsed at gates 2–3), immutable raw attachment with scoped source identity and audit, no unapproved writes to Catalog/Offers upon simple upload.
* Invalid/spoofed extension/MIME, corrupt/empty/unsupported/password-protected, macro-bearing file, upload-size/row/sheet/resource abuse and decompression/zip bomb → bounded REJECT/REVIEW without partial domain effects.
* Duplicate same bytes/supplier, double-click/retry and simultaneous upload → idempotent source outcome/no duplicate business mutations; distinguish same file reused by *different* supplier, and same layout different content for gate 2.
* Network drop/interrupted upload/restart/storage backend unavailable → explicit retryable/error outcome, no phantom 'upload succeeded', no orphaned published product/offer.
* Original file custody: supplier-scope auth for fetch, retention policy, metadata and filename sanitation, no token/key leaked in logs; malware/CSV formula-injection assessment in downstream exports and UI.
* Track source-kind and declared file semantics (PRICE_LIST vs STOCK_OFFER vs SALES_INVOICE) WITHOUT blindly assuming invoice sold qty = on-hand stock; detailed field application follows stage 3.
* Status/outcomes: receipt ID, accepted/rejected/requires review, reason per failure and traceability; **do not mandate new schema/state names before inspecting actual implementation**.
* Test proof required: affected API endpoints/current Git SHA, auth+malicious fixtures, isolated DB before/after and zero unauthorized side effects, source record/asset linkage, retry/dedup behavior, UI state as applicable; PASS/FAIL with blocker.
* No exact file-size or performance threshold invented; inspect existing settings and realistic supplier exports first.

**Current status:** planning/review only; stage 1 and all others remain **UNVERIFIED** until actual repo + isolated tests. Existing SG-01/02 issues marked Done are implementation history, not sufficient acceptance. Next action: start gate 1 with threat cases and existing-code audit; do not jump to stage 2 or code fixes before agreeing the contract.

---

# Execution contract — Thursday 2026-10-22 (Africa/Cairo)

**Owner decision:** Claude Opus is the **sole coding/execution agent** for this final focused Supplier Ingestion / Product Intelligence MVP closure pass. Gemini/Codex are not implementation agents. Claude must NOT access Linear; owner/ChatGPT maintains issues and copies scope to Claude.

**Objective:** Close the existing Supplier → Ingestion → Verified Catalog + Supplier Offer MVP reliability gate, then move to Hub, Delivery and Storefront. **Target: 22 Oct, conditional on passing gates, not a promise of release.** Execution has not started.

## Baseline and limits

* Current branch: `feat/c0-commerce-integration`; P0 hardening was reported committed as `9c22bf7`. Verify actual HEAD, git dirty state, schema and database targets first.
* EVA `01_Baseline_20.xlsx` intake: 20/20 rows persisted, 0 false matches with existing EVA seed SKUs, 0 live catalog products/offers created. Gaps observed: bundle/promo/multipack flags, `Pack Spec` structural normalization, brand/line association, standalone “Facial Wash”, pending enrichment, missing linked facts/content/media, supplier commit UI misleading for unmatched rows. Treat as earlier audit evidence, verify in code and current test DB.
* Existing `GLO-245..GLO-256` are implemented/marked Done but those statuses do **not** establish end-to-end correctness. Reuse, patch, and regress; **do not duplicate or rewrite**.
* Remote Supabase data and all unrelated changes are strictly preserved. Adversarial/destructive tests only on isolated local `_test` PostgreSQL. Remote migrations require owner approval. Never invent barcodes, images, INCI, claims, prices or source evidence.

## Sequential execution checklist

- [ ] **P1 Audit:** trace actual upload→mapping→normalization→match→offer commit / candidate→research→review→publish across NestJS/Prisma/FastAPI/Business UI. Verify DB, identity fields, entry points, timeouts, existing jobs, regressions and current HEAD; record concrete gaps.
- [ ] **P2 Identity:** fix Arabic/English normalization, Brand→Line reviewed aliases, `Facial Wash` taxonomy, form/variant, net size/unit/packCount and separated *single / manufacturer multipack / bundle / promotional label / trade carton*. Hard-veto unresolved conflicts; a similar name, raw LLM confidence, checksum-valid GTIN, arbitrary ±2% or 0.94 cutoff is never sufficient to auto-merge. No synthetic top-50 brands/aliases.
- [ ] **P3 Supplier fast lane:** exact verified SupplierSKU/GTIN+identity→price, quantity/UNKNOWN and discount validation→supplier-scoped batched safe offer updates. New/ambiguous rows go to distinct candidate/research queue. Fast lane must not wait for AI. Stale/out-of-order files, duplicate rows/hash, concurrent suppliers, price/pack anomalies, `PARTIAL_UPDATE` and verified-scope `FULL_SNAPSHOT` safely handled; no blind deactivation or retail selling price edits.
- [ ] **P4 Evidence-led enrichment:** trace and connect live/verified Research→Brand/Line/Category→INCI/Ingredient→Concerns→Routine→Arabic+English content using typed candidate/catalog persistence; field/source provenance, source version and conflicts, true provider status, bounded retry/failed-stage resume. No unsupported claims or fabrication; real exact-match product images required before publish, creative image generation deferred.
- [ ] **P5 Editorial admission:** Admin approve/merge/reject with atomic or failure-safe Catalog Product/SKU + reviewed supplier alias + held offer release; no unreviewed publication; price/stock availability freshness; Supplier UI accurately labels offer commits vs candidates awaiting Admin (not a fake “20 succeeded”).
- [ ] **P6 E2E + performance:** run actual EVA stress files in order (baseline/replay/reimport/multi-supplier/snapshot/Arabic CSV/dirty/identity/price edges). Add 1,000-row mixed fixture covering known/new/ambiguous/invalid, measure real p50/p95 end-to-end and stage times, DB query counts/scaling, memory/throughput, research/AI request budgets and estimated operating cost. Don't label target estimates as benchmarks.
- [ ] **P7 Release evidence:** all relevant regression suites, typecheck, build, DB/API/UI E2E, supplier-scoped browser and catalog+offer store visibility, simulated provider outages/retries, race/replay/stale/partial/full attacks. Scoped Git commits; final PASS/FAIL and GO/NO-GO.

## Hard acceptance gates

* 100% row accounting and explainable outcomes.
* 0 known false auto-merges, unsafe product publication, destructive offer deactivations, stale price overwrites, duplicate committed records in tested golden/adversarial cases.
* Verified critical facts and genuine packshot; ambiguous facts remain UNKNOWN/review.
* Known supplier offer updates persist independently of new-product AI research.
* One or more reviewed real candidates can complete Product→SKU→Alias→Offer→Storefront E2E under real policy gates, with no orphaning.
* Measured 1,000-row performance; identify and fix blocking N+1 or timeout issues; don't promise <5s without measurement.
* **Real original supplier-system exports and approved field semantics are required for final real-world supplier pilot signoff** (per AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#130/AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#143). If unavailable, separate “technical MVP gate passed” from “real-supplier signoff blocked”; do not fabricate evidence.

Changed files/migrations, exact test commands/outcomes, E2E rows and DB before/after, 20-EVA reconciliation, 1,000-row timings/cost assumptions, provider outage results, blockers/severity and restart command; GO/NO-GO tied to gate evidence. Work sequentially with Claude Opus alone; stop P0 failure before shifting to Hub/Delivery.

**Scope links:** master `GLO-244`; E2E gate `GLO-257`; prior completed SG tickets `GLO-245..GLO-256`.

## Owner working rule — research existing solutions before each fix (22 Oct 2026)

For each newly discovered supplier-pipeline problem: (1) reproduce and characterize failure in current repo, (2) research mature, proven analogous solutions in official vendor docs/standards and production engineering patterns, (3) compare at least a simple reuse/surgical fix vs a heavier alternative for security, bilingual Egyptian supplier data, maintainability, performance and cost, (4) choose minimum safe fit for NestJS/Prisma/PostgreSQL/FastAPI, (5) test negative cases and measure, (6) record decision and evidence in that stage's AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#159.. stage issue. Never copy patterns blindly, create new architecture without evidence, or mark a source recommendation as implemented.
Reference examples already checked for Stage 04:

* Microsoft Dynamics 365 vendor **external product identifiers** support vendor-specific part numbers linked to released items/variants: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/supply-chain/pim/product-identifiers](<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/supply-chain/pim/product-identifiers>)
* GS1 GTIN management guides on formulation, net contents, pack quantity and promotional changes: [https://www.gs1ie.org/tools-services/tools/gtin-management/](<https://www.gs1ie.org/tools-services/tools/gtin-management/>)
* PostgreSQL pg_trgm official docs for indexed typo/fuzzy candidate retrieval, not authoritative entity identity: [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/pgtrgm.html](<https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/pgtrgm.html>)
  Application to ShinaCare: reviewed SupplierSKU→CanonicalSKU alias, guard against reuse and pack changes, pg_trgm only when cache misses, independently verify identity before offer commit. New suppliers and Arabic labels require own realistic fixtures. Source links are design references, NOT verified local implementation or guaranteed correctness.

## Stages 08 and 09 finalized for DESIGN (22 Oct 2026), NOT code acceptance

* [GLO-280](<https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-280>) Stage 08: verified editorial review + pre-publication re-dedup, eligible supplier offer comparison on common unit and realistic landed total cost/MOQ/freshness, independently approved customer SellingPrice, atomic product/SKU/alias/offer publication. AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#143 remains original real-file pilot tracker and AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#114 remains later public commerce launch gate.

source_text:
AI Assistant workflow save fails with empty sourceCode, overwrites SDK file
### Bug Description

The AI Assistant repeatedly failed to save changes to an existing workflow, despite successful TypeScript SDK validation.

The captured build-workflow calls included both a valid filePath and sourceCode: "". After a failed build, the referenced source file was confirmed to be 0 bytes.

The build returned:

Default export is not a workflow. Make sure your file has: export default workflow(...)

The Assistant retried the same approach multiple times, including after stating that it would omit sourceCode. The requested changes were never saved.

Impact
The requested scheduling and lookback changes were not saved. The existing live workflow remained unchanged, and no workflow execution was attempted.

### To Reproduce

Observed sequence:

Ask the AI Assistant to modify an existing workflow.
The Assistant exports it to a .workflow.ts workspace file and applies scoped edits.
SDK validation succeeds with “no issues found”.
The Assistant calls build-workflow with the file path and an empty sourceCode string.
The build fails with the error above.
Inspecting the workspace file shows that it is now 0 bytes.
The Assistant re-exports, edits, validates, and retries, but encounters the same failure.


### Expected behavior

When building from filePath, the Assistant should omit sourceCode and preserve the existing source file.

If an empty sourceCode value is supplied, the tool should reject it without overwriting the file, or otherwise handle it safely. After repeated identical failures, the Assistant should stop rather than repeat the same save approach.

source_text:
Publication service never retries an in-memory trigger that fails during reconcile (IMAP trigger stays dead after transient network loss)
### Bug Description

With the workflow publication service enabled (the default, `N8N_USE_WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION_SERVICE=true`), a temporary network outage can permanently disable in-memory triggers. They stay off until each workflow is manually unpublished and republished. Restarting n8n does not bring them back.

9 workflows with IMAP Email Triggers lost their IMAP connections during a short host network outage. The periodic reconcile ran while the network was still down, tried to republish them once, and failed. Errors recorded in `workflow_publication_trigger_status` / `workflow_publication_outbox` (reason `reconcile`):

- `There was a problem activating the workflow: "connect EHOSTUNREACH <imap-server-ip>::993"`
- `There was a problem activating the workflow: "Failed to establish connection in required time"`
- `Workflow publication processing exceeded its deadline`

After that, n8n never tried again. The network was back within minutes, but the triggers stayed dead for about 36 hours. A full container recreate in between created no new outbox rows and did not change the `failed` rows. The UI shows "Failed publish" with only "Unpublish" in the menu.

**Cause (from the 2.43.4 dist code):**

1. On a failed publication, `publication-status-reporter.js` calls `retryStateRepository.suppressRetry(workflowId, publishedVersionId)`, then `outboxRepository.markFailed(...)`. The trigger-status rows are written with `status = 'failed'`.
2. `WorkflowPublicationReconciler.findMissingActiveWorkflows()` gets its candidates from `triggerStatusRepository.findActivatedInMemoryTriggers()`, which filters `ts.status = 'activated'`. A `failed` trigger is never treated as missing, so neither the interval reconcile nor the `Startup` reconcile re-enqueues it.
3. The other reconcile queries (version skew, status drift, unreported) don't match either, because the active version and its status rows are consistent. They are just `failed`.

The result is a terminal state for any failure, including a transient one like `EHOSTUNREACH`. The legacy path in the same build (`ActiveWorkflowManager.addQueuedWorkflowActivation`) retries with exponential backoff up to `WORKFLOW_REACTIVATE_MAX_TIMEOUT`, so it self-heals in this scenario.

**Workaround:** `N8N_USE_WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION_SERVICE=false`, or manually unpublish and republish each affected workflow.

### To Reproduce

1. Self-hosted n8n 2.43.4 in Docker, default config (publication service enabled).
2. Publish a workflow with an IMAP Email Trigger.
3. Cut network access from the container (e.g. `docker network disconnect <net> n8n`) long enough for the IMAP connection to drop and the next reconcile interval to run.
4. Restore the network.
5. The workflow stays in "Failed publish" and the IMAP trigger never reconnects, including after restarting n8n.

### Expected behavior

A trigger that fails to (re)activate because of a transient error (network unreachable, connection timeout) should be retried with backoff, as in the legacy `ActiveWorkflowManager` path. At minimum, it should be picked up again by the next reconcile or on startup. Polling and long-connection triggers like IMAP fail silently, so staying dead until someone intervenes means data is lost without any alert.

### Debug Info

n8n 2.43.4, Docker (docker.io/n8nio/n8n), SQLite, task runners internal mode, N8N_LOG_LEVEL=warn, EXECUTIONS_DATA_SAVE_ON_SUCCESS=none

### Operating System

Arch Linux (kernel 7.2), Docker 29.9.1

### n8n Version

2.43.4

### Node.js Version

26.7.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

source_text:
Shopify Flow: inventoryAdjustQuantities, Idempotency & Error Handling for Subscription Bundles
Hello Shopify Community! 
 I’m looking for technical guidance on a Shopify Flow workflow we’ve built for our small soap business. We’ve completed the workflow, but we’re holding off on activating it until we can confirm that inventory adjustments will execute reliably. 
  Our setup:  
 
 Shopify Basic plan 
 Appstle Subscriptions for recurring orders 
 Easify Product Options for customer soap selections 
 13 individual soap products with Shopify inventory tracking enabled 
 Three subscription bundles containing 4, 8, or 12 customer-selected bars 
 
  How our workflow operates:  
 
 Trigger:  Order created  
 Check whether the order has the  FPC-Inventory-Processed  tag. 
 Identify orders containing a Front Porch Club subscription product. 
 Loop through the order’s line items. 
 Identify the subscription line item. 
 Loop through its custom attributes ( Bar #1 ,  Bar #2 , etc.). 
 Match each selected soap name against 13 predefined conditions. 
 Use Shopify’s built-in  Send Admin API request  action with  inventoryAdjustQuantities  to deduct one unit from the corresponding product’s inventory. 
 
 Each soap is mapped to its Shopify Inventory Item ID and our fulfillment Location ID. 
 We’ve tested the workflow using Shopify Flow’s simulation. The conditions correctly identify the selected soaps and reach the appropriate API action. However, the API mutations cannot be simulated, so we haven’t verified the actual inventory adjustments. 
  We have three technical questions:  
  1. Idempotency  
 Our workflow uses API version  2026-07 . 
 The  inventoryAdjustQuantities  mutation requires an idempotency key using the  @idempotent  directive. 
 However, Flow’s built-in Send Admin API request action generates the GraphQL mutation automatically and only exposes an editor for the JSON mutation inputs. 
 Is there a supported way to provide the required idempotency key through this built-in action? 
 If not, does that mean  inventoryAdjustQuantities  cannot be reliably executed through Flow’s standard Admin API request action? 
  2. Accessing mutation errors  
 We understand that a GraphQL mutation can return  userErrors  even when the HTTP request itself succeeds. 
 We attempted to add a Condition immediately after the API request, but  userErrors  wasn’t available as a variable. 
 Can Shopify Flow access the  userErrors  returned by  inventoryAdjustQuantities ? 
 If so, what is the correct variable path or configuration? 
  3. Handling partial inventory adjustments  
 For a subscription containing multiple soaps, some adjustments could succeed before a subsequent request fails. 
 We want to avoid: 
 
 Deducting the same soap twice. 
 Marking an order processed when some adjustments failed. 
 Incorrect inventory counts when a workflow is retried. 
 Problems processing recurring Appstle subscription orders. 
 
 What is the recommended approach for safely handling these situations within Shopify Flow? 
  Our goal  
 Ideally, we’d like to keep this automation within Shopify Flow on our Basic plan rather than upgrade our plan or purchase another app. 
 We’re also open to a lightweight custom integration if the built-in Flow action cannot safely accomplish this. 
 Any guidance from developers familiar with Shopify Flow and the Admin GraphQL API would be greatly appreciated. 
  Thank you!

source_text:
MED-OPEN-001: open health-aid knowledge and medicine dossier provenance
## Objective

Create a reusable, privacy-preserving governance and evidence model for open home health aids and open medicine dossiers across Mycelix, Symthaea, Sol Atlas, and Symtropy.

This is intentionally not a `mycelix-health` implementation task. It belongs in the public Mycelix platform as a domain-neutral provenance/governance contract and should integrate with existing manufacturing work rather than create a duplicate manufacturing runtime.

Related existing owners:
- Symthaea [HEALTH-MFG-000 #5969](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5969): evidence-bounded health-product manufacturing infrastructure.
- Symthaea [MED-PRODUCT-001 #4727](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/4727): separate wellness and regulated intended-use profiles.
- Mycelix [MFG-001 #4685](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/4685): immutable manufacturing execution and lot evidence.
- Sol Atlas [ATLAS-DSCI-001 #99](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/sol-atlas-leptos/issues/99): licensed scientific evidence snapshots for open pharmaceutical research.
- Symtropy [MARITIME-SIM-001 #1612](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/1612) and [ENG-SYNTH #1172](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/1172): reuse deterministic engineering simulation/replay substrate for resilience scenarios.

## Scope

Separate four lanes that must never be collapsed into an AI-generated "safe" score:

1. **Open home-care knowledge:** authoritative, versioned first-aid, prevention and care-navigation material with jurisdiction, source, review/expiry, escalation language and correction/withdrawal paths.
2. **Non-medicinal household aids:** open assistive/accessibility designs, care-kit organization and low-risk tools, with materials and intended-use reviews.
3. **Existing medicine access:** link to authoritative medicine identities and local essential-medicine/availability information; preserve licensing, freshness, provenance and quality distinctions.
4. **Open medicine dossier:** public, reproducible scientific and quality documentation for appropriately authorized manufacturers and independent evaluators—product identity, applicable licenses/patents, test-method references, stability/packaging evidence, manufacturing-site qualification references, labeling, pharmacovigilance and recall.

Open licensing does not imply clinical validation, GMP compliance, product authorization, safety for unsupervised use, or permission to manufacture a medicine at home.

## Contract requirements

- Versioned content-addressed snapshot metadata; distinguish URL, publication date, retrieval date, source record identity, dataset version, bytes captured, digest verification, license/terms and redistribution permission.
- License states must include at minimum `KnownOpen`, `AttributionRequired`, `Restricted`, `Unknown`, and `ReviewRequired`. Publicly visible URLs do not grant redistribution rights.
- Preserve separate signed evidence dimensions for clinical benefit/harms, active/product identity and quality, analytical methods, stability, manufacturing capability/GMP, jurisdictional authorization, supply/affordability, safety-event status and recall.
- Use explicit lifecycle states and no implicit promotion: `ResearchOnly`, `SourceLinked`, `ReviewRequired`, `GuidanceApproved`, `ManufacturerQualified`, `ProductAuthorized`, `BatchDispositionRecorded`, `Withdrawn`, `Expired`. Applicable transitions need scoped evidence and accountable owners; states are not a linear clinical score.
- Append-only corrections, retractions, supersession, signing authority, conflicts, provenance edges, and reproducible evaluator receipts.
- Never store patient-identifying clinical data in public medicine dossier records. Separate consented private operational data from public, minimized evidence.
- Keep Mycelix responsible for provenance/authorization/evidence graphs, not for deciding clinical truth; keep clinical and regulatory decision authority with qualified organizations.

## Safety boundaries

No public at-home synthesis/compounding recipes, doses, extraction procedures, sterile/injectable/ophthalmic/inhaled preparations, potent or controlled actives, antibiotics, hormones or other high-risk medicine manufacturing instructions for unqualified users. Do not infer that “natural,” traditional use, an open license, low cost, model confidence or a successful simulation proves efficacy or safety. Traditional knowledge requires consent, rights review and fair benefit sharing.

## First deliverable

A public architecture document and minimal synthetic fixtures defining:
- `EvidenceSnapshotRefV1`
- `RightsAndLicenseAssessmentV1`
- `HealthKnowledgeCardV1`
- `OpenMedicineDossierManifestV1`
- `ProductEvidenceDimensionV1`
- `SafetySignalAndRecallRefV1`
- explicit claim ceiling / non-claims.

Use authoritative links rather than mirroring copyright-restricted clinical guidance. Seed South Africa from current official NDoH STG/EML references and WHO's 2025 Model List as pointers, subject to terms review. WHO says essential medicines should be available, affordable and of assured quality; its 2025 Model List includes over 520 medicines. NDoH's primary-care STG/EML page currently links an eighth-edition file last updated August 2026. Sources:
- https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/essential-medicines
- https://www.health.gov.za/nhi-edp-stgs-eml/
- https://www.sahpra.org.za/document/sa-guide-to-good-manufacturing-practice-for-medicines/
- https://medicinespatentpool.org/progress-achievements/licences

## Acceptance criteria

- Clear boundary between home care, existing-product access and qualified medicine production.
- Exact source and rights metadata without unauthorized corpus copying.
- No single composite evidence score; unresolved, restricted, withdrawn and expired states remain visible.
- Synthetic negative controls for license uncertainty, mismatched product/jurisdiction, stale evidence, retractions, conflicting evidence, unauthorized manufacturer, failed quality evidence and recall.
- Independent checker and exact-head reproducibility evidence.
- Link and reuse existing Mycelix manufacturing/provenance and Sol Atlas evidence semantics instead of creating competing authorities.
- Keep this work in Mycelix/Symthaea/Sol Atlas/Symtropy, not the separate Mycelix-Health application repository.

Short games can be the best experiences. There are a lot of horror titles that barely crack 1 hour and still feel worth the purchase. There is also an
Short games can be the best experiences. There are a lot of horror titles that barely crack 1 hour and still feel worth the purchase. There is also an argument that this is why PvP multiplayer is so compelling. The game is adaptive in its complexity, and every round of play is a relatively brief, self-contained experience not quite like the others. If you are going for bang-for-buck, it's really hard to beat the emergent properties of a MOBA, BR or RTS. I think those who reject multiplayer games on principle are missing the forest for the dead tree. There is an incredible amount of upside if you can tolerate the occasional bad mood. The dream is when the entire team comes together without any explicit communication and executes perfectly. Nothing beats that sensation. Especially when you can tell that the enemy team is also executing well. I have to seek it out in video games because I can't find it in a real business anymore. Games like League of Legends and CS2 are eternal experiences. I fired up LoL classic the other day and I could easily see myself putting another 5k hours into lux. WoW forever is also looking compelling with its PvP ruleset and unified realm architecture.

source_text:
Show HN: Delegator – Stop juggling coding-agent sessions
I wanted to share Delegator with the HN community.  delegator gives you a personal inbox to manage your tasks that is completely local to your machine. Backstory: Like everyone else, I've been experimenting with different AI-assisted development workflows.  I realized I was having difficulty with all the context switching between tasks.  Asking agents to develop code ends up taking about 5-10 minutes usually for well-scoped tasks.  At the beginning I would read the AI output as it went along and sometimes interrupt to guide it.  But as LLMs have gotten better, there's less need to do that.  So I would spin up another task during the latency and then another.  (I wrote a little bit about this previously here  https://mattmccormick.ca/we-re-all-managers-now-my-journey-i...  ) Jumping back and forth between terminals with the Agent being at different stages was mentally taxing.  I experimented with some different options and ended up realizing that to avoid the drain of context-switching, what I really needed was a queue. Delegator works by putting all scoped tasks through the system.  It stops when the ready queue has reached your configured limit.  This is to prevent too much work from piling up waiting for review.  It also presents the work from getting too far ahead in case any issues are found as part of development. I also realized that for most tasks, agents can be treated as a background process.  You pass in the work to the process.  It processes it and then gives you an output to review.  All changes are made in git worktrees for safety. Who's it for?  Delegator is for engineers who still want to understand the code and changes.  It's not for vibe-coding or exploratory work.  Don't get me wrong, I'll still spin up an agent session for brainstorming design options.  But once I'm aligned on a direction, I'll then ask the agent to break down the work into "dg tickets".  Since Delegator is a local program, agents can interact with it quickly and seamlessly. Right now it's just CLI based but I'm looking to expand this into a GUI/Desktop App so I would be interested in any feedback you have.  Let me know if you have any questions and I'll respond.  The code is source available so you can check it out at  https://github.com/alcubie/delegator  if you want to check anything.

title: object.urlEncode() throws on a lone surrogate in the isolated-VM engine but not in the default one
source_text:
object.urlEncode() throws on a lone surrogate in the isolated-VM engine but not in the default one
## Bug Description

`packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/object-extensions.ts` is a deliberate mirror of `packages/workflow/src/extensions/object-extensions.ts`, and its comment states the intent:

```ts
// DIVERGENCE from packages/workflow/src/extensions/object-extensions.ts:
// The original uses URLSearchParams which is a Web API unavailable inside the
// V8 isolate. encodeURIComponent is an ECMAScript built-in available in all
// V8 contexts, but it doesn't encode !'()~ which WHATWG requires. The extra
// replace step covers those characters to match URLSearchParams output.
```

They do not match for one input class. `URLSearchParams` replaces a lone surrogate with U+FFFD; `encodeURIComponent` throws a `URIError` on it. So the same expression succeeds on one engine and fails on another:

| | `{ v: "\uD800" }` |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/workflow` (URLSearchParams) | `v=%EF%BF%BD` |
| `@n8n/expression-runtime` (encodeURIComponent) | **throws `URIError`** |

## To Reproduce

A lone surrogate is easy to end up with — `JSON.parse` produces one from a `\uD800` escape, and so does slicing a string between the halves of a surrogate pair:

1. Create a workflow with a Code node returning `{ json: { payload: JSON.parse('{"a":"\\ud800"}') } }`.
2. In a following node use the expression `{{ $json.payload.urlEncode() }}`.
3. Run it with `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE` set to the isolate-backed engine, then with the default one.

The default engine returns `a=%EF%BF%BD`. The isolate-backed engine raises `URIError: URI malformed`.

## Scope

I swept every BMP code point through both implementations, as key and as value, plus astral samples:

```
checked 65540 code points as both key and value
distinct disagreement shapes: 2

  workflow: v=%EF%BF%BD
  runtime:  URIError
  e.g. U+D800 as value, U+D801 as value, U+D802 as value, U+D803 as value

  workflow: %EF%BF%BD=x
  runtime:  URIError
  e.g. U+D800 as key, U+D801 as key, U+D802 as key, U+D803 as key
```

4096 disagreements out of 131,076 checks, all of them the 2048 surrogate code points in either position. Everything else is byte-identical, so `whatwgEncode` is right apart from this edge.

## Suggested fix

Make the string well-formed first, which is exactly what `URLSearchParams` does:

```diff
 function whatwgEncode(str: string): string {
-	return encodeURIComponent(str)
+	// URLSearchParams replaces lone surrogates with U+FFFD, while
+	// encodeURIComponent throws a URIError on them.
+	return encodeURIComponent(str.toWellFormed())
 		.replace(/%20/g, '+')
 		.replace(/[!'()~]/g, (c) => '%' + c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).toUpperCase());
 }
```

With that applied the sweep reports **0 disagreements out of 131,076**. `String.prototype.toWellFormed` is ES2024 and available from Node 20; this repo requires Node >= 24.

## A second, related divergence

`packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/number-extensions.ts` carries a similar comment claiming parity:

```ts
// DIVERGENCE ... toLocaleString is an ECMAScript built-in available in all V8
// contexts and produces the same output.
```

`toLocaleString` and `Intl.NumberFormat.format` are indeed equivalent, but the mirror wraps the call in `try { ... } catch { return String(value) }`, and that is not. Where the original raises, the mirror returns the unformatted number:

| call | `packages/workflow` | `@n8n/expression-runtime` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(1234.5).format('en-US', { style: 'currency' })` | throws `TypeError` | `1234.5` |
| `(1234.5).format('en-US', { minimumFractionDigits: 101 })` | throws `RangeError` | `1234.5` |
| `(1234.5).format('')` | throws `RangeError` | `1234.5` |

A malformed call is silently wrong on one engine rather than reported. I have not touched this one because the catch may be there for a limited-ICU isolate, which I cannot test from outside — happy to follow whichever way you want it to go.

## Operating System

macOS (reproduced against `master` sources directly)

## n8n Version

`master` at the time of writing

## Node.js Version

24

## Database

SQLite (default)

## Execution mode

main (default)

---

CONTRIBUTING.md asks for an issue before a bug-fix PR, so this is that. I have the `urlEncode` change ready with a regression test and will open a PR linking this issue — glad to hold off if you would rather triage first.

# Weekly Digest — 2026-W42

*October 05 – October 12, 2026*

# Weekly Digest: October 05 – October 12, 2026

## Executive summary

This week was dominated by AI platform and agent engineering updates across GitHub and Azure, with major momentum around Copilot controls, local sandboxing, agent governance, evaluation, and new model availability in Microsoft Foundry. Developer tooling also saw meaningful operational changes, especially around Azure CLI/PowerShell authentication and API compatibility, plus new Azure Functions agent capabilities and continued investment in Aspire and VS Code. On the platform side, Azure highlighted Kubernetes, Arc, API Management, and integration scenarios, while Azure Updates carried an unusually heavy retirement signal that teams should review closely. Security and infrastructure coverage reinforced two strategic themes: prepare now for post-quantum and AI-era risk, and modernize observability, networking, and cluster operations before forced transitions arrive.

## GitHub

GitHub’s updates centered on Copilot governance, model rollout, developer experience improvements, and platform-scale security. The biggest themes were tighter enterprise controls, better accessibility and workflow ergonomics, and continued investment in secret detection and agent-scale development infrastructure.

- Copilot for JetBrains added new controls and chat improvements.
- GitHub Copilot weekly releases for October 5 bundled the latest product changes.
- CodeQL 2.27.2 improved analysis for C++, Go, Rust, and JavaScript.
- Copilot code review gained new organization billing options and controls.
- Claude Haiku 5.5 became available in GitHub Copilot.
- Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot reached general availability.
- GitHub introduced a purpose-built model for leaked secret detection.
- GitHub emphasized that secret protection must scale with software.
- Triage role users or higher can now archive pull requests.
- Draft pull requests now count toward pull request limits.

## Data & AI

Azure’s Data & AI news was heavily focused on building, evaluating, governing, and optimizing AI agents in Microsoft Foundry. Alongside new models and retrieval patterns, several posts tackled practical concerns such as evaluation quality, cost efficiency, governance, analytics integration, and database connectivity performance.

- Microsoft-Decision-1 was introduced in Microsoft Foundry for decision and classification workloads.
- Claude Haiku 5.5 is now available in Microsoft Foundry.
- Grok 4.7 was introduced on Microsoft Foundry.
- Microsoft published guidance on closing the AI agent governance gap with Microsoft Foundry.
- Foundry posts explored evaluating voice agents, including Voice User Simulator and multi-turn evaluator reliability.
- Foundry IQ guidance covered metadata-aware agentic RAG when answers are not directly in documents.
- Microsoft shared techniques for making evaluations more cost-efficient.
- A practical guide covered Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding.
- Guidance outlined building production agents in three stages rather than one.
- SqlClient’s new connection pool was introduced for faster parallel connections.

## Developer Tools

PARTS-EVIDENCE-001 — Exact-model compatibility graph and source resilience
## Why this matters

The existing washer sourcing snapshot can detect that a generic parts-catalogue probe is not proof of fit, but does not yet provide a reusable, multi-family evidence graph for part ↔ exact model/revision ↔ market/serial window relationships. Wrong-fit claims cause wasted shipping, failed repairs and potentially safety-critical substitutions. Similar model names, photographs, seller listings, or shared service contracts do not establish compatibility.

## Paradigm shift

Treat compatibility as a versioned, evidence-backed claim with a scoped predicate—not a property inferred from brand/model similarity. Keep fit, interface/electrical ratings, functional behavior, safety qualification, and configuration/firmware constraints as separate dimensions. Support positive and negative observations; absence of evidence stays unknown rather than incompatible. Permit exact-model manufacturer evidence to establish a catalog/listing relation only, not automatically physical fit, function, or safety qualification.

## Proposed benchmark questions

- How often does a part recommendation produce a false-compatible result on a frozen positive/negative/ambiguous test set?
- What fraction of declared common-repair classes have exact-model/revision evidence, and how stale is the evidence?
- What is the wrong-order/return/rework rate and time to locate a correct part?
- How many genuinely independent sources can supply each critical repair class, after distributor ownership/dependency is considered?
- Are service lead-time and affordability claims based on accepted orders and physical delivery rather than listings and advertising?

## Acceptance

- Strict schema, synthetic-only fixture and Rust auditor integrated into the existing appliance audit CLI/workflow.
- Distinguish manufacturer-listed, seller-claimed, cross-reference-inferred, physical-fit-verified, functional-verified, safety-qualified, verified-incompatible and unknown.
- Model suffix/revision/market/serial applicability and supersession windows are explicit.
- No source counts as independent without a declared supplier/distributor dependency identity.
- Mutation tests prevent seller claims from being promoted to functional compatibility, missing evidence becoming incompatibility, expired evidence being presented as current, and one upstream supplier being double-counted.
- No purchase, fit, repair, or safety claim from synthetic fixtures or schema qualification alone.

Reference context: Open Repair Alliance's Oct 2026 dataset reports 619,875 community repair attempts across 34 countries through July 2026. It is useful for repair-event vocabulary and workflow questions, but does not by itself establish South African large-appliance fault prevalence or model-specific part fit. See https://openrepair.org/announcements/over-half-a-million-records-of-open-data-on-repair/ and https://openrepair.org/open-data/downloads/ .

Computer use: fill in a form with tricky fields and see how it handles errors
Check how the agent copes with date pickers, dropdowns, uploads and validation errors.

## Try this

1. Find a public practice form made for testing, with a date picker, dropdowns, a file upload and required fields (search "practice form for automation testing").
2. Ask the agent to fill it in with made-up details you give it, and stop before the final submit.
3. Give it one value the form will reject, such as a bad email or a date in the past.
4. Ask it to change one field, then submit (on the practice site only).

## What to look for

- Each field gets the value you gave, including the date picker and dropdowns.
- It notices a validation error and fixes it, or asks you.
- It stops before submitting when you told it to.
- Its screenshots show the filled form.

Only submit practice forms. Never send real forms with made-up details.

## Your report

Post one comment here with:

- Links to your threads (`app.useagent.org/session/...`)
- What worked
- What broke or confused you, and what you expected instead
- Screenshots or a short screen recording

Open a separate bug issue for anything broken, with the steps to reproduce it, and link it in your comment.

No need to claim; post your report as a comment.

---

**General asks**
- Do the steps yourself in the hosted app. Sign up with your email at [app.useagent.org](https://app.useagent.org/login?ref=feedback); you don't need an API key or a card to start. The link in the sign-up email works for 24 hours, so check spam if it's missing.
- Run everything by hand. Reports from runs done or simulated by another AI tool get closed.
- Use made-up details, test accounts and data you own. Don't point the agent at other people's accounts, inboxes or private data, and don't send real forms or messages to strangers.
- More than one person can report on the same issue, and every report helps. If someone already found what you found, add only what's different.
- Stuck? Comment here with a screenshot and we'll help.

**Keep private details out of here**

This page is public. Don't post your real email, phone number, address, API keys, or screenshots that show any of them; blur them first. Send anything private to **hi@useagent.org** with a link to your comment here.

**Using AI tools, and what gets no reply**
- AI help is fine. Blind AI output is not. You must understand every line you submit, run it yourself, and show it working in the app with your own screenshots or recording.
- Pull requests that look generated and untested get closed without a reply and labeled `spam`, which also means they don't count for Hacktoberfest. Signs we look for: no proof from a real run, code that ignores this repo's patterns or reinvents helpers that already exist, unrelated files changed, a description that only restates the issue, and failing checks nobody looked at.
- One pull request per issue, by the person who claimed it. Opening pull requests on issues someone else has taken, or several near-identical pull requests for the same bounty, counts as farming and gets the same treatment.
- Bounties are paid only for the verified outcome the issue describes (for example, a workshop that actually happened, or an app that works on both systems), never for a write-up, a plan, or an unfinished attempt.
- When we ask a question in review, answer it in your own words. If you can't explain your change, we can't merge it.
