source_text:
Proposal: global supplier catalogue from free sources (CoE results + Open Supply Hub + Trase), after the trip
**Decision needed:** approve a global supplier catalogue, built from free sources we're allowed to use, after the trip-critical work (#13 → #8 → #10 → #9). **Recommendation: approve, but build it after Jan 17.** This answers your question on #8 about where the data would come from.

## Problem / opportunity
The Sourcing CRM starts with 41 Costa Rican organisations. A roaster or importer sourcing from Colombia, Ethiopia or Brazil starts with an empty list, and no free worldwide producer registry exists. The research found three sources we're allowed to use. Together they cover top farms, plus co-ops, mills and exporters, in about 17 origins.

## Proposed feature (what Z will see and be able to do)
- **Load suppliers** in the Sourcing tab, by origin (multi-select). It adds source-linked, *unverified* organisations, the same way the Costa Rica seed works. Loading twice never duplicates.
- Each organisation shows its **source and license** and keeps `verified = no` until you mark it.
- On every organisation, **Check certificate** links open the Fairtrade (FLOCERT) and Rainforest Alliance public searches pre-filled with its name. Nothing is copied from them.

## Approach (files touched, data sources + their terms, new dependencies)
- **Cup of Excellence results** (ACE public results pages, about 17 origins, 1999–2026): hand-curated facts per lot (farm, producer, region, rank, score, auction $/lb) with a link back. This matches the Costa Rica seed and ACE's guidance. We won't use ACE's Farm Directory, which is for members only.
- **Open Supply Hub coffee locations** (co-ops, mills, warehouses, exporters; **CC BY-SA 4.0**): a coffee extract downloaded by hand from the free web tier, stored in its own file `app/crm/seed_osh_coffee.json` with attribution. The README data-source table will note that this file is CC BY-SA, not MIT. We won't use the paid API.
- **Trase coffee exporters** (2020, 10 producing countries): only if the Zenodo license turns out to be open. I'll check that first and drop the source if it isn't.
- New `source_license` field in `app/crm/schema.py`, and per-country seed loading in `service.seed()`. No new dependencies and no scraping.
- Rejected alternative: scraping national registries or certification databases. None offers a feed, and their terms are unclear or restrictive.

## Out of scope
Personal contact details (never seeded), paid customs or shipment data (it would improve quality, but we won't wire it in), and auto-refresh (a manual yearly refresh is fine).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Load by origin, idempotent; every record has a source link and license and `verified = no`
- [ ] The README data-source table lists each source with its terms, including the CC BY-SA note for the OS Hub file
- [ ] Certificate links on the organisation page
- [ ] ruff + pytest pass; demo-mode curl smoke test

## Size: M (2 runs). Build after #10 and #9, ideally after the trip.

## Research behind it
[agent/research/2026-10-20-global-producer-catalog-sources.md](https://github.com/zack-hum/coffee-intelligence-v1.1/blob/docs/research-2026-10-15/agent/research/2026-10-20-global-producer-catalog-sources.md) (PR #12)

source_text:
Allocation edge cases leave orders stuck or over-allocated
Found during the docs review (#96). Each was read from the code; none has a test.

**1. An order allocated entirely by hand never reaches suppliers.**
- Allocating every line from the supplier list (`CreatePurchaseOrderItemHandler` → `OrderItemAllocator::forOrderItem`) creates the PO items as PENDING.
- PO items only move to PROCESSING at the end of an `OrderAllocator::process()` run that started with something outstanding (`OrderAllocator.php`, `allItemsAllocated()` → `updateItemStatus()`).
- After a full manual allocation, clicking Allocate returns "No items to allocate." (`AllocateOrderHandler`) and changes nothing.
- `app:build-purchase-orders` only picks orders with no PO yet (`CustomerOrderDoctrineRepository`), and acceptance only reads PROCESSING POs.
- The order stays Pending until someone sets each PO item to Processing by hand.

**2. A cancelled order item still counts as outstanding.**
- An item can only be cancelled while nothing is on a PO, so its outstanding quantity is its full quantity.
- `getOutstandingQty()` doesn't look at the item's own status (`CustomerOrderItem.php`), and `OrderAllocator::process()` doesn't skip cancelled items.
- So Allocate can put a cancelled line on a PO. If no supplier has the stock, the order reports "Cannot allocate all items" for ever.

**3. Rewind can over-allocate a line.**
- `PurchaseOrder::forceRewindToPending()` sets every item to PENDING, including REFUNDED and CANCELLED ones.
- A refunded item's quantity has usually been allocated again on another PO by `app:refund-purchase-orders`. After a rewind it counts again (`getQtyAddedToPurchaseOrders()` skips only cancelled and refunded items), so the line is on POs twice.

**4. The nightly refund skips rejected items on a mixed PO.**
- `app:refund-purchase-orders` handles POs whose overall status is REJECTED.
- A PO's status is its least advanced item. A rejected item next to an ACCEPTED one is never refunded or reallocated automatically.

**5. A partly allocated order is never picked up again by the schedule.**
- `app:build-purchase-orders` needs an order with no PO.
- If one line had no supplier with stock at the time, it waits for someone to click Allocate.

### To decide
- Should Allocate also move manually created PENDING PO items to PROCESSING when nothing is outstanding, or should a separate action do it?
- Should rewind leave REFUNDED and CANCELLED items alone?
- Should the schedule retry orders with outstanding quantity?

JNISleuth-MCP – Recover Stripped JNI Bindings and Ollvm Branches for Ghidra/Ida
Hi HN, I’m a security engineer focused on Android anti-malware and reverse engineering.
When reversing hardened Android apps or wild malware, one of the most tedious parts is crossing the Java-to-Native (JNI) boundary when `.so` binaries are stripped, methods are bound dynamically via `RegisterNatives` inside an OLLVM-flattened `JNI_OnLoad`, and `JNIEnv ` vtable calls decompile as raw pointer offsets like `(*(code *)( param_1 + 0x548))`.
I built JNISleuth-MCP to automate that workflow:
1. It parses multi-DEX APKs for `native` declarations and sweeps `.rodata` / `.data.rel.ro` (or section-header-stripped `PT_LOAD` segments) for `(char* name, char* sig, void* fnPtr)` triplets.
2. It statically resolves ARM64 OLLVM `CSEL` + `BR X8` indirect branches and `.rodata` jump tables in `JNI_OnLoad` (and can patch them in-place with direct `B.cond` / `B` instructions).
3. For runtime-packed samples that detect Frida, it includes a C++/NDK Dobby collector that hooks `RegisterNatives` mid-function.
4. It syncs the full 233-slot `JNIEnv*` vtable types and recovered C signatures into headless Ghidra and IDA Pro 9.0 (`idalib`/`idat64`), and exposes a model-agnostic MCP server + OpenAI/Gemini/Ollama tool schemas.
The repo includes a synthetic multi-DEX + stripped ARM64 `.so` crackme so you can test the entire pipeline in 30 seconds without needing a live malware sample. Would love feedback from anyone doing mobile RE or binary analysis!

source_text:
HTTP Request node with pagination does not refresh credentials that use preAuthentication on 401
### Bug Description


The HTTP Request node does not renew an expired token for credentials that use `preAuthentication` (for example Microsoft Entra Service Principal) when pagination is enabled.

When the stored Microsoft Graph access token expires (every 60 to 90 minutes), Graph answers:

```
HTTP 401 {"error":{"code":"InvalidAuthenticationToken","message":"Invalid token lifetime."}}
```

n8n shows "Authorization failed - please check your credentials". "Retry On Fail" (3 tries, 5000 ms) does not help: all tries fail with the same error. The Microsoft Entra sign-in logs show no service principal sign-in during the failing executions, so n8n does not request a new token. The workflow works again only after another workflow uses the same credential without pagination, gets a 401, and renews the stored token.

Root cause (n8n 2.44.6, unchanged on master):

1. `requestWithAuthenticationPaginated` (`packages/core/src/execution-engine/node-execution-context/utils/request-helpers/pagination.ts`) sets `simple = false` and `resolveWithFullResponse = true` for each page.
2. Thus `requestWithAuthentication` (`.../request-helpers/authentication.ts`) resolves the 401 instead of throwing it. The `preAuthentication(credentialsExpired = true)` refresh and the resend exist only in its `catch` block, so they do not run.
3. `pagination.ts` then throws the 401 itself, outside the refresh path.
4. Each node retry reads the same expired token from the database.

`requestOAuth2` already handles a resolved 401 under `simple: false` (it throws it so that the token refresh runs). Credentials with `preAuthentication` do not get this handling. This affects all such credential types with HTTP Request pagination.

Related: #14426 (same symptom in the Microsoft Entra ID node, fixed in #30943 at node level).

### To Reproduce

1. Create a "Microsoft Entra Service Principal" credential for an app registration with the `Mail.Read` application permission.
2. Create a workflow: Schedule Trigger (every 10 minutes) → HTTP Request (typeVersion 4.2):
   - Authentication: Predefined Credential Type, Credential Type: Microsoft Entra Service Principal
   - `GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/<user>/mailFolders/inbox/messages`
   - Pagination: Mode "Response Contains Next URL", Next URL `{{ $response.body['@odata.nextLink'] }}`, Pagination Complete When "Other", Complete Expression `{{ !$response.body['@odata.nextLink'] }}`, Limit Pages Fetched: 10
   - Settings: Retry On Fail (3 tries, 5000 ms)
3. Use this credential in no other workflow.
4. Activate the workflow and wait until the first token expires (60 to 90 minutes).
5. All later executions fail with 401 "Invalid token lifetime". The Entra sign-in logs show no new service principal sign-in.

### Expected behavior

On a 401 for a page, n8n runs `preAuthentication` with `credentialsExpired = true`, stores the new token, and sends the page request again. This is the behavior without pagination and for OAuth2 credentials.

source_text:
Instance-level MCP: `search_workflow_executions` always fails output-schema validation after upgrading to 2.42.6
### Bug Description

After upgrading a self-hosted instance from 2.39.8 to 2.42.6, the instance-level MCP tool `search_workflow_executions` fails on every call from Claude (claude.ai custom connector) with:

```
Structured content does not match the tool's output schema: data must NOT have additional properties
```

It fails even with a filter that returns zero executions (a workflow with no executions), so the extra property seems to be on the root object of the structured response, not on individual execution rows. Other read tools work on the same connection: `search_workflows`, `get_workflow_details`, `get_workflow_execution` (metadata only), `search_nodes`, `get_node_types`. Refreshing the client's tool list does not help (same 13 tools, same schema). The same call worked on 2.39.8 with the same client and scopes (`workflow:read` + `execution:read`).

**Additional context**
Probably related to a change in the response shape (pagination or count fields) that was not reflected in the tool's `outputSchema` with `additionalProperties: false`. Clients that don't validate structured content may not notice.

### To Reproduce

1. Self-hosted n8n 2.42.6 (Docker, Postgres, `n8nio/runners` external), Instance-level MCP enabled, OAuth client with `workflow:read` + `execution:read`.
2. From an MCP client that validates `structuredContent` against `outputSchema` (Claude), call `search_workflow_executions` with any arguments, e.g. `{ "workflowId": "<any exposed workflow>", "limit": 5 }`.
3. The client rejects the result with the error above.

### Expected behavior

The tool's `structuredContent` matches its declared `outputSchema` (or the schema declares the new property), as in 2.39.8.

### Debug Info

- n8n version: 2.42.6 (self-hosted, Docker), upgraded from 2.39.8
- Database: Postgres 16
- Execution mode: regular (main) + external task runners
- MCP client: Claude (claude.ai custom connector), OAuth
- Hosting: Coolify

### Operating System

Ubuntu Linux 24.04 (Docker, Coolify)

### n8n Version

2.42.6

### Node.js Version

v26.7.0

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

I think you're making the wrong takeaway here. LLMs aren't bad because of sycophancy tendencies. Any prediction at all is bad when it isn't based on r
I think you're making the wrong takeaway here. LLMs aren't bad because of sycophancy tendencies. Any prediction at all is bad when it isn't based on real data, whether or not it ends up being correct, whether or not it is made by an LLM, a human, or some other thing capable of spitting out a number. Analogize to basketball here. How confident are you that you can hit a free throw? If you ask someone who has played a thousand hours a year for the past ten years, has recorded their own statistics, and has averaged 70% success rate oer those past ten years, and they tell you they're 70% confident they can hit a free throw, that's a good prediction. If you ask me and I give you any prediction at all, I'm full of shit. I haven't played basketball or taken a free throw in 30 years. I can pull a number out of my ass, I can reason through it, I can do a Fermi, I can assume I'll be the average of all people who have ever tried and do my best to collect whatever data might exist on brand new players with no experience trying to take a free throw for the first time. I can narrow that to people my height, my age. Now we're getting better, but it's still not as good as having a real record of my actual past performance and basing a prediction off of that. This is just science. Hierarchy of evidence. Epistemology. Sometimes answering a question requires collecting data that doesn't exist yet and waiting a while, in the meantime admitting you don't have an answer. It was already sorely lacking in the world, but in this age of oracles, it's only getting worse.

source_text:
T27G Epic: Trinity Game — guided onboarding quests, player progression and achievements
# T27G — Trinity Game / Quest System (Epic)

## Vision
Create the global game/quest layer for Trinity. The game teaches new participants how the product works through welcome screens and interactive gameplay, then tracks verified progression so each player can see their level, achievements and contribution history.

This is a system-level responsibility and should have a dedicated game agent/team, proposed code **T27G** (confirm naming against the existing 27-team registry before registering). T27G owns game design, onboarding quests, progression rules, badges/credentials and the integration contract between gameplay and real Trinity activity. It works under Queen's coordination and cooperates with T27U (University) rather than duplicating curriculum ownership.

## Core experience
1. A newcomer enters the Trinity world and starts a guided welcome quest.
2. Each quest step introduces one real product concept through the existing map/honeycomb and focused interactive scenes.
3. The player performs a meaningful action: explore a spec, complete a lesson, inspect a dependency, run a test, open or complete a task, or make a reviewed contribution.
4. The system records verified completion and advances quest/level progress.
5. The player sees a profile showing level, completed quests, earned badges and evidence-backed contributions.
6. Achievements can be shared through a stable public profile/achievement URL, with privacy controls.

## Agent boundary
- **T27G Game Agent:** game loop, onboarding, quest graph, progression/level rules, achievement criteria, badge/credential metadata, UX narrative and game telemetry.
- **T27U University Scientist:** canonical teaching content, course structure, learning objectives, theory modules and educational correctness.
- **Queen:** global coordination, assignment and cross-agent orchestration.
- Engineering agents: implement product capabilities and provide tests/evidence.
Avoid a second course engine, task tracker, profile store or orchestration framework. Reuse existing systems after auditing them.

## Progression and credentials
- A level must be derived from explicit, versioned rules and persisted quest events, not a decorative counter.
- A badge requires a defined criterion and evidence (completed lesson, passing test, reviewed contribution, etc.).
- Keep learning completion, contribution status, reputation and rewards as separate dimensions.
- Non-transferable on-chain credentials / soulbound tokens are a possible future delivery mechanism, not an assumed existing feature. First define a platform-neutral achievement schema and verify feasibility, privacy, wallet/account binding, revocation/correction, sybil resistance, cost and applicable chain standards. Do not promise token issuance or financial value before a tested implementation and approved policy.
- Avoid exposing private user activity. Public sharing must be opt-in and only expose approved evidence.

## Technical plan
### Phase 0 — audit
- Inspect existing game/Arena/map UI, welcome flow, course system, player identity/profile, task/test status, monitoring, agent registry and any token/credential code.
- Identify canonical event sources and persistence; document what exists vs missing.
- Reuse existing visual design and square-cell map; do not create a parallel game frontend.

### Phase 1 — vertical slice
- One first-time-user onboarding quest with 5–7 short steps.
- At least one step links to a real honeycomb cell/spec and one step to a T27U course/lesson.
- At least one practical step is verified against a real task/test/event rather than self-reported click completion.
- Persist quest progress and derive a level from explicit rules.
- Award one test badge with criterion, timestamp/version and evidence reference.
- Display a progress view and a shareable achievement page, with privacy-safe defaults.
- Include skip/resume/replay paths, accessibility, mobile layout and reduced-motion support.

### Phase 2 — extensible game system
- Data-driven quest definitions and prerequisites.
- Reusable quest-step types and validation handlers.
- Versioned levels/badge rules and migration strategy.
- Admin/agent-authoring workflow with review and safe publication.
- Optional credential adapter after platform-neutral badge model is validated.

## Acceptance criteria
- New participant can complete onboarding without prior knowledge and understand the map, specs, agents and how to make a useful contribution.
- Quest completion and level are reproducible from persisted events and documented rules.
- At least one achievement is awarded only after evidence validation.
- T27G and T27U responsibilities are clear and integrated without duplicate systems.
- Existing map/course/task systems are reused; no parallel dashboard or fake progress.
- Security/privacy review covers shared profiles, forged events, replay, identity binding and any future token mechanism.
- Tests, telemetry, known limitations and a next-phase roadmap are included.

## Explicit non-goals for MVP
- No token price, financial reward or GPU payout promises.
- No requirement to deploy a blockchain credential in the first slice.
- No arbitrary scripts embedded in social posts; shared links open a safe Trinity-hosted quest.
- No redesign of the existing honeycomb map.

## Deliverables
1. Architecture audit and component reuse map.
2. T27G agent/team definition using the actual registry convention.
3. Quest schema, progression rules and badge evidence model.
4. Working onboarding vertical slice and tests.
5. Documented credential adapter proposal, including trade-offs and decision gate.

source_text:
Show HN: Hindsight – Lightweight, elegant, open-source tracker for Windows/macOS
Hi HN, I’m building Hindsight, a free, open-source activity tracker for Windows and macOS. I know there are plenty of time trackers. I wanted something that combined automatic tracking, detailed charts, and cross-device sync in a lightweight app with an interface I enjoyed using. I couldn’t find a free option that fit, so I started building my own. Hindsight records active apps and window titles while it’s running, without requiring you to start and stop timers. You can explore your activity through daily, weekly, and monthly charts, drill down into individual apps and window titles, and use a yearly heatmap to spot patterns. Categories are customizable. There’s also an optional screenshot and OCR feature for finding something you previously saw on screen. Both are off by default. When enabled, you can search recognized text and jump back to the corresponding screenshot. The AI features can generate daily summaries or answer questions about your activity, with links back to the underlying records so you can check the answers. You can use a local model or connect a cloud API; third-party API fees may apply. Optional sync through Google Drive or WebDAV lets you view activity from Windows and Mac devices separately or together. I’ve also recently added plugin support so other developers can extend the app. I’d appreciate feedback, particularly on how you’d want to explore your activity history. What would make this useful to you beyond simply showing how many hours you spent in each app? Happy to answer questions about how it works.

Vienna, a year ago.  A quiet, dark little bar, Schwartze Flamingo.  A friend and I are sitting there on a Thursday evening, kinda bored.  It’s the sor
Vienna, a year ago.  A quiet, dark little bar, Schwartze Flamingo.  A friend and I are sitting there on a Thursday evening, kinda bored.  It’s the sort of place that just feels like it’s missing something.  Plenty of space for it, whatever it is.  Just, missing. I look up from my beer, which I kinda don’t want, and say to my friend, “there’s gotta be something better to do than sit here getting drunk..”, and as I say it, I look over his shoulder, my eye caught by the glint of some shiny thing.  Looking closer, it’s a sticker on the divider of our booth, ‘Pinball Crew Vienna’ .. “like .. we could find and then play pinball, for instance!”, I exclaim, kind of half assed. My friend looks over his shoulder too, and takes a picture of the sticker, and goes quiet for a moment while he looks things up .. “well, there’s a tournament tomorrow, and its in our neighborhood .. I’ve never played pinball, whats it like?” What?!! Where?! “In the IKEA building at the Westbahnhof”.   A building I had, to that point kind of despised, because I loathe IKEA in general. Nevertheless, the next weekend, we put away our aversions to global particle board distribution, and make our way to the Westbahnhof .. Jo+Joes, a hostel I had no idea existed, occupies the 5th floor.  The elevator opens, and it is like the pearly gates spreading wide, disco balls for miles to see, a joyous bright and pastel atmosphere, people laughing everywhere, smiles from wall to wall .. and oh, so many pinball machines! “VIENNA IS LIT!”, scream the posters, and the immediately recognizable sound of flipping spinners, drop target resets, inevitable drain lanes and bumpers galore, greet us. I immediately sign up for the tournament.  I haven’t played pinball properly - for fun or for competition - in 40 some odd years.  I’d grown up on a beach esplanade in Australia, my Dad’s burger shop, where I’d witnessed the many much loved pinball machines of my distant memories, slowly at first, and then suddenly like a fever, be replaced with Breakout and Space Invaders, the first ‘real computers’ I’d ever seen as a small kid. All the memories come back.  The love I had for that one drop target that’d get a free game, the shock of the bump targets, perfectly aligned, sending another coin into the slot.  The delightful whiff of solenoids and window cleaner.  The internal wiring I felt in myself, changing, adjusting to new things learned.  That old familiar hacker vibe, at its root, analog and perfectly shaped. So, I played for 6 hours straight, just blistering everything I could extend .. and I came 63 out of 65 competitors, and it was a BLAST! Just walking past the 30 or so machines, crammed into this crazy hostel I’d not known even existed due to my prejudices and bigotries, replaced now with curiosity and a kind of relief .. all the good times came flooding back - and now, as a seasoned systems engineer in his 50’s, it was just the right time, too.  Newly divorced, trying to find myself a bit, in a city that will eat you alive slowly, this was the perfect new (old) hobby for these weary bones. I play every week.  I joined a pinball club, started my own team, made us t-shirts.  The weekly journey to FlipperAsyl (perfectly named) injects life and joy and vigor into things again. The IKEA building is our meeting point now, they have two tables permanently installed .. Wrestlemania and Avengers.  We only play Avengers, our little group have a competitive edge, and every month one of us takes the throne, having learned some new tricks or two. Eventually we connect with the other folks in our neighborhood .. slowly all our high scores are erased by one FLO, who we track down and invite and challenge, on the regular. Pinball is a quantum machine for calculating fun  and  disappointment, but mostly fun. It is powered by human soul. Play it with your friends, teach each other things as you learn them, get to know the table and get to know yourselves. Each table has lessons to learn, the generations themselves visible in every machine.  The soul of thousands of fun-seekers can be felt, if you pay attention to the quirks and rhythms.  The spirit in the machine is really there, I promise.  You can feel it. Had Barracora at home for a few months, she felt positively possessed, and for many weeks, was our little shrine. Got Swords of Fury at home, now. My pinball club leases tables to trusted members - a solution to the GAS that afflicts the pinball crew. (Gear Acquisition Syndrome - i.e. too many tables not enough room) There’s another twist.  Pinball is a male-dominated sport. Our little team of discarded men, new fathers, old fathers, some of us recovering addicts, some just in it for fun - we have bonded over the tricks and details, this past year.  It has been a truly unifying experience for our little club of men. But FlipperAsyl has ladies nights too - necessary because we men do tend to dominate - and that is also fun to observe at a distance. There is cross-pollination too of course - I regularly learn major things from some of the nice regular ladies in the Asyl. It has been soothing and healing. We’ve already mapped out all the pinball machines we can find in the city, before one of us discovered the pinball map .. so now there’s a day trip planned, to the Pinball Museum Budapest, and our little merry crew of pinball misfits will make that train journey some day soon.  It’s gonna be GREAT. So .. yeah .. “VIENNA IS LIT!”, is happening again this year, in case any HN’ers are in town and want another GREAT hobby to apply themselves to .. hey, if you’re out of town, maybe get yourself a plane ticket, get yourself booked into JO+JOES, and get ready for 2 days of PURE FUN.  https://events.eventjet.at/e/vienna-is-lit-wiens-groesstes-f...  See you there!

Useful project — quantity mapping is exactly the hard part of PrintNC builds.

One data gap for EU users: the same part list has very different landed cost depending on shipping origin. US-direct orders end up +40–50% after customs/VAT handling, while the same parts from EU warehouses (PL/DE/CZ/ES) arrive in 3–10 days with zero customs. There are also a few recurring part-spec traps (1605 vs 1610 ballscrew ends, anti-backlash nut handedness, rail length vs travel) that a generator could validate.

Looking for AI Chatbot That Can Use External Knowledge Base (TXT/CSV) for Support & Product Info
Hi all, 
 I’m looking for a Shopify-compatible AI chatbot that can respond to customer questions using  a structured knowledge base  — like a TXT or CSV file — rather than relying only on what’s in Shopify’s product listings. 
 Many of my product options and configurations are managed through a  third-party product options app , so I can’t rely on Shopify’s native catalog alone. I need a bot that can: 
 
 Import and reference external data (ideally via TXT or CSV) 
 Respond  only using the content I provide , without making things up or rewording 
 Follow a consistent format with specific titles and URLs (not summaries or paraphrases) 
 Be powered by something like ChatGPT, so it can follow clear instructions 
 Integrate with my Shopify storefront 
 
 Here’s the thing — I’ve already been able to get this working exactly how I want using ChatGPT directly , but none of the Shopify app store bots I’ve tried so far come close to that level of control or reliability. They often lack file upload support, or they try to guess and summarize — which just doesn’t work for what I need. 
 If anyone out there has found a solution — app, workaround, or even a custom integration — that can do this kind of knowledge-based chatbot well inside Shopify, I’d love to hear about it. 
 Thanks in advance!

Show HN: Standard Topic – An AI and RSS-powered news and resource platform
Hi HN, I'm John, a knowledge management and AI enablement professional. I created Standard Topic, an AI and RSS-powered news and resource platform, with assistance from Claude Code. Standard Topic uses AI integrations and RSS feeds to curate news and resources across relevant topics and presents these in the form of top stories, trending items, and a curated prompt library to easily gather further context on a given topic (examples of topics being World News, Politics, Business, Technology, Sports, Science, Health and more.) On topic hubs, you can find a regularly updated at-a-glance AI briefings providing relevant updates, top stories with AI insights and cited sources, and additional recent news coverage. A governance system is in place with AI assisting in ranking stories, retiring items from the top stories section, determining which additional news is displayed, and more. An AI-generated briefing podcast, in the format of a radio news program, releases each morning and evening (5 AM and 5 PM ET), covering the latest global news. While in the past I've released apps and websites that felt duct-taped together and which I stopped using after some time, with this one I've actually found myself using it more than Twitter/X and other daily news briefing platforms, while also leading me to more frequently engage directly with publishing platforms cited on Standard Topic. My recent work in AI has been around finding practical uses in the content and knowledge management areas for integrating the technology, and Standard Topic has developed into what I see as a product that uses structured outputs and automated insights to deliver consistent and trustworthy, cited content while maintaining transparency about being primarily powered by artificial intelligence. There's still some kinks to work out in terms of automated workflows, design aspects and more. Let me know what you think!

Map: the VIN-based parts shop for carlab.rs, full architecture spec
## Destination

A full architecture spec for carlab.rs's real parts shop, ready to hand to implementation: VIN/model-based parts lookup (germsp.ru-style exploded-diagram ETK, starting with BMW), a part-identity/cross-reference data model spanning N suppliers (Intercars + our own warehouse + future suppliers), the fitment-data sourcing decision (paid TecDoc-like license vs build-by-hand vs supplier API), the core commerce platform choice (rebuilt Medusa vs an alternative, informed by research), per-supplier/warehouse markup with multi-source stock/price aggregation, Typesense search, a minimal admin (manual fitment curation running in parallel with whatever automatic source is found), cash+card payment (cash at pickup first, online card fast-follow), pickup first with delivery fast-follow, and ru/en/sr localization via the existing `@podbor/i18n` pattern.

**Acceptance:** no open decision blocks someone from starting to build. Every architectural fork below is either decided (see Notes) or has a research/grilling/task ticket in flight. This map does not carry execution — it ends at a spec, not working code (contrast with the old CarLab-Medusa map, #61, which did carry execution).

## Notes

**Domain:** `AGENTS.md`'s CarLab section, `docs/adr/0028-no-vehicle-dictionary-until-fitment-is-required.md`, `docs/adr/0034-pause-medusa-deploy-pending-shop-rebuild.md`, `docs/research/serbia-online-shop-legal.md` (the existing Serbian legal research — see "Accepted, not revisited" below). The old shop map is [#61](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/61) (closed) — its 57-story spec (#77) and ADRs 0016–0027 describe the *abandoned* battery-only catalog+cart; this effort replaces it, not resumes it.

**Reference UX, studied live:** germsp.ru/etk (BMW ETK). VIN decodes to model/engine/trim with production-date and spec facts (oil volumes, paint code, etc). Catalog is organized as groups → exploded-diagram schemas with numbered callouts; each position is an OEM number + attributes (volume, "effective until" production-date cutoffs, gearbox/steering-side variant codes) + "see equivalents" (cross-reference/aftermarket numbers) + "see prices and availability", which expands into several lead-time tiers (70d/45d/16d/2-4d/1d/in-stock), each with its own price and quantity — and "in stock" splits further by region/warehouse with separate add-to-cart buttons. This is the shape carlab.rs is aiming to match, starting with consumables (germsp.ru's group=02). **Correction (from #323's research):** germsp.ru is an unrelated Russian importer, not an Intercars reseller — treat it as a UX/UI pattern to copy, not as evidence of how Intercars itself structures its data or pricing tiers.

**Standing decisions from the destination-pinning grilling session (2026-10-16), full rationale and the live Q&A in [Pin the destination and initial scope decisions](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/321):**

- **Maximize ready-made.** Prefer an existing open-source/SaaS piece over hand-rolling, at every layer (platform, fitment data, VIN decode, search, payment) — custom code only where nothing fits. This is the standing tie-breaker for every research ticket below.
- **N-supplier architecture from day one**, not hardcoded to "Intercars + our warehouse". Each supplier/warehouse is a row with its own connector shape and its own markup %; adding a third supplier later is a new row, not a model change.
- **Part identity is layered, not one id.** OEM/factory number, manufacturer-brand aftermarket number, EAN, and each supplier's own article number are all different things pointing at the same physical part. Resolved as `Part` / `PartIdentifier` / `SupplierOffer` — see [GLOSSARY.md](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/blob/main/GLOSSARY.md), [ADR-0035](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/blob/main/docs/adr/0035-part-identity-one-canonical-part-brand-keyed-identifiers.md) and the gist in Decisions so far.
- **Fitment data: both paths in parallel, not sequenced.** An automatic source (paid license, alternative data vendor, or a supplier API that already carries fitment) and a manual hand-curation admin workflow are designed side by side from the start, each covering what the other doesn't — not "try automatic, fall back to manual only on failure".
- **Paid fitment-data licensing is on the table** (e.g. TecDoc-style) if the price is reasonable — research should price options, not restrict itself to free/open-source.
- **Markup is a per-warehouse/supplier %, editable in the admin.** No per-category/per-brand granularity at launch (fast-follow if ever needed).
- **Payment: cash at pickup/meeting first; online card payment is fast-follow**, designed in this spec but not required for launch.
- **Delivery: pickup-only first; delivery within Serbia is fast-follow**, same treatment as payment above.
- **Admin: prefer whatever admin ships with the chosen commerce platform** (e.g. Medusa's own admin) over building one from scratch. Day-one users are the owner plus 1-2 staff, one role, no RBAC needed yet.
- **Existing Serbian legal research is accepted as sufficient, by explicit owner choice** — `docs/research/serbia-online-shop-legal.md` is not being re-opened for online payment/fiscalization/delivery even though it explicitly left those out of scope when written for the old pickup-only/cash-only shop. This is a knowingly accepted gap, not a finding that the gap doesn't exist.
- **Old Medusa code stays in the repo for this map.** `apps/medusa`, `infra/medusa`, the old `apps/auto-service` shop pages are not deleted here — deletion is a task for implementation kickoff, once the new architecture is chosen, not part of this planning effort (point 12 of the owner's brief: this map is research + decisions only, no code changes).
- **Localization:** reuse `@podbor/i18n` (ru/en/sr) exactly as approved.rs/details.rs/carlab.rs already do. No new i18n mechanism — every new page/admin surface this spec produces plugs into the existing section-loader pattern.
- **Pilot:** start concretely with BMW (matches the germsp.ru reference studied live), roughly 2-liter engines, then automate outward to other German brands — the exact model/engine-code list is sharpened once the fitment-data research ([Fitment/TecDoc-like data source options](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/324)) shows what's actually well covered.
- **Intercars relationship:** in-progress negotiation, preliminary green light — API research can proceed on a best-effort/public basis now; a task tracks getting real docs/sandbox access.

## Decisions so far

- [Pin the destination and initial scope decisions](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/321): closed immediately after the destination-pinning grilling session — see the bullet list in Notes above for the gist of each standing decision; the ticket holds the full live Q&A.
- [Research: Intercars e-cat API capabilities](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/323): Intercars runs a real public REST "IC API" (catalog, inventory/stock, pricing, sales, delivery, invoice), registered-client auth, pull/polling only (no webhooks), documented batch caps (100 SKUs / 10 warehouses per call). VIN/fitment is TecDoc-licensed through Intercars as a TecDoc consumer, not Intercars-proprietary — their own endpoints look like SKU/category search, not VIN search. Open questions for the access task (#328): exact auth/grant type, whether Serbia is live on the IC API vs CSV/legacy-only, real rate limits, and dropship-to-third-party-address support. Full findings in `docs/research/intercars-ecat-api.md` on branch `research/intercars-ecat-api`.
- [Research: online card payment (PSP) options for a Serbian shop](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/326): **recommendation is CorvusPay and Monri WSPay**, get both on a call. CorvusPay is the only genuinely independent PSP with a published rate card (EUR 30/mo + 1.30%+EUR0.04 EEA / 3.20%+EUR0.04 non-EEA) and explicit Dina/DinaCard support; Monri, WSPay and NestPay all run on the same Payten/Asseco SEE infrastructure, Monri WSPay being the regional default with the broadest e-commerce-platform plugin ecosystem but unconfirmed Dina support. Stripe flatly rejects Serbian merchant entities; PayPal/Payoneer are cross-border-only, not confirmed to settle RSD locally, so neither is viable as the primary checkout. No PSP in this market publishes exact fees/settlement timing/onboarding docs — that needs a direct sales conversation, not more research. Full comparison in `docs/research/serbia-online-payment-psp.md` on branch `research/serbia-online-payment-psp`.
- [Research: ready-made / open-source options for a VIN-based parts shop](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/322): **no open-source project combines fitment/compatibility search with a storefront** — every fitment feature anywhere (dedicated automotive tools or bolted onto Magento/WooCommerce/PrestaShop/BigCommerce) is a hand-populated Year/Make/Model/Engine join table, because real fitment data (TecDoc/ACES-PIES) is licensed closed data, not software a platform can ship. Narrows the platform-choice ticket (#329) to two live candidates: **Spree** (Ruby/Rails, BSD-3-Clause, free-tier multi-warehouse + multi-vendor `seller_id` primitives mapping directly onto "N suppliers with markup", first-party Meilisearch — but a new Rails runtime in an all-TypeScript monorepo) vs **Vendure** (TypeScript, GPLv3 core + paid commercial license, same runtime as the rest of this repo, an exact-fit pricing-override hook). Saleor/Shopware/Sylius/Bagisto/Medusa have no comparable fitment or multi-vendor story. A from-scratch Astro+DB build is real but narrower than first assumed: it could reuse `packages/shop-catalog`/`@podbor/i18n`/`site-kit`, not `packages/lead-crm`'s storage layer, and still needs a fresh Postgres + search engine regardless. **Recommendation: don't build a commerce platform from scratch — narrow #329 to Spree vs Vendure.** Fitment/VIN logic is custom either way, platform choice doesn't change that. Also found and reused a thorough prior unmerged research pass (`docs/research/platform-survey.md`, branch `research/platform-survey`, written under stale issue numbers #293/#291 from an earlier session) rather than redoing it from scratch. Full findings in `docs/research/parts-shop-opensource-landscape.md` on branch `research/parts-shop-opensource-landscape`.
- [Research: VIN-decode service options](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/325): **NHTSA vPIC is not viable** — live-tested against a real BMW VIN, it resolved only WMI/plant and failed structurally on model/engine/trim (its check-digit/model-year rules are North-America-specific). Open-source ISO 3779/3780 libraries (`vininfo`, `vin-decoder`) are WMI-level only — manufacturer/country/plant/year-candidate + checksum, useful as a free validation layer but their own docs list extra engine/trim tables only for AvtoVAZ/Ford AU/Nissan/Opel/Renault, not BMW. Of the paid EU options, **Vincario** (rebranded vindecoder.eu) is strongest — ~48 fields, correctly resolves BMW engine/body/series, 3 free lookups/mo then paid tiers. **Critical finding: none of these, paid or free, reach germsp.ru/ETK depth** (paint code, interior trim, fluid volumes, exact production date) — that lives in OEM EPC/ETK or TecDoc-style systems, not generic VIN-decode APIs. TecAlliance's own material says TecDoc already bundles a VIN/VRM lookup tied to its fitment data (flagged, not deep-dived — overlaps the fitment-data-sourcing ticket). **Recommendation: treat "VIN decode" and "BMW parts-fitment spec" as two separate purchases**, use a free ISO 3779 library for validation now, and resolve the fitment-data ticket first since its answer may make a dedicated VIN-decode subscription redundant. Full comparison in `docs/research/vin-decode-options.md` on branch `research/vin-decode-options`.
- [Research: fitment/TecDoc-like data source options, with pricing](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/324): **TecDoc** gives aftermarket fitment + OE cross-refs by KType but only coarse matching (gearbox/steering-dependent parts return multiple candidates) and no exploded diagrams; no public price, a regional partner exists (QUANTUM-AutoMARKET, Belgrade) to get a real quote from. **BMW's own AOS portal** has the full OEM catalogue/diagrams free, but it's a human tool not a data feed, and its terms suggest an EEA/Switzerland company requirement that likely excludes a Serbian company (unverified). **Parts-Catalogs.com is the only vendor with public reseller pricing for OEM diagrams including BMW** (EUR 229-1,299/mo by volume), with a REST API/widget and a 2-day demo — but its data provenance/rights are undisclosed. Laximo has good OEM data but is Russia-based/RUB-billed, logistically awkward for a Serbian company. The Intercars API (#323) carries no fitment/cross-reference data at all, only a TecDoc-ID mapping alongside stock/price — complements TecDoc, doesn't replace it. ACES/PIES is the wrong standard (US/CA/MX, no bundled fitment data, $2,500-12,075/yr). germsp.ru-style sites disclose no data source; Russian practitioners typically combine Laximo + TecDoc as two separate paid services (scraping is also acknowledged as common in that market, not a path to recommend here). **Recommendation: get a scoped quote from QUANTUM-AutoMARKET for TecDoc, in parallel prototype Parts-Catalogs.com against real BMW VINs (B47/B48/N47/N20 engine codes) while confirming their BMW data rights in writing, use Intercars only for price/stock, skip ACES/PIES and scraper-based options, and fall back to manual staff lookup if TecDoc pricing doesn't pencil out at pilot scale.** Full comparison in `docs/research/fitment-data-sourcing.md` on branch `research/fitment-data-sourcing`.

- [Domain-model the part identity & cross-reference model across N suppliers](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/327): **the canonical unit is `Part`** — one interchangeability position (e.g. "oil filter, BMW B47/B48"), never a single brand's number; the OEM number and every aftermarket equivalent sit under one `Part`. Every number is a `PartIdentifier` keyed on the compound `(type, brand, value)` — `oem` / `manufacturer-number` / `ean` — brand mandatory even when unknown (`generic`), so two manufacturers reusing the same string never collide. A supplier's own article id is **not** a `PartIdentifier` — it lives on `SupplierOffer`, scoped to one specific brand-variant, so the same Part sold under two brands by one supplier is two separate purchasable lines at two different prices, never one button hiding a staff pick. Rejected: OEM-number-only canonical key (kills non-OEM-stocked inventory as a dead end), one-Part-per-brand with no shared parent (kills fast "find everything that fits" lookups), supplier-sku-as-a-fourth-identifier-type (duplicates what `SupplierOffer` already is). Full rationale in [ADR-0035](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/blob/main/docs/adr/0035-part-identity-one-canonical-part-brand-keyed-identifiers.md), terms in the repo's first [`GLOSSARY.md`](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/blob/main/GLOSSARY.md), both in [PR #333](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/pull/333) (not merged). **Explicitly deferred, not solved here:** the Vehicle/fitment-position side — spun out as [Domain-model the Vehicle/fitment-position entity](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/334), which also reverses part of ADR-0028.

**All 5 research tickets plus the part-identity ticket are now resolved.** Remaining open work on this map: [Task: get real Intercars API docs/sandbox access](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/328) (unblocked, owner/business-side), [platform choice](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/329) (unblocked), [pilot scope sharpening](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/330) (unblocked), [Domain-model the Vehicle/fitment-position entity](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/334) (unblocked, new); [multi-warehouse pricing UX](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/331) still waits on the platform choice, and [admin fitment-curation workflow](https://github.com/Zikrasoft/approved_rs/issues/332) still waits on the new Vehicle/fitment ticket.

## Not yet specified

- Typesense hosting (self-host vs Cloud) and the sync pipeline from whichever commerce platform gets picked — depends on the platform-choice ticket.
- Delivery mechanics within Serbia (carrier, zones, cost) — deliberately vague, it's a fast-follow.
- Online payment integration specifics (checkout flow shape, webhook/order-status mapping) — depends on the platform choice and the PSP research.
- Admin roles/RBAC beyond owner + 1-2 staff — revisit if the team grows.
- Per-category/per-brand markup granularity beyond the per-supplier % — fast-follow if ever needed.
- Catalog expansion beyond the BMW/German-2-liter pilot (other brands, other part categories) once the pilot proves out.
- Typesense indexing schema specifics (how a `Part` with several `PartIdentifier`s and `SupplierOffer`s becomes one or more search documents) — the identity model is settled (#327), only the index shape is still open, and likely falls out of the platform-choice ticket.

## Out of scope

Nothing yet. The owner chose "full spec for the whole product" as this map's destination (not an MVP-only spec), so nothing from the original 13-point brief has been ruled beyond it — every point is in scope, sequenced via the fast-follow markers above rather than excluded.

How often do you sync supplier stock with your Shopify store?
I run a small dropshipping store and built an automation that syncs supplier stock to Shopify every 4 hours. It works, but I still worry about the gap: an item can sell out at the supplier between syncs and a customer can still order it. 
 For those of you with supplier-based inventory: 
 
 How often do you sync? 
 Do you keep a safety buffer (for example, showing 0 when the supplier has fewer than 5)? 
 How do you handle the occasional order for something that’s actually gone? 
 
 Curious what’s worked for others.

W25 — Real-Time Events & Notifications: E2E Verification
# W25 — Reliable Real-time Notifications and Operational Events

**Audit/acceptance tracker; not new implementation ownership.** Owner requires **real-time** server-confirmed updates in this W25/W26 phase, not manual refresh. Historical Done issues are not proof of functioning browser streaming. Design-first audit only; no code, Git, DB, Linear changes by coding agents. Read current repo before selecting SSE/WebSocket. Cloud Neon must not be used for mutating tests. Use isolated disposable \*\_test DB for real acceptance.

## Should-be scope

* Online customer sees customer-safe order state, availability action required, approved amendment, delivery/return/refund and support changes **without refresh**. Supplier sees only their own PO updates, Hub only its own receiving/preparation/dispatch queue, support only authorized urgent cases. Driver assignment only if current driver surface exists.
* Reuse canonical owner-domain committed state, existing AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#18 durable Notification Outbox and AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#67 domain events if appropriate. Real-time transport does NOT own workflow state; backend REST API remains authoritative for all writes. Event has eventId/type/entityId/version/cursor and minimum non-sensitive content; frontend refetches canonical projection. Never broadcast sensitive supplier cost, internal notes, prices from unsanitized records or customer PII.
* **Transport proposal:** Prefer authenticated NestJS SSE for server-to-client push if code inspection confirms a largely one-way flow; use existing WebSocket if already present/justified. No Redis/Kafka/new broker or paid messaging provider by default. External WhatsApp/DM delivery is independent of website real-time and not promised immediate.
* Strict server-side scoped subscriptions: customer Order ownership, guest opaque token/session, supplierId, Hub assigned location, Driver assigned run, support/admin permissions. For browser SSE, native EventSource cannot attach custom Authorization headers: choose safe same-origin HttpOnly-cookie auth or authenticated fetch streaming; never include guest token in URL or logs. Check auth revocation and CORS.
* Reliability: committed-event delivery only, deduped events and meaningful notifications, no optimistic state changes, reconnect/heartbeat, cursor or canonical REST snapshot on missing messages, jitter/backoff and safe polling fallback. React Query targeted invalidation. Test multiple tabs, process restart, slow/offline network, duplicate/out-of-order events, and deployment proxy buffering/timeouts. Single-process MVP okay if limitation and multi-instance rollout boundary explicit; don't assume in-memory event emitter works across replicas.
* Notification center backed by durable read/unread records, not transient stream only; meaningful customer events only, no spam on every sourcing step; actionable links point to owner-domain decision.

## Acceptance matrix

1. Two browsers see same current Order after one confirmed change, with no refresh or duplicate side effects.
2. Supplier A vs B, Hub A vs B, Customer A vs B and guest invalid access: no cross-tenant subscriptions or event data leaks even with guessed IDs.
3. Timeout/reconnect/server restart restores exact current status/COD/refund and unread state via trusted REST snapshot.
4. One outbox event retried multiple times does not duplicate notifications/actions.
5. Safety/support P0 event reaches human operator queue, not just an unhandled outbox record.
6. Render truthful customer-safe event only after committed transaction; provider/stream outage does not affect actual Order state.
7. Server connection cleanup and production proxy/multiple-instance strategy assessed.

## Existing implementation ownership

AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#18 Outbox (Done), AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#67 events (Done), [GLO-74](https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-74/implement-order-readstatus-apis) status (Done), [GLO-83](https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-83/build-hub-operations-console) Hub UI (Todo), AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#2 Supplier UI (Backlog), AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#19 support queue (Backlog), [GLO-91](https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-91/close-critical-tests-authsecurity-and-failure-paths)/205 security/testing and [GLO-93](https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-93/run-end-to-end-release-candidate-smoke-test) E2E. **W25 remains UNVERIFIED** until safe stream + REST persisted state E2E evidence. No code implementation from this audit ticket.

EU sourcing notes for the V4 BOM: EU-warehouse suppliers + customs traps (info)
Sharing notes from mapping the PrintNC / LowRider / MPCNC BOM to suppliers that ship from EU warehouses — relevant for anyone sourcing the V4 parts list from Europe.

Key findings from doing my own EU build:
- US-direct orders (control boards, ballscrews, kits) end up +40–50% delivered once customs/VAT handling and shipping are added. EU-warehouse orders clear in 3–10 days with zero customs.
- The PrintNC steel kits sold in DE have been sold out for months; local steel merchants cutting per your section list are the practical fallback.
- Recurring ordering traps seen across build threads: 1605 vs 1610 ballscrew end machining, anti-backlash nut handedness mismatch, rail length vs travel mismatch, plate thickness vs gantry design revision, PSU current vs parallel stepper sets, and missing metric fastener assortments.
- Per-build quantity tables (X/Y/Z axes, 1015/1501/2006-class variants) mapped to PL/DE/CZ/ES warehouse suppliers.

Full free list (maintained, includes traps and a 48-hour ordering plan):
https://gist.github.com/estovisioncontact-bit/d80d74146b9ea5b9ebd7586559b130a2
Web version: https://estovisioncontact-bit.github.io/cnc-sourcing-pl-eu/

I compiled this while sourcing my own build — the guide is free; there's an optional paid custom-research service if maintainers or users want country-specific supplier quotes. Happy to contribute an "EU suppliers" section directly into this repo/wiki if that's preferred over an external link.

source_text:
Modern Oral Nicotine Products Market Intelligence: Trends, Consumer Shifts, Regulation, and Competitive Dynamics
Introduction

Modern oral nicotine products are reshaping parts of the nicotine industry through compact formats, discreet use, and evolving consumer preferences. Products such as nicotine pouches, tobacco-free oral nicotine sachets, and newer dissolvable formulations are attracting attention from manufacturers, retailers, regulators, and investors. Their development reflects changing expectations around convenience, product variety, and alternatives to conventional tobacco consumption.

However, the category is not defined by growth opportunities alone. Public health concerns, differences in national regulations, product safety questions, and restrictions on marketing are influencing commercial strategies. Understanding these interconnected factors is essential for evaluating the market's direction and identifying developments that may affect its long-term prospects.

Understanding the Modern Oral Nicotine Products Market

Modern oral nicotine products generally deliver nicotine through the lining of the mouth without requiring combustion. Nicotine pouches are among the most recognizable formats, typically containing nicotine, plant-based fibers or other fillers, flavoring ingredients, and moisture-regulating components. They are placed between the gum and lip for a specified period, allowing nicotine to be absorbed orally.

These products should not be treated as a uniform category. Formulations, nicotine concentrations, ingredients, packaging, and intended consumer groups vary considerably. Some oral products contain tobacco-derived nicotine, while others use synthetic nicotine or nicotine extracted from tobacco. The distinction can affect product classification, regulatory treatment, and manufacturing requirements.

Market analysis must also distinguish tobacco-free nicotine pouches from traditional smokeless tobacco products. Although both may be consumed orally, their compositions, exposure profiles, and applicable regulations can differ.

Key Factors Influencing Market Development

Convenience and Changing Consumption Patterns

Discreet packaging, portability, and the absence of smoke make oral nicotine products attractive to some adult nicotine consumers. Unlike combustible products, pouches do not require lighting or produce smoke during use. Their compact format can also fit into existing retail and e-commerce distribution models, where permitted.

These characteristics influence product positioning and purchasing decisions. Nevertheless, convenience should not be confused with safety. Nicotine is addictive, and oral products can cause dependence and other adverse effects. Their appeal and commercial performance must therefore be assessed alongside potential public health consequences.

Product Formulation and Differentiation

Manufacturers compete through differences in pouch texture, moisture content, flavor profiles, nicotine delivery, packaging design, and product consistency. Formulation decisions affect the consumer experience, manufacturing complexity, and quality-control requirements.

Nicotine concentration is particularly important. Higher concentrations may increase exposure and the potential for adverse effects, while inconsistent product composition can create additional safety concerns. Responsible development requires validated testing, clear ingredient disclosure, appropriate labeling, and controls that help prevent accidental exposure, especially among children.

Innovation is therefore increasingly connected to formulation stability, manufacturing precision, packaging integrity, and compliance rather than product novelty alone.

Retail Access and Distribution Strategies

Distribution has a significant influence on market accessibility. Convenience stores, specialist tobacco retailers, and other authorized outlets may serve as important sales channels in markets where these products are legally available. Online sales can provide additional reach, but they also raise concerns about age verification, cross-border transactions, and compliance with local restrictions.

Retail availability differs substantially between countries. Businesses must account for licensing obligations, permitted sales channels, advertising limitations, taxation, and minimum-age requirements before entering new markets.

Competitive Landscape and Business Considerations

The competitive environment includes established nicotine companies, specialist pouch manufacturers, contract producers, and emerging brands. Companies with experience in regulated consumer products may have advantages in quality assurance, supply-chain management, distribution relationships, and regulatory administration.

Competition is not determined by brand recognition alone. Reliable product quality, transparent labeling, compliant packaging, manufacturing efficiency, and the ability to respond to changing regulations can influence a company's position.

For decision-makers, [modern oral nicotine products market intelligence](https://www.pristinemarketinsights.com/modern-oral-nicotine-products-market-report) involves evaluating the interaction between consumer demand, product design, regulatory exposure, and commercial execution. A useful assessment should consider market accessibility, operating costs, product differentiation, and the risks associated with changes in public policy.

Companies should also evaluate supplier concentration and ingredient sourcing. Dependence on a limited number of nicotine suppliers or packaging manufacturers may expose operations to cost volatility, interruptions, and quality inconsistencies. Diversification, supplier qualification, and documented quality-management processes can improve operational resilience.

Regulatory Environment and Public Health Considerations

Diverging National Policies

Regulation remains one of the most important determinants of market access. Countries differ in how they classify nicotine pouches, whether they permit their sale, which authorities oversee them, and what restrictions apply to product composition, packaging, and promotion.

Some jurisdictions impose specific authorization requirements or restrictions on nicotine pouch sales. Others apply broader nicotine-product rules or prohibit particular products. These differences complicate international expansion and make regulatory monitoring a core business function.

Manufacturers and distributors must verify current local requirements instead of assuming that approval or lawful sale in one country establishes permission elsewhere.

Youth Access and Consumer Protection

Youth nicotine use is a major public health concern. Flavoring, compact packaging, and discreet consumption may contribute to product appeal, making age restrictions, responsible marketing, and effective retail controls particularly important.

Clear warnings, child-resistant packaging where required, secure storage, and reliable age-verification procedures can help address preventable risks. Marketing practices should not target minors or imply that nicotine products are harmless.

Evidence concerning the health effects of newer oral nicotine formulations continues to develop. Although these products avoid combustion, that difference does not establish that they are safe. Nicotine dependence, potential cardiovascular effects, oral irritation, and accidental ingestion remain relevant considerations.

Challenges and Strategic Risks

Several challenges may influence the category's development. Regulatory changes can increase compliance costs, restrict product availability, or require reformulation. Public scrutiny may also affect brand reputation and retailer willingness to stock certain products.

Other risks include price competition, inconsistent product standards, uncertain long-term consumer retention, and changing perceptions of nicotine use. Businesses that rely heavily on aggressive flavor expansion or high nicotine concentrations may face additional regulatory and reputational pressure.

A balanced assessment should avoid assuming that early commercial momentum guarantees sustainable demand. Product adoption can change quickly when rules, prices, distribution access, or consumer preferences shift.

Future Outlook

The future direction of modern oral nicotine products will depend on the interaction of regulation, consumer behavior, manufacturing standards, and public health policy. Product consistency, transparent disclosures, traceable ingredients, and stronger age-control systems are likely to remain important operational priorities.

Market participants should monitor changes in national legislation, authorized product lists, retail access, taxation, and enforcement practices. They should also distinguish measured sales performance from unverified growth expectations and consider how different regulatory scenarios could affect market entry and profitability.

Conclusion

Modern oral nicotine products represent a distinct and evolving segment of the broader nicotine industry. Their compact formats and varied formulations create commercial opportunities in some jurisdictions, while addiction risks, public health concerns, and regulatory differences impose substantial constraints.

A credible assessment requires more than tracking product launches or consumer interest. Manufacturers, retailers, and strategic decision-makers need to examine product quality, lawful distribution, responsible marketing, supply-chain reliability, and the implications of changing policy. Businesses that incorporate these factors into their planning will be better positioned to understand the category's risks and opportunities without overlooking its wider public health responsibilities.

Show HN: Ternlux – Free, local-first, bring-your-own-key AI pipeline builder
For the past 12 years as a data engineer, I've been building pipelines across many different business categories and sizes. Most pipelines that I’ve encountered were relatively simple jobs and required more orchestration and infrastructure than the work seems to justify. I wanted to make it easier for business users or analysts to take on the less complicated requests and technical engineers be able to focus on more complex pipelines. So in the past year I've been building a local desktop application (Mac/PC/Linux) to make it easy enough for analysts to build pipelines and answer analytical questions they have about their data, no matter their level of technical expertise. It’s called Ternlux, and it streamlines the process of transforming and getting your data where it needs to go. There are two key features: - Ask questions: AI helps to write the query for your connection and answer your question
- Build reusable workflows: The AI generates SQL, Python, and workflow logic that executes based on your defined rules and triggers One of the key advantages of the application is you can perform cross-database joins between databases, local files, vector databases, and cloud storage. You describe the workflow you want and the app writes the code and builds the environment to execute it in (for local joins, it uses either JS, Python, or DuckDB to execute the code). For example, if I want to build a workflow that joins a Postgres table with a CSV file and write the results to Snowflake, I just describe the tables I want to use, the keys to join on, and where the join should run. The app takes care of the rest. I also wanted the app to be as secure as possible. It always asks for approval before performing any database or local file manipulation. It never sends anything to Ternlux servers if you haven’t opted into telemetry. It’s important to note that the app will send query results to your selected AI provider to analyze and answer your questions. It will also send the schema and a small sample size of your data to build workflows properly. It is a bring your own key application. It supports Gemini, Claude, OpenAI, and any models that are OpenAI compatible (Ollama, LM Studio, Openrouter…). All of your credentials stay encrypted locally. And the app is completely free including all features (besides the AI models you use with your own key obviously). I’ve built a quick demo showcasing the applications Demo:  https://www.ternlux.com/online-demo/  3-min overview:  https://youtu.be/tA7N7wiLliA  The list of connectors that exist:
Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, MongoDB, Pinecone, LanceDB, S3, GCS, Azure Blob, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, and Google Sheets. I would love your honest feedback on this. How can this product be improved? Would you currently use it as a tool to replace your current tool or in conjunction with your other tools? What feature do you find most useful and I should focus on from the list?
