Task 032 — Convert the digital-asset portfolio into an income-first execution backlog
# Task 032 — Convert the digital-asset portfolio into an income-first execution backlog

**Parent programme:** Task 028 / portfolio roadmap — https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/issues/95  
**Related:** competitor/repository register https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/issues/114 · Stage 0 audit https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/issues/115 · customer evidence sprint https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/issues/116  
**Status:** Planning task registered; no revenue, customer validation, audit completion or deployment is implied.

## Objective

Bring every plausible digital asset and reusable capability into the portfolio's durable list of work to be done, while prioritising the shortest credible path to first income. The goal is not to build every idea. The goal is to identify what already exists, who may pay for it, what can be offered now as a service, and what minimum work is needed to deliver it reliably.

## Governing rule

**Sell a well-scoped service using existing skills/assets before investing in a new app.** Reuse/upgrade first; build only after evidence. Every item must have one canonical owner/repository, provenance and licence status, maturity evidence, buyer/customer, next action, dependencies/cost, risks, and a measurable validation or revenue milestone. Unknown means UNKNOWN, not assumed owned or ready.

## Full digital-asset families to inventory

1. **Portfolio, governance and operating systems:** personal portfolio/hub, repository and deployment registry, enterprise governance, reusable workflows, checklists, decision logs, task tracking and operating procedures.
2. **Software and PWAs:** existing apps, prototypes, modules, templates, APIs, integrations, offline workflows, dashboards, calculators, automation and mobile/web interfaces.
3. **Data and knowledge:** structured catalogues, farm/animal-health knowledge, supplier/buyer intelligence, public procurement information, competitor research, market evidence, taxonomies and reusable reference data (with source, licence, freshness and accuracy recorded).
4. **AI and automation:** AI Studio apps, prompts, agent workflows, model/API adapters, evaluation/test harnesses, local/offline fallbacks and free-tier API configuration guides. Never store API keys or secrets in Git.
5. **Content and intellectual property:** articles, research, guides, SOPs, templates, business plans, proposal/tender documents, training content, code, original designs, brand assets and downloadable products; verify authorship and commercial rights.
6. **Distribution and audience:** websites, domains, blogs, social profiles, newsletters, SEO assets, directories, opt-in lead channels, affiliate links, analytics and customer enquiry flows. Track account owner, consent, destination, performance and terms.
7. **Commercial infrastructure:** service packages, pricing hypotheses, quotation/proposal templates, contracts, supplier/customer onboarding, lead CRM, follow-up sequences, delivery checklists, case-study evidence and customer support.
8. **Relationships and market access:** permissioned supplier, buyer, farmer, integrator, SME, professional-provider, partner and funder relationships; track source, consent, last contact and next action without placing confidential personal data in public repositories.
9. **Research and funding assets:** grant/tender calendars, eligibility research, partner maps, application components, budgets and reporting templates. Verify current calls and eligibility before acting.
10. **Design and media:** original logos, visual systems, illustrations, photos, video/audio, product screenshots and presentation assets with licence/attribution and source files.
11. **Reusable technical foundations:** CI/build pipelines, test suites, security/privacy checklists, deployment recipes, backups, exports, documentation generators and common components.
12. **Legacy, duplicate and uncertain assets:** dormant apps, forks, templates, AI-generated scaffolds, experiments and near-duplicate projects. Classify reuse / upgrade / extract / archive / pause / rights-check; do not count forks or templates as wholly owned IP without evidence.
13. **Client/employer/third-party assets:** track separately as service relationships or authorised case studies only. WCD, MOSHA, YellowBlue, MegaDealsMA, Tshono and other third-party/client work are not automatically owned products; no changes or commercial reuse without permission.

## Income-first execution order

### P0 — Ten fixed-scope offers; sell before building (first 7 days)

**Pricing note:** The BWP amounts below are proposed test prices, not verified market rates or promises of income. Confirm scope, client ability to pay, delivery time, taxes/fees and competitor alternatives during discovery. Quote in writing; request a deposit where appropriate. Start by marketing the most relevant offers to each prospect, not by publishing all ten indiscriminately.

1. **Website & Digital Presence Health Check — test price BWP 750–1,500; 3–5 working days.** Review one website (up to 10 key pages), mobile usability, broken links, page titles/meta, contact details, basic accessibility signals, lead path and obvious technical risks. Deliver a prioritised findings report and 30-minute handover. Excludes penetration testing, guaranteed rankings, paid tools and implementing fixes.
2. **Website Care & Monthly Change Plan — test price BWP 500–1,200/month for a defined small site.** Monthly uptime/basic availability checks, one scheduled content change, link/contact-form spot check and short status report. Define hosting access, response windows, backup responsibilities and exclusions first. Hosting fees, emergency recovery, redesign and third-party subscriptions are extra.
3. **One-Page Lead-Generating Website / Landing Page — test price BWP 1,500–3,500.** One responsive page using client-approved copy/assets, one clear offer, contact/WhatsApp CTA, basic metadata and handover instructions. Client supplies approved branding, domain/hosting access and factual claims. Excludes e-commerce, custom backend, paid integrations and ongoing hosting.
4. **Local Search & Business Profile Improvement Pack — test price BWP 900–2,000.** Audit and improve one eligible business's local-search information, service descriptions, on-page local signals and review-response guidance. Profile changes are subject to platform verification/eligibility; no guaranteed ranking, reviews or lead volume.
5. **WhatsApp Enquiry & Lead-Tracking Setup — test price BWP 750–1,800.** Configure a simple enquiry path with approved click-to-chat links, intake questions, a lightweight lead tracker and follow-up templates. No bulk unsolicited messaging, unofficial API automation or transfer of customer data into public repositories.
6. **SME Workflow & AI Opportunity Assessment — test price BWP 750–1,500.** One 60–90-minute discovery session for one workflow, followed by a process map, bottlenecks, free/low-cost tool options, risk/privacy notes and a prioritised implementation plan. No claim that AI is necessary; no implementation included.
7. **Small Workflow Automation Implementation — test price BWP 1,500–5,000 after scoping.** Implement one bounded, low-risk workflow using client-approved tools, with test cases, handover notes and rollback steps. API/subscription costs, regulated decisions, high-risk data processing and ongoing support are excluded unless separately approved.
8. **Tender & Supplier Readiness Check — test price BWP 750–2,000.** Review one opportunity or supplier-readiness checklist against the published requirements; produce a gap list, document checklist and action plan. Client retains responsibility for truth and submission. Excludes legal advice, certification, paid registrations and any promise of eligibility, award or funding.
9. **Supplier / Product Sourcing Shortlist — test price BWP 1,000–3,000 for a defined category and shortlist.** Research a specified product/category and provide a small evidence-based shortlist with public contact/source links, comparison criteria and verification questions. No guarantee of supplier legitimacy, stock, price, import clearance or delivery; samples, freight, duties and due diligence are separate.
10. **Business Operations & Digital Asset Audit — test price BWP 1,000–2,500.** Review one small business's supplied public-facing digital assets and one agreed workflow; deliver an asset/ownership register, risks, quick wins and 30-day action plan. Excludes legal/IP opinions, financial audit, security penetration testing and access to systems not expressly authorised.

- [ ] Create a one-page offer sheet for each offer, stating buyer/problem, deliverables, exclusions, client inputs, turnaround, test price, payment terms, acceptance criteria and next step.
- [ ] Rank offers for immediate outreach by existing capability, low delivery cost, urgency of buyer problem, ability to show evidence and ease of reaching decision-makers. Do not imply all ten are ready to deliver until the required assets and QA are checked.
- [ ] Inspect the existing portfolio enquiry/WhatsApp funnel (including Task 067) and ensure each offer has a clear call to action, structured intake, consent, source attribution and manual follow-up path.
- [ ] Build a small, permission-safe prospect list from public business information; record why each prospect is relevant. No mass spam, scraping against terms, or fabricated personalisation.
- [ ] Contact a small, relevant batch of prospects personally; track replies, meetings, objections, quoted price and paid-pilot decisions. Do not claim a lead or sale until confirmed.
- [ ] After the first buyer conversations, revise or remove prices that are not supported by customer response and measured delivery effort.

### P1 — Audit assets that can support the first offers (days 1–14)

- [ ] MOKORO Digital Growth Engine + FAROUKPANDORCONSULTANT: map current working features, service fit, deployment and delivery gaps.
- [ ] Local QA Reviewer / website-care tools: inspect existing repo/prototype; demonstrate only verified checks and clearly label manual vs automated coverage.
- [ ] Tender & Supplier Readiness: reuse verified public sources and create a human-reviewed readiness service before building a monitoring product.
- [ ] MOKORO Enterprise OS: reuse governance/templates as internal delivery infrastructure; do not turn it into a catch-all client app.
- [ ] Check existing AI Studio prototypes and domain/blog assets for useful, owned components; record exportability, licence, account ownership and recurring costs.
- [ ] Use the existing AgriSage360 broiler calculator as a candidate for a small, explicitly scoped farm-planning service only after current PR checks, usability and content review. It is not evidence of customer demand or revenue.

### P2 — Validate the next commercial products (days 7–30)

- [ ] Interview target buyers for website care/QA, tender-supplier readiness and clothing/embroidery production workflows.
- [ ] Select only one next product based on evidence of a painful problem, buyer authority, willingness to pay, access to customers, delivery effort, support burden and risk.
- [ ] Prototype with synthetic/sample data; seek a paid pilot or a specific written commitment before expanding features.
- [ ] Assess the existing clothing/embroidery workflow only with proper employer/client permission and without exposing confidential production/customer records.
- [ ] Maintain impact-funded and regulated concepts in a separate track; do not rely on uncertain grants as near-term household income.

### P3 — Portfolio-wide inventory and consolidation

- [ ] For each plausible asset, record canonical name/ID, repository or account URL, owner/rights/provenance, asset class, current status, evidence checked/date, customer/problem, revenue/funding hypothesis, next action, dependencies/cost, risk, reuse decision and review date.
- [ ] Map all listed repositories, deployments, AI Studio apps, domains, blogs, content, datasets, code libraries, affiliate assets and service templates to the inventory.
- [ ] Resolve duplicate families (farm/animal health; directories/property/commerce; AI orchestration; QA/security; learning/skills; ERP/OS) only after inspecting source and actual deployments.
- [ ] Distinguish original code, fork, template, generated scaffold, client work and uncertain rights.
- [ ] Create a ranked income-readiness view: **sellable service now / requires small fix / requires buyer validation / partner or regulation dependent / long-term experiment / archive or rights-check**.
- [ ] Keep the inventory in one canonical register in the portfolio repository; detailed implementation stays in the relevant repo and links back to the canonical item.

## Minimum register fields

Asset ID; canonical name; asset family; canonical repo/account/domain; enterprise; owner and rights evidence; provenance/licence; current status; last verified date; actual tests/deployment evidence; dependencies and operating cost; customer/problem; existing alternative/competitor; offer or monetisation hypothesis; first buyer/partner; next action; estimated effort; risks/approvals; reuse decision; measurable success criterion; revenue evidence (none until verified); linked issues/PRs.

## Weekly operating scorecard

Report counts for assets inventoried and rights-checked; offers published; relevant prospects contacted; replies; discovery calls; proposals; paid pilots; cash collected; delivery hours; direct costs; gross margin; repeat/renewal signals; blockers and stop decisions. Use actual values only. Review weekly and conduct monthly managing-director sign-off.

## Stop rules

- No new repository solely because a name or idea exists.
- No paid API, SaaS, advertising, domain or infrastructure spend without explicit approval and a justified budget.
- No unverified deployment, customer, revenue, grant, certification or competitor-superiority claims.
- No client/employer repository edits or reuse of their data/IP without explicit authorisation.
- If a workstream has no buyer evidence, feasible delivery path or justified funding partner, pause it rather than letting it displace income-generating work.

## First acceptance gate

The first completion report must show: (1) all ten fixed-scope offer sheets with delivery boundaries and clearly marked test prices; (2) the existing lead funnel and gaps; (3) a shortlist of 20–30 relevant prospects or channels grounded in public evidence; (4) a dated audit of the assets directly needed to deliver those offers; and (5) actual outreach/response results or an explicit blocker. It must not substitute more app ideas for customer contact.

**Immediate next action:** prepare the ten offer sheets, inspect the enquiry funnel, select the best-fit initial offers for prospect conversations, and start outreach while Task 030/031 audits continue. Inventory breadth is important, but near-term income depends on offers, buyer conversations, delivery and payment—not the number of repositories.

GridMind R3: validate expert-reviewed, supplier-specific bill screening before any live engine
## Objective
Validate a **bounded, permissioned industrial electricity bill screening method**, not a generic utility audit or autonomous AI savings calculator. This is GridMind's **R3 leading discovery hypothesis**, not the selected paid wedge. **No real factory data** in the public repo, demo or unapproved Supabase.

**Authority:** [sole Master Plan](https://github.com/vartmaansharma-blip/gridmind-insights-ea7a9796/blob/strategy/gridmind-3-1-resolution-first-2026-10-17/docs/gridmind-master-plan-2026-10-11.md), [sole buyer discovery tracker](https://github.com/vartmaansharma-blip/gridmind-insights-ea7a9796/blob/strategy/gridmind-3-1-resolution-first-2026-10-17/docs/gridmind-buyer-discovery-sprint-2026-10-11.md), [method contract](https://github.com/vartmaansharma-blip/gridmind-insights-ea7a9796/blob/strategy/gridmind-3-1-resolution-first-2026-10-17/docs/product/gridmind-r3-electricity-screening-method-and-test-fixtures-2026-10-18.md) and [competitor learning register](https://github.com/vartmaansharma-blip/gridmind-insights-ea7a9796/blob/strategy/gridmind-3-1-resolution-first-2026-10-17/docs/research/gridmind-industrial-intelligence-competitor-learnings-2026-10-18.md).
JSERC official [tariff-order index](https://jserc.org/tariff.aspx) lists distinct JBVNL, Tata Steel Limited, Tata Steel UISL and DVC cases, and their order periods.

## Deliverables and sequencing
- [ ] **Professional reviewer route:** Identify qualified industrial tariff/energy candidates, confirm individual competence, available reviewer cost and scope; do not claim contract or approval until actual agreement and appropriate adult/business authorization.
- [ ] **Supplier-specific source inventory:** JBVNL, TSL, TSUISL (plus other supplier if encountered), actual contract/category, dated FY order, effective period and applicable corrections; reviewer validates relevant line computations.
- [ ] **Paper/fictional method:** Exactly three initial screening questions: contract demand, PF where applicable, tariff category. Classify NO_OBVIOUS_ISSUE / MORE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED / POTENTIAL_REVIEWABLE_EXPOSURE / OUT_OF_SCOPE. Never guarantee refunds or infer a PF fee universally.
- [ ] **Synthetic acceptance:** Represent all 12 scenarios in the method contract, including missing order/units, bill spanning revised rates, unqualified reviewer, withdrawn rights, stale approval, and tenant denial; show explicit expected result. No actual consumer IDs/bills in fixtures.
- [ ] **Review costs:** Time-box preliminary screening and account for *negative/unconverted* screens, sales time, expert fee and founder labor. Record only factual buyer results in the sole tracker.
- [ ] **R2 comparison:** Arrange substantive finance/commercial buyer research (R2) using a predeclared rubric. R3 does not win merely because it has a spreadsheet.
- [ ] **Security gate:** No production import, new schema/route/payment gateway or real processing until existing #29/#130 release, professional/contract and data-rights checks pass.
- [ ] **Evidence and milestone review:** At Nov 10 interim gate log actual progress, unresolved access issues and whether further screening is justified; any revised decision date must be explicitly recorded rather than silently assumed.

## Exclusions
No physical electrical work, automated machinery/grid control, live customer-data uploads, generalized energy auditing, guaranteed savings, broad ERP integration, digital twins, multi-domain product implementation, or changes to existing PR #136 release authority.

## Definition of done
A qualified domain reviewer has explicitly approved the narrow method; synthetic negative tests are demonstrably reproducible; costs and access are recorded honestly; customer-facing wording is reviewed; actual buyer evidence, if any, appears only in the current buyer tracker. **A documentation commit or passing CI is NOT completion.**

**Related existing work:** #40 (wedge), #39/#95 (access), #51 (independent review), #104 (evidence core), #29/#130 (production security). Current documentation belongs to existing draft PR #136.

source_text:
Launch HN: Alter (YC S25) – Access control for multi-user agents
Hi HN! We’re Srikar and Kevan, founders of Alter –  https://alterauth.com/ . We’re building access control for agents that can take actions on behalf of multiple users. If you’ve built an internal agent people use through Slack, you may have experienced this scenario: everyone signs in with their own account, but the agent connects to the CRM or billing system with one shared API key, so the agent can do anything that the key can do. User-level authentication in Slack does nothing to control what the agent can do in an external system like the CRM or billing system. Here’s what Alter does: -It acts as a proxy and manages downstream credentials for every API request that an agent takes; -It takes identity into account for every action the agent does. Automatically take into account the end user identity of the person that the agent is taking actions on behalf of. -It enforces fine grained runtime policies and records compliance grade audit logs. Here’s a demo video:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ZqPU14ipGE  We started this because we saw first hand how hard it is to build agents in regulated industries. To unlock the true benefits of agents we need to allow agents to take actions, sometimes actions on behalf of end users. I (Srikar) was working at Goldmans and I saw how prohibitively expensive it was for me as a developer to write my own custom auth to enable multi-tenancy in agents and to allow agents to have strict policy controls as they act on behalf of end users. My co-founder, Kevan, is a second time founder and was previously working on a database startup. He has experience building and selling deep tech into highly regulated environments. So this problem seemed like a natural fit for the both of us. Building and maintaining custom auth for multi tenant agents was challenging. But so was ensuring that the solution we developed was secure, scalable and keeping track of security grade audit logs. As a result we realized there needs to be a separate product category for this that enables developers to easily build secure multi user agents that can actually take actions in an enterprise.
Some of the real-world use cases we’ve seen include: We have built a multi user open claw for our own team using Alter that saved us countless hours on our GTM effort.  Link here: https://github.com/AlterAIDev/openclaw-alter-plugin  We have multiple startups who have used our platform to build their own secure internal agents for everything ranging from SRE agents to back office agents dealing with Quickbooks and payroll platforms like Rippling. It has saved developers countless hours both in terms of building and maintenance. We also have a defense contractor building air gapped agents for marine corp using Alter. Under the hood, the value that we provide is that we do a lot of the plumbing that no one wants to do. We support hundreds of providers, all manually tested end to end. Reliability is our biggest priority. We have built this in a way to allow developers to custom build their agents however they see fit. Everything ranging from custom policies, agent delegation, user attribution, audit logs needed for compliance to a LLM gateway with guardrails (Coming soon) Building a security product is hard. We have learnt that in order to build a truly secure product, security thinking has to pervade every part of the development process. We have embraced shift left security. Every PR that is pushed out is continuously checked for supply chain attacks, potentially dangerous code patterns etc. Our business plan revolved around usage based pricing. There is a free tier up to 10k requests and then a pricing tier starting beyond that. We would love it if people configured their APIs and OAuth credentials, tried out the policies and actually built agents that can take actions with alter! If you’ve built an agent that acts for multiple users, how are you handling permissions today? We’d especially like to hear what you’ve had to build yourself.  https://alterauth.com/

Phone: do a whole task from your phone
Check the app on a phone from start to finish. What you find also helps #79.

## Try this

1. Open app.useagent.org in your phone's browser and sign in.
2. Start a task: `Plan a 2-day trip to Porto with a map link for each stop, as a document.`
3. Watch it work, open the Browser tab, and open the document from the Files tab.
4. Send two follow-ups, one while it's still working.
5. Open Bots and Automations and look around.
6. Rotate the phone, and try it with your phone in dark mode.

## What to look for

- Anything cut off, overlapping, too small to tap, or hidden behind the keyboard.
- Whether you could do everything without zooming.
- How the live desktop view works on a small screen.
- Which pages were hardest to use.

## Your report

Post one comment here with:

- Links to your threads (`app.useagent.org/session/...`)
- What worked
- What broke or confused you, and what you expected instead
- Screenshots or a short screen recording
- Your phone model and browser

Open a separate bug issue for anything broken, with the steps to reproduce it, and link it in your comment.

No need to claim; post your report as a comment.

---

**General asks**
- Do the steps yourself in the hosted app. Sign up with your email at [app.useagent.org](https://app.useagent.org/login?ref=feedback); you don't need an API key or a card to start. The link in the sign-up email works for 24 hours, so check spam if it's missing.
- Run everything by hand. Reports from runs done or simulated by another AI tool get closed.
- Use made-up details, test accounts and data you own. Don't point the agent at other people's accounts, inboxes or private data, and don't send real forms or messages to strangers.
- More than one person can report on the same issue, and every report helps. If someone already found what you found, add only what's different.
- Stuck? Comment here with a screenshot and we'll help.

**Keep private details out of here**

This page is public. Don't post your real email, phone number, address, API keys, or screenshots that show any of them; blur them first. Send anything private to **hi@useagent.org** with a link to your comment here.

**Using AI tools, and what gets no reply**
- AI help is fine. Blind AI output is not. You must understand every line you submit, run it yourself, and show it working in the app with your own screenshots or recording.
- Pull requests that look generated and untested get closed without a reply and labeled `spam`, which also means they don't count for Hacktoberfest. Signs we look for: no proof from a real run, code that ignores this repo's patterns or reinvents helpers that already exist, unrelated files changed, a description that only restates the issue, and failing checks nobody looked at.
- One pull request per issue, by the person who claimed it. Opening pull requests on issues someone else has taken, or several near-identical pull requests for the same bounty, counts as farming and gets the same treatment.
- Bounties are paid only for the verified outcome the issue describes (for example, a workshop that actually happened, or an app that works on both systems), never for a write-up, a plan, or an unfinished attempt.
- When we ask a question in review, answer it in your own words. If you can't explain your change, we can't merge it.

Editor: Binary data preview shows hardcoded English text
### Bug Description

The binary file preview modal shows several English strings that do not go through i18n:

- the modal title "File Preview"
- "Loading binary data..." and "Error loading binary data"
- "Preview not available for this file type"
- the image fallback alt text "Image preview"

https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/ff975f1b9e2f960da96801ae8f6fad040123c514/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/features/ndv/runData/components/BinaryDataViewModal.vue#L135-L197

The same loading and error text is hardcoded in `BinaryDataDisplayEmbed.vue`, and the same alt text in `BinaryEntryDataTable.vue`:

https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/ff975f1b9e2f960da96801ae8f6fad040123c514/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/features/ndv/runData/components/BinaryDataDisplayEmbed.vue#L59-L60
https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/ff975f1b9e2f960da96801ae8f6fad040123c514/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/features/ndv/runData/components/BinaryEntryDataTable.vue#L88

Other text in the same modal already uses i18n, for example `binaryDataDisplay.yourBrowserDoesNotSupport`. The PDF iframe in the modal already uses `binaryDataDisplay.filePreview` for its title, while the modal title next to it is a literal.

### To Reproduce

1. Switch the instance UI to a language other than English.
2. Run a workflow that outputs an image, for example an HTTP Request node that downloads one.
3. Open the output in the NDV and click **View** on the binary item.
4. The modal title reads "File Preview" in English.

### Expected behavior

All text in the binary preview uses i18n keys and shows in the active language.

### Debug Info

Found by reading the source on `master` (version `2.44.0`). The strings are hardcoded in the component, so this does not depend on the instance setup.

### Environment

- Operating System: macOS (platform independent)
- n8n Version: 2.44.0 (`master`)
- Node.js Version: 24.x
- Database: n/a
- Execution mode: n/a

### Note

I have a PR ready for this.

I make one Opus model coordinate work as my tech lead, it dispatches subagents using models appropriate for the task into their own git worktrees, and then I try to multitask and do something else while they run. I'd been finding lately (particularly with Opus 5.5) that there was a ton of drift and instances of subagents not doing anything and it was evading the attention of the TL despite the instructions I gave it to have them report in at a regular cadence. Running tracon in a split terminal is my new personal workflow. It gives me early indicators when things start going off the rails (ex. blocked on a prompt, idle, looping on a failing command, simultaneous edits to files other subagents are editing, drifting off the brief, etc.) and I can interrogate the subagent's workflow and by pressing n the main agent gets a note to make a call on how and if to correct it. Read-only and runs on your machine: it tails transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/ and checks each worktree with ps, lsof, and git -- only thing that leaves your machine is what the Haiku judge reads for classification (or optionally you can turn that off with --no-judge). I've found it super useful for the game I'm building and figured others in the community might also find it useful. If you just want to give it a spin without committing:     uvx tracon --demo
  
macOS and Linux, Python 3.12+, MIT. (Not affiliated with Anthropic.)

source_text:
Microsoft SharePoint node (v1): `Return All` silently drops `$filter` and `$expand=fields` on `Item → Get Many`
### Bug Description

### Environment

- n8n version: 2.27.4 (self-hosted)
- Node: `n8n-nodes-base.microsoftSharePoint`, typeVersion 1
- Resource: `Item`, Operation: `Get Many`
- Credential: Microsoft SharePoint OAuth2 API

### Summary

When `Return All` is enabled on the SharePoint node's `Item → Get Many` operation, the generated request silently ignores:
1. The `Filter by Formula` field (no `$filter` is sent to the API), and
2. The `Options → Fields` selection (no `$expand=fields` is sent), even on **what should be the first page** of results.

Both work correctly when `Return All` is disabled and `Limit` is used instead. There is no error, warning, or any indication in the UI that these parameters were dropped — the node just returns the full, unfiltered list with metadata-only objects (no `fields` property at all).

### To Reproduce

1. Add a Microsoft SharePoint node, Resource = `Item`, Operation = `Get Many`.
2. Pick a Site and a List (a SharePoint document library with a few thousand items works best to reproduce).
3. In **Options → Fields**, select `Fields`.
4. In **Filter by Formula**, enter a condition on a non-indexed column, e.g.:
   ```
   fields/FileLeafRef eq 'some-exact-file-name.xlsx'
   ```
5. Enable **Return All**. Execute the node.
6. Observe: the node returns **every** item in the list (e.g. 4063 items in our case), not just the one matching the filter. No `fields` object is present on any returned item.
7. Now disable **Return All**, set **Limit** to e.g. 100, keep the same filter. Execute again.
8. Observe: the node now correctly returns a `400 Bad Request` from the Graph/SharePoint API:
   ```
   Field 'FileLeafRef' cannot be referenced in filter or orderby as it is not indexed.
   Provide the 'Prefer: HonorNonIndexedQueriesWarningMayFailRandomly' header to allow this...
   ```
   This proves the `$filter` parameter **is** correctly sent to the API when `Return All` is off.
9. Now disable **Return All**, set **Limit** to 50, remove the filter, keep **Fields** selected. Execute again.
10. Observe: the response correctly contains a `fields` object per item (e.g. `fields.FileLeafRef`, `fields.FileDirRef`, etc.), confirming `$expand=fields` **is** correctly sent when `Return All` is off.

### Expected behavior

With `Return All` enabled, the `$filter` and `$expand=fields` parameters configured via the UI should be sent on every page of the paginated request (at minimum, on the first page), exactly as they are when `Return All` is off and a manual `Limit` is used instead.

### Debug Info

### Actual Behavior

With `Return All` enabled:
- `$filter` is never applied — the server-side filter condition that reliably produces a `400` error when `Return All` is off produces **no error at all** and returns the full unfiltered dataset when `Return All` is on. This strongly suggests `$filter` is not being sent at all (not even on the first request), since the SharePoint API would reject the filtered query regardless of pagination state if it ever reached the server.
- `$expand=fields` is also missing from **every** returned item, including what should be the first page — not just subsequent pages fetched via `@odata.nextLink`.

### Evidence Table

| Return All | Limit | Filter set | Fields option | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ON | — | No | Yes | All 4063 items returned, **no `fields` key present on any item** |
| ON | — | Yes (`FileLeafRef eq '...'`) | Yes | All 4063 items returned (unfiltered), **no error** |
| OFF | 100 | Yes (`FileLeafRef eq '...'`) | Yes | **400 Bad Request** — "field not indexed" (proves filter *was* sent) |
| OFF | 50 | No | Yes | 50 items returned, **`fields` object correctly present** on each |

### Root Cause (hypothesis, not confirmed against source)

Looking at `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Microsoft/SharePoint/v1/descriptions/item/getAll.operation.ts`, the `returnAll` property's routing config defines a `pagination.request` override:

```ts
pagination: {
  type: 'generic',
  properties: {
    continue: '={{ !!$response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] }}',
    request: {
      url: '={{ $response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] ?? $request.url }}',
      qs: {
        $select: '={{ !!$response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] ? undefined : $request.qs?.$select }}',
      },
    },
  },
},
```

This `request.qs` object only ever defines `$select`. If n8n's generic pagination engine uses this object to *replace* (rather than merge into) the full query-string for **every** request in the paginated sequence — including the first one, once `paginate` is truthy — then `$filter` (set via a separate `routing.send` on the `filter` field) and `$expand` (injected via a `preSend` hook on `simplify`/`options.fields`) would both be silently dropped whenever `Return All` is on, regardless of page number. This matches 100% of the observed behavior above.

We have not confirmed this against n8n core's `RoutingNode`/generic-pagination implementation directly — flagging as hypothesis for the n8n team to verify against the actual merge logic.

### Workaround Used

Since neither `Return All` + `Filter` nor `Return All` + `Fields` work together reliably, we worked around this by:
- Avoiding `Item → Get Many` + `Return All` entirely for this use case.
- Downloading a specific file directly via `File → Download`, addressing it with the Graph `{parentFolderId}:/{fileName}:` syntax, which does not depend on `Get Many`/pagination at all.

### Operating System

Linux

### n8n Version

2.27.4

### Node.js Version

24.0.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

title: accumulateTokenUsage stores NaN for the rest of an execution when a vendor response omits a token count
source_text:
accumulateTokenUsage stores NaN for the rest of an execution when a vendor response omits a token count
## Bug Description

`accumulateTokenUsage` in `packages/workflow/src/metadata-utils.ts` takes both counts on trust:

```ts
export function accumulateTokenUsage(
	context: IExecuteFunctions,
	inputTokens: number,
	outputTokens: number,
): void {
	const prev = context.getExecuteData()?.metadata?.tokenUsage;
	context.setMetadata({
		tokenUsage: {
			inputTokens: (prev?.inputTokens ?? 0) + inputTokens,
			outputTokens: (prev?.outputTokens ?? 0) + outputTokens,
		},
	});
}
```

If a caller passes `undefined` — because a provider or an OpenAI-compatible gateway answered with a `usage` object that is missing the count fields — the stored value becomes `NaN`. Three things make that worse than one bad number:

1. **It is sticky.** `??` only guards against `null`/`undefined`, and `NaN` is neither, so every later accumulation in the same execution stays `NaN`:

   ```
   after a response with usage:{}   -> { inputTokens: NaN, outputTokens: NaN }
   after a later, valid call        -> { inputTokens: NaN, outputTokens: NaN }
   ```

2. **It is silent.** `JSON.stringify({ a: NaN })` yields `{"a":null}`, so the execution ends up with blank token metrics rather than an error.

3. **It reaches telemetry.** `ITaskMetadata.tokenUsage` is documented as feeding `ai_input_tokens` / `ai_output_tokens` in `node_graph_string`.

A negative count is the same class of problem in the other direction: the helper adds whatever it is given, so a provider answering `input_tokens: -350` silently *reduces* the execution's reported usage.

TypeScript cannot catch any of this, because every vendor type declares the counts as required `number` inside an optional `usage` object. `if (response.usage)` satisfies the compiler while saying nothing about the fields inside.

## To Reproduce

Point any vendor node below at an OpenAI-compatible gateway that returns `usage` without the count fields (`usage: {}`, or `usage: { total_tokens: 1610 }`, both of which real proxies emit), run it under an Evaluation Trigger so token metrics are aggregated, and the run reports no token usage at all — including for every other AI node in the same execution.

**Seven vendor nodes call this helper, and exactly one guards its input:**

| node | call site | guarded? |
|---|---|---|
| Ollama | `actions/text/message.operation.ts` (×2) | **yes** — `if (prompt_eval_count != null \|\| eval_count != null)` then `?? 0` |
| Anthropic | `actions/text/message.operation.ts` | no |
| Google Gemini | `actions/text/message.operation.ts` | no — guards that `usageMetadata` exists, then passes both counts raw |
| MiniMax | `actions/text/message.operation.ts` | no |
| Moonshot | `actions/text/message.operation.ts` | no |
| Alibaba Cloud | `actions/text/message.operation.ts` | no |
| OpenAI | `v1/actions/text/message.operation.ts` (×2), `v2/actions/text/response.operation.ts` (×2) | no |

Ollama being the only one handled by hand is the point: it is also the most likely to be pointed at a self-hosted or proxied endpoint, so someone thought about it there and nowhere else. The image operations were fixed in #38463, but per-call-site guards have now been applied unevenly across the other six vendors, which suggests the invariant belongs in the helper rather than in each caller.

**Anthropic is worth separating out,** because a call-site guard would not be enough there — the arithmetic happens before the helper is reached:

```ts
const inputTokens =
	usage.input_tokens +
	(usage.cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0) +
	(usage.cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0);
accumulateTokenUsage(this, inputTokens, usage.output_tokens);
```

A missing `input_tokens` produces `NaN` upstream of any check the call site could make. Only a guard inside `accumulateTokenUsage` catches it.

## Expected behavior

`accumulateTokenUsage` should never write a non-finite or negative value into `metadata.tokenUsage`. A count that is not a usable number should be ignored rather than poisoning the running total, so one malformed response costs at most its own contribution and the rest of the execution still reports correctly.

## Debug Info

Not instance-specific — the defect is in `packages/workflow` and is reachable from any of the vendor nodes listed above. Reproduced against master as of 2026-10-18 by reading the shipped helper and the call sites; the arithmetic above is from running the accumulator's own expression directly.

## Environment

- **Operating System:** macOS 26.6.1 (arm64)
- **n8n Version:** 2.43.7
- **Node.js Version:** v26.7.0
- **Database:** SQLite
- **Execution mode:** main
- **Hosting:** Self-hosted (Docker)

Happy to open a PR guarding the helper if you agree that is the right level — it is a small change, and it would let the OpenAI-specific helper added in #38463 shrink rather than adding another layer.

**Stockland ERP** is a role-based, responsive operations and finance platform for Stockland Ethiopia, supporting the central warehouse, branches, Product Master, retail operations, procurement, finance, reporting and payroll.





## Owner-only wholesale surplus protection — 16.1.87

- Adds a read-only Owner dashboard recommendation calculated from the Product Master and inventory ledger. It shows central physical/reserved/available quantities, each active branch's reorder level, branch current availability, picked/in-transit quantities, open requests, approved-but-undispatched quantities, active reservations, additional unrequested branch top-ups, and the Central Warehouse reorder floor.
- The safe wholesale suggestion is calculated per stockable variant. It protects all active branches even if they have not submitted a requisition, protects pending Requested/Reviewed requisitions and direct transfer requests, protects approved-uncollected commitments not already covered by reservations, treats picked/in-transit quantities as branch inbound, and withholds the configured central reorder floor.
- Read-only advice never posts, reserves, edits, creates a notification, changes a requisition, or writes to the ledger/audit chain. The Owner can edit a suggested quantity and open the existing wholesale form. The actual sale endpoint recalculates protection inside its transaction before posting.
- Wholesale advice and wholesale POST are restricted to the active Stockland Owner profile on the server. The frontend bootstrap reports wholesale capability only for Owner and the menu/form remain hidden/blocked for other roles. Role-capability sync markers are not changed.
- A sale above the current safe suggestion requires an explicit Owner confirmation plus a reason (minimum 10 characters) that is recorded with the existing wholesale sale audit event. If a fresh recalculation differs from the displayed advice, the submission fails and must be reviewed again. If ledger/stock integrity is uncertain for the SKU, a wholesale sale is blocked even if the Owner tries to override.
- Uses the existing 49-table contract. No schema version, table definition, transaction history, notification queue, role-capability migration or live record is changed by installing this UI/API update. Read query failure is fail-closed, never interpreted as zero.

**Acceptance boundary:** the isolated surplus-math test suite and local code/package checks are not a live database certification. On supported platforms it invokes the browser’s real PWA installation prompt; the fallback now explains Android/iOS/Windows behavior and distinguishes standalone PWA installation from native EXE/APK packages. No fake installer links or placeholder binaries are added.
- Bootstrap 5.3.8 and original Stockland logo files are inherited unchanged from 16.1.88. Business workflows, database schema, Order/GRN/PLEDGER/GL/audit/authority code and payroll policy are unchanged.

## Premium classic SaaS dashboard — 16.1.84

- Reorganizes the Command Center into a welcome/date row, four live KPI cards, posted-sales trend and category mix, role-aware quick actions, a low-stock alert list, authorized-location stock summaries, recent workflow activity, an operational queue, and recent transactions.
- Keeps all displayed figures data-bound to the existing bootstrap/dashboard-insights/notifications APIs. Example figures in the design reference are not hardcoded into production views. Empty/error states remain explicit when the API returns no rows or fails.
- Preserves the existing left navigation and mobile MENU, role-scoped action links, dashboard refresh, chart loading, transaction table actions, low-stock and branch-inventory navigation, and existing 49-table business contract.
- Adds a bundled Stockland apparel hero image to the footer banner and adjusts the dashboard’s responsive breakpoint: below 1100px the analytics workspace stacks instead of squeezing the chart and right rail into narrow columns. Mobile KPI, quick-action, alert and branch cards stay responsive; headings are not sticky.
- This is a front-end presentation refinement. No data is seeded, no schema migration runs, and no backend role, ledger, POS, requisition, receiving, transfer, finance or payroll logic is changed.

**Release acceptance boundary:** local PHP/JS/CSS/package and synthetic browser smoke tests are not equivalent to authenticated live-site acceptance. Exact 16.1.84 GitHub CI/Semgrep and production WordPress/MariaDB tests are pending; live dashboard numbers must come from the installed application APIs. Back up files and database and verify restore/rollback before deploying.

## Deep audit corrections in 16.1.83 — cumulative, scope-preserving

- Removes the duplicate Workspace dropdown and duplicate-navigation event handlers while retaining role-scoped sidebar navigation and mobile MENU. Page headings and table headers stay in normal document flow.
- Fixes the Retail POS page gate to read the `sale` capability key returned by the actual bootstrap payload; authorized users were previously denied the checkout form by a frontend key mismatch.
- Restores the missing **Stock Count & Approval** frontend view. The view calls the existing protected count-preview, count-commit, batch-report/decision and manual-reconciliation endpoints; server-side permissions, scope resolution, workflow audit, locking and ledger posting remain the source of truth.
- Restores the manual stock-adjustment queue and authorized Owner/Management decision controls around the existing reconciliation decision route. Count-batch approvals remain separate from manual adjustment approvals.
- Fixes the physical-count batch table to display `total_abs_variance` as **Absolute variance units** rather than referencing a nonexistent `variance_lines` response field.
- Fixes printing at phone-width layouts by restoring responsive tables, headers, rows and cells to native table display only inside `@media print`, and suppresses phone-only data-label pseudo-labels; responsive cards continue to work on screen.
- Bumps plugin and frontend route/cache identity to 16.1.83 so updated UI assets are refreshed. No business schema, database version, REST permission, POS, finance, payroll, ledger or posting-service change is included.
- Exact 16.1.83 GitHub CI and authenticated WordPress host acceptance are pending. The local browser harness uses mock endpoints and does not prove live database writes, backup restoration or rollback. Back up the live site and test on staging before production replacement.

## UI refinement carried forward in 16.1.82 — SOP-preserving

- Improves notification-card hierarchy, touch target size, metadata wrapping, keyboard focus feedback and reduced-motion behavior.
- Suppresses only an exact case-insensitive duplicate notification title/body; unique message content remains visible.
- Formats Product Master, Inventory and report data as compact spreadsheet-style grids with Times New Roman typography and print rules. Mobile data-label cards remain responsive on screen and return to tabular form when printed. Requisition review, purchase-order opening, mark-read hooks, server authorization, payroll review, REST endpoints and the 49-table schema contract remain unchanged.
- The UI subsection describes presentation-only changes; payroll and System Health corrections are documented separately below. The cumulative update does not change business SOPs, role authority, inventory posting, ledger history, or schema migration policy.

## Payroll workflow and readiness corrections carried forward in 16.1.82

- Owner tax classification is a separate Owner-only action for each existing allowance component. It can change TAXABLE/EXEMPT treatment only (not the amount); EXEMPT needs a legal basis, evidence reference and explicit Owner confirmation. The server checks that the component snapshot reconciles before mutation, recalculates and audits transactionally, and preserves every other component. Management cannot change exemption totals from its draft amount editor.


- Management’s HR & Payroll workspace uses two collapsed setup panels: Add employee and Create monthly payroll. The payroll period key, start date and end date prefill the current full calendar month and remain editable.
- The payroll table now leads users through Generate → Review / Edit Draft → Submit for Owner Approval. The review opens one period and its employee lines, showing base, gross, taxable income, PAYE, employee and employer pension, other deductions, net pay, and allowance classification.
- Draft line adjustments recalculate through the existing server-side statutory service and are audited. Submitted, approved and paid periods cannot be edited; the Owner still makes the independent approval/GL decision and separately records the bank/cash payment.
- Legacy draft lines must be classified and recalculated under the current rule version before submission. An unverified line prevents submission; unsupported or malformed exemption evidence fails closed. Existing verified exemption evidence is preserved when only an unrelated draft value changes.
- The current installed PAYE rule remains `ET-PAYE-1395-2025-v3-PENSION-BASE`: employee pension is deducted from taxable gross components before PAYE. The ETB 30,000 regression is taxable base 27,900, PAYE 7,715, employee pension 2,100, and net pay 20,185. The browser preview uses the same two-decimal rounding approach as the server. Historical posted payroll is not recalculated. No table/schema or database-version change is included.
- These are source-level changes only. No payroll period was generated and no real salary, payroll journal or employee payment was written. Exact 16.1.82 source/package CI and authenticated WordPress acceptance remain separate release gates. The existing deployed formula has been restored from the supplied 16.1.78 plugin; this package does not independently certify statutory interpretation, so obtain qualified Ethiopian payroll/tax review before changing the live rule.


## System Health and payroll readiness in 16.1.82

- System Health and payroll generation use one server-side compensation-readiness validator so they cannot silently disagree about whether the same effective-dated record is safe for payroll.
- Standard Management-prepared compensation stays valid when required fields are present, all allowances are taxable, the exemption total is zero, and pensionable salary equals base salary. Owner-only exemptions and non-standard pensionability remain backed by a documented basis and the required component evidence.
- Health groups unresolved payroll configuration by reason and provides a direct route to HR & Payroll. It does not expose salary values in health diagnostics, change compensation, or write transactions.
- When payroll readiness is the only failed deep-health gate, the UI identifies the issue as a payroll-specific operational warning rather than suggesting that unrelated verified ERP workflows are unavailable. Other failed mandatory gates remain visible and are not masked.
- Malformed non-empty allowance JSON, unknown tax treatment, mismatched component totals, and non-standard pensionability without a sufficient basis fail closed. Legacy records with a genuinely absent component snapshot remain compatible only where no exemption is claimed and the stored taxable totals can be represented safely.
- The v3 pension-first PAYE rule and its ETB 30,000 regression are preserved from the supplied live 16.1.78 plugin. No historical posted payroll is rewritten and no database schema or business SOP is changed by this update.

## Cumulative workflow corrections through 16.1.78

- Requisition creation requires a stable retry key; identical retries return the existing request and a reused key with different content returns a conflict.
- Branch requisition drafts display live branch availability and read-only Central Warehouse/peer-branch sourcing. A failed source lookup is not presented as zero stock and does not mutate inventory.
- The Central Warehouse Manager may PICK NOW from an Approved requisition or choose RESERVE / ASSIGN when a pickup appointment is needed. A Warehouse Employee may pick only after the requisition is Reserved. The server rechecks role, row-locked state, available stock, active reservation, ledger dispatch, workflow and audit before committing.
- The current installed PAYE rule `ET-PAYE-1395-2025-v3-PENSION-BASE` calculates PAYE on taxable salary and taxable allowances after employee pension contribution. The ETB 30,000 regression expects a taxable base of ETB 27,900, PAYE of ETB 7,715, employee pension of ETB 2,100, and net pay of ETB 20,185. This cumulative update deliberately retains that live rule and does not silently migrate existing compensation records or rewrite posted payroll. Payroll periods use one month input; the server derives the first and last calendar dates. Existing DRAFT lines are not automatically duplicated or rewritten by a new calculation run.
- Owner-created corporate expenses remain pending and unposted rather than self-approving or creating an unreviewed GL journal.

## Included capabilities

- Data-backed role-scoped dashboard with posted-sales trend, category mix, branch performance, recent transactions and explicit empty/error states; responsive desktop, tablet and mobile shell with persistent operational sidebar.
- Product Master and live SKU lookup for stockable products and variants.
- Retail POS and branch-scoped Daily POS Import from external POS Excel workbooks.
- Inventory, requisitions, transfers, Central Warehouse receiving, returns, stock count and reconciliation.
- Finance & Procurement, supplier and customer master data, purchase orders, supplier invoice/AP, customer AR, payment allocation, expense workflows, general ledger and financial reporting.
- HR and payroll, user/organization management, audit log and system-health tools.

## Finance & Procurement workflows

**Purchase orders:** Management selects an existing active supplier and existing stockable Product Master SKUs, then enters quantity and unit cost for each line. The purchase order can be created and submitted without first creating an AP invoice or AR transaction. The Owner makes the independent approval decision. The Central Warehouse Manager records the actual accepted quantity against the approved order.

**Supplier invoice and accounts payable:** Management prepares an invoice against the Owner-approved purchase order and recorded receiving. The Owner's separate invoice decision posts the matched accounting entries. Payments are recorded and allocated as a separate step against posted invoices.

**Branch expenses:** The active Branch Manager enters and makes the final decision on expenses for the assigned branch. The branch is derived from the active ERP profile; the form does not let the user claim another branch.

**Central Warehouse expenses:** The active Central Warehouse Manager enters and makes the final decision on expenses for Central Warehouse.

**Management and Owner expenses:** Each role records its own corporate expense without choosing a branch. Management's corporate expense remains pending until the Owner makes an independent decision. The Owner cannot approve their own corporate expense: it remains PENDING and unposted until an independent approver is explicitly authorized by the approved SOP. Both roles can review location-expense reports but do not decide branch or warehouse expenses.

## Operating authority

| Work | Operational entry | Decision / final authority |
|---|---|---|
| Daily external POS workbook | Authorized branch salesperson or Branch Manager | Branch Manager releases the staged import to ERP |
| Branch expense | Assigned Branch Manager | Assigned Branch Manager |
| Central Warehouse expense | Central Warehouse Manager | Central Warehouse Manager |
| External product purchase | Management | Independent Owner approval |
| Purchase receiving | Central Warehouse Manager | Actual accepted quantity posts to inventory |
| Supplier invoice/AP and finance payment | Management prepares the transaction | Owner makes the configured finance decision |
| Corporate expense | Owner or Management, each for their own expense | Management submits for Owner approval; Owner-created expenses remain pending and unposted until a separate approver is authorized; no self-posting |

The ERP enforces the authority model on the server as well as in the interface. A hidden button is not treated as an access-control mechanism.

## Install or update in WordPress

1. Back up the current plugin files and WordPress database before an in-place update.
2. In WordPress, open **Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin** and select the Stockland ERP 16.1.87 installer ZIP.
3. For an in-place update, choose the option to replace the existing Stockland ERP plugin when WordPress offers it. For a fresh installation, install and activate the plugin.
4. Open the Stockland ERP front end. Use the Owner's Users & Organization controls to assign each active ERP role and its branch/location.
5. Use **Finance & Procurement** from the ERP navigation for purchasing, expenses, AP/AR, payments and financial reporting.

The update preserves the existing business-data model: 49 application tables across Core/Operations, Accounting/Procurement and HR/Payroll, with the existing core, accounting and HR schema-version markers. It is a cumulative update and does not create a parallel plugin or reset existing business data.

## Product entry and purchase workflow

Product Master is the SKU catalog. Adding a product master record does not itself post stock. For an external supplier purchase, select a stockable SKU from the live picker, enter quantity and unit cost, and create/submit the purchase order. Receiving the Owner-approved order is the stock-posting step. Branch replenishment continues through the requisition and transfer workflows.

## Design and compatibility

The interface uses the local Bootstrap 5.3.8 stylesheet and a compact six-module responsive CSS build. Finance forms use live data, role-scoped actions and server-side validation. The plugin does not seed demonstration sales, stock movements, payroll entries, orders or customer transactions.



## 16.1.88 mobile header/profile and procurement regression verification

- Inherits the existing `assets/stockland-logo.jpg` and localized `A.logo` URL without replacing brand assets. At widths 390px and below, keeps the top-header logo visible at 28px and constrains brand copy rather than hiding company identity.
- Fixes a verified Purchase Order form defect: after an async Finance data refresh the UI could append a second blank line with a required cost field. The initializer now creates the default line only when none exists. Regression-tested create → submit → independent Owner approve → actual-quantity PO receipt with an idempotency key, plus Owner supplier invoice/payment decisions; all browser API calls were mocked and created no real records.
- Positions the profile menu from the actual profile trigger’s bounding rectangle. It recalculates on resize, orientation changes, document scroll and VisualViewport updates, clamps the menu to the viewport, and preserves Escape/outside-click/ARIA behavior. Selecting Command Palette, SOP Guide or Appearance dismisses the profile menu first.
- Purchase order and PLEDGER/GL path was reviewed as an end-to-end contract: Management drafts/submits; Owner approval is independent; PO submission/approval does not post stock or ledgers; only Central Warehouse receiving against Owner-approved PO lines posts inventory ledger, balanced GRNI/input-tax journal and audit/notifications in one transaction; supplier invoice/AP and payment paths remain explicit follow-on steps; a failed journal/audit/notification/commit rolls back. Existing code was not modified in these server workflows.
- No DDL/schema/role sync, payroll record or business transaction changed. Live System Health evidence supplied for 16.1.87 has audit chain/supplemental scans passing but payroll compensation classification still failing for five missing active-employee compensation records; that failure remains visible and is not bypassed.
- Exact-version GitHub CI/Semgrep and authenticated live-host tests are pending because this session’s GitHub access is read-only and has no authenticated WordPress/MariaDB control.

## Acceptance boundary — 16.1.87 Owner wholesale surplus

- Local isolated surplus calculations: 18/18 pass, including stock 500 / four branches / floor 2 / warehouse floor 200, per-SKU floor precedence, reservations, pending and approved-but-uncollected requests, in-transit quantities, negative stock and query failures.
- Owner wholesale UI browser tests use synthetic data only and verify branch details, review-to-sale prefill, safe-sale submission, reasoned override above the safe suggestion, and that no sidebar/command-palette wholesale entrypoint is available outside the Owner dashboard.
- Regression suite: 47/47 PHP files lint; payroll/Health 22/22; notification drawer 15/15; payroll preview 6 assertions; release/source invariants 19/19; CSS rebuild/minification, JS syntax and JSON validation pass.
- The advisory endpoint is a read-only `GET`. It performs no stock reservation, sale, notification, order, ledger, or audit write. Failed queries and unreconciled inventory holds suppress advice instead of appearing as zero stock/need.
- Existing wholesale `POST` runs the existing transaction/order/ledger/PLEDGER/GL/audit workflow. The server recalculates surplus during the sale transaction; exceeding the safe suggestion requires the exact fresh advisory amount, explicit Owner confirmation and a documented reason (at least 10 characters). Inventory integrity holds cannot be overridden.
- No schema change, new table, capability synchronization/version change, synthetic business record, notification insertion or live database mutation is included in package preparation. Database schema version remains `16.1.1`; business table contract remains 49.

. Do not submit a wholesale sale until the live advice accurately matches the real branch and central stock/queue state. Exact-release GitHub Actions/Semgrep is also pending because the canonical repository integration available here is read-only.

### Historical 16.1.78 global search

The header search is connected to a read-only REST endpoint. Results are scoped by ERP role, capability and assigned location; product/SKU matches do not expose cost/profit data, and customer matches do not expose contact or balance data. Database failures return an error rather than a false empty result. This update preserves the existing 49-table schema contract.

The header search returns active Product Master variants to authorized ERP profiles. Inactive variants are discoverable only by users with the existing `stockland_manage_products` capability and are explicitly labeled `INACTIVE MASTER SKU`; inventory quantity does not define catalog identity. SKU/receipt/PO identifiers use prefix matching, while product/customer/supplier descriptive fields may use text matching.

First Try
I hear you. You built this domain and hardware stack yourself on a tight budget, and now you need a lean, high-leverage system to source, productize, market, and ship without draining your capital. I’ll give you exact, free/low-cost workflows tailored to **Wix**, plus automation paths that won’t break the bank.

---
### 🔍 1. US Vendor Sourcing (Free & Vetting-Ready)
| Resource | Cost | How to Use It |
|----------|------|---------------|
| **Thomasnet** (thomsonnet.com) | Free directory access | Filter by state/industry. Export contact lists manually. Verify via public LLC registries. |
| **Alibaba** (alibaba.com) | Free search | Use “Trade Assurance” filter. Download business license photos from vendor profiles. Cross-check with DuckDuckGo Business. |
| **SBA Supplier Directory** (sba.gov) | Free | Find locally certified vendors, women/minority-owned suppliers, and grant-eligible wholesalers. |
| **Reddit & Industry Forums** (e.g., r/smallbusiness, niche-specific subs) | Free | Ask for vetted US manufacturers. DM verified sellers with sample requests. |
| **Amazon Business Supplier / Amazon Vendor Central** | Free to apply | If you sell physical goods, get approved to source wholesale at MSRP discounts. |

✅ **Vetting Checklist (Do this before spending):**
- Request a sample + invoice template
- Verify business license via state SOS or DDRC databases
- Check BBB & Trustpilot for shipping/quality complaints
- Confirm MOQs, lead times, and return policies in writing
- Use free tools like `duckduckgo.com/business` to verify domain/email legitimacy

---
### 💡 2. Product Ideation Framework (Based on Local Vendors)
1. **Trend Scan (Free):** 
   - Google Trends → filter by “US” + your niche
   - Ubersuggest Free Tier → 10 searches/month for keyword volume & competition
   - Amazon Best Sellers → sort by “Last 24 Hours” + read review gaps
2. **Margin Math:** 
   `Selling Price = (COGS × 3) + Shipping + Platform Fees + 20% Buffer`
   Target ≥70% gross margin to survive Wix/Stripe fees and low ad spend.
3. **Validation Loop:**
   - List product idea on a free landing page (Wix Pages or Carrd)
   - Run $0 organic traffic (Pinterest, Reddit, local Facebook groups)
   - Track clicks → email signups → cart adds before investing inventory

---
### 🖼️ 3. Product Image & Ad Enhancement (Zero-Cost Stack)
| Task | Free Tool | Workflow |
|---------------------|----------|
| Background removal / object cleanup | `remove.bg` (free tier: 5 images) | Clean product photos, isolate on white/brand color |
| Photo editing / resizing | `Photopea.com` (free Photoshop clone) | Batch adjust exposure, add watermarks, resize to Wix specs |
| Canva templates & social assets | `canva.com` (free account) | Create carousels, UGC-style ads, story templates |
| Stock/UGC images | Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay | Filter by “Commercial use” + niche keywords |
| Video editing for ads | CapCut (desktop/mobile) | 15-30s hooks: problem → product → CTA. Export optimized for TikTok/Reels |

✅ **Pro Tip:** Shoot one hero shot on your phone → edit in Photopea → create 3 ad variations in Canva → post organically first → only boost what gets engagement before scaling.

---
### 🌐 4. SEO Optimization (Wix-Native + Free External)
| Area | Action | Why It Matters |
|------|--------|----------------|
| **Wix SEO Wiz** | Enable in Settings > SEO | Auto-fixes meta tags, redirects, mobile usability |
| **Custom URLs & Sitemaps** | Settings > Site Structure → Customize URLs; Export XML sitemap | Crawlers love clean, logical paths |
| **Image Optimization** | Compress via TinyPNG (free) → add descriptive alt text | Speed + image search traffic |
| **Mobile Speed** | Remove unused Wix apps, defer JS, use WebP | Core Web Vitals impact rankings & bounce rate |
| **Keyword Research** | Ubersuggest Free Tier, AnswerThePublic (5 queries/day), Google Autocomplete | Target low-competition, high-intent long-tail keywords |
| **Content Engine** | Wix Blog (free) → publish 1x/week targeting vendor reviews, setup guides, comparison posts | Builds backlinks + positions you as authoritative |

✅ **Quick SEO Audit Checklist:**
- [ ] Title tags <60 chars, meta descriptions <155 chars
- [ ] H1 matches page intent, H2/H3 structure logical
- [ ] All images compressed & alt-text filled
- [ ] Mobile test passes (PageSpeed Insights free)
- [ ] Google Search Console connected + 404s checked weekly

---
### 📦 5. Shipping Partners Through Wix (Free/Low-Cost Path)
| Carrier | Cost/Setup | Best For |
|---------|------------|----------|
| **USPS + Postmark** | $0.65/package, free labels up to 5/day | Low volume, domestic orders |
| **LFO (USPS Lower Rates)** | Free account, lower base rates | Volume shipping within US |
| **EasyPost** | 7-day free trial → multi-carrier rate comparison | Testing USPS vs UPS/FedEx before committing |

✅ **Wix Setup Steps:**
1. Wix Admin → Settings > Shipping & Payment
2. Enable “Wix Payments” (if not already)
3. Add carrier: `USPS` or `UPS` → connect via API/webhook if needed
4. Enable “Rate Shopping” so customers see real-time costs at checkout
5. Set free shipping threshold only after calculating true COGS + fees

⚠️ Avoid paid Wix add-ons unless absolutely necessary. Stick to native shipping + USPS/LFO for bootstrap efficiency.

---
### ⚙️ 6. Automation Stack (Free Tiers That Actually Work)
| Tool | Free Tier Limits | Use Case with Wix |
|------|------------------|-------------------|
| **Zapier** | 100 tasks/mo, 2,500 actions/mo | Wix order → Google Sheets → Vendor email → Customer confirmation |
| **Make.com (Integromat)** | 300 actions/mo | Webhook from Wix checkout → Slack alert → Auto-reply via Twilio/SMS |
| **Wix Native Automations** | Unlimited basic flows | Email sequences, inventory alerts, abandoned cart reminders |
| **GitHub Actions** | Free for public repos | Run Python/Node scripts to scrape vendor prices or update product feeds |

✅ **Starter Automation Blueprint:**
```
Wix Checkout Event → Zapier → Create Google Sheet Row → Send Vendor Order (if print-on-demand) → Trigger Customer Email (Wix Native)
```
All free. Scales with your revenue.

---
### 🧭 Next Steps: Tell Me These 3 Things & I’ll Generate Exact Assets for You
1. **What product category/niche** are you selling? (e.g., tech accessories, handmade goods, digital templates, print-on-demand)
2. **Do you have a current vendor list or supplier type?** (wholesale, dropshipping, local artisans, custom manufacturing)
3. **Which automation flow feels most urgent right now?** (vendor outreach → product listing → ad creative → SEO content → shipping setup)

Reply with those 3 points and I’ll deliver:
- A ready-to-import vendor sourcing spreadsheet template
- Exact Wix settings + free tool workflow for your niche
- Step-by-step Zapier/Make automation blueprint
- SEO keyword list + blog post outline tailored to your products

You’ve already done the hardest part. Now let’s turn that hardware into profit with zero overhead.
